# SDAIA Academy Course Catalog

> The SDAIA Academy course catalog: courses in data and artificial intelligence in five tracks, with a page for every course.

# USE-FLU-101 · Data and AI Literacy Baseline for Everyone at Work

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Everyone](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-FLU.md)
- Level: Level 100 · Explain
- Format: Primer: self-paced on web or phone in seven short modules, in Arabic and English, with a scenario test
- Total hours: 3 h
- Audience: beginner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-101/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-101/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-101/practice.html

## Description

A self-paced primer, usable on a phone, built one-to-one on the 40 items of an all-professionals data and AI literacy baseline. Participants work through short workplace scenarios: they decide whether a task involves data or AI and where their own role stops, pick an approved tool, strip personal and confidential details from a prompt, read a dashboard before trusting it, check an AI draft against a source, write a disclosure line and choose whom to escalate to. A scenario test closes the course, and its result can serve as an organisation's training record.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish everyday use of a data or AI tool from specialist design, validation and governance work that belongs to a responsible team.
- Classify the personal, confidential or proprietary content in files, messages and prompts, and rewrite them with safer wording before using an approved tool.
- Prepare a request to an approved assistant that states the intended output, context, audience, constraints and review needs.
- Identify the title, source, date, unit, legend, filter and scope of a chart, dashboard or AI output, and the red flags that make it unsafe to rely on.
- Apply a source, sensitivity, accuracy, authorisation and impact check to decide whether to use, revise, pause or escalate an AI output.
- Explain why responsibility stays with the person who submits or acts on AI-assisted work, and when policy requires disclosure.
- Identify the right contact, such as data owner, AI owner, steward, compliance contact or supervisor, for a data or AI issue beyond personal authority.

## Prerequisites

- None; written for any professional in any field

## Next courses

- [USE-FLU-201 · Working with AI Assistants: Delegate, Describe, Judge, Own](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-201.md)
- [USE-FLU-202 · AI Productivity for Knowledge Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-202.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: ما البيانات وما الذكاء الاصطناعي، وأين ينتهي دورك

- استخدام يومي أم عمل متخصص؟

### Day 2: الأدوات المعتمدة وحماية المعلومات

- احمِ المعلومة قبل أن تشاركها

### Day 3: طلب المساعدة والتعامل مع النتيجة بوصفها مسودة

- اطلب بوضوح، وراجع قبل أن تعتمد

### Day 4: قراءة الرسوم البيانية والجداول ولوحات المعلومات والمخرجات

- اقرأ قبل أن تثق

### Day 5: التحقق والتوقف

- تحقق، ثم قرّر

### Day 6: الإفصاح والمساءلة

- عملك باسمك، ولو ساعدك المساعد

### Day 7: التصعيد والمراجعة البشرية

- لمن تصعّد، ومتى

## Topics

### What data and AI are, and where your role stops

- Data as records that can be incomplete, duplicated or outdated
- AI output as patterns from data and instructions
- Using a tool versus designing, validating or governing it
- Common terms for asking clear questions

### Approved tools and protecting information

- Approved tools, accounts and channels
- Personal, confidential, sensitive and proprietary content
- What providers may store, log or review
- Safer wording and minimal disclosure
- Reading tool warnings, permissions and limits
- No workarounds: personal accounts and unapproved tools

### Asking for help and treating the result as a draft

- Stating output, context, audience, constraints and review needs
- Draft support, not a final answer
- Domain judgement before acting on a suggestion

### Reading charts, tables, dashboards and outputs

- Title, source, date, unit, legend, filter and scope
- Filtering and sorting without changing the underlying data
- Red flags: missing labels, inconsistent totals, unclear definitions
- Facts, opinions, predictions, assumptions and AI content
- Decision support is not a decision

### Verifying and stopping

- Comparing with an official source or original record
- Bias and missing perspectives
- The five-point check: source, sensitivity, accuracy, authorisation, impact
- When to pause or stop use

### Disclosure and accountability

- Responsibility stays with the person who acts
- When policy requires disclosure
- AI-assisted conclusion versus established fact
- Consequences of data and AI choices for people and trust

### Escalation and human review

- Who owns what: data owner, AI owner, steward, compliance contact, supervisor
- Cases affecting rights, safety, compliance or significant resources
- Requests beyond personal authority

# USE-FLU-102 · Reading Data, Charts and Claims at Work

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Everyone](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-FLU.md)
- Level: Level 100 · Explain
- Format: Primer: one facilitated day of six sessions or six self-paced modules, with a scenario test
- Total hours: 6 h
- Audience: beginner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-102/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-102/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-102/practice.html

## Description

Participants practise reading the numbers that reach them every day: tables, charts, dashboards, forecasts and the AI summaries written about them. They check source, date, unit, definition and filter; recompute a headline average in a spreadsheet; separate percentage change from percentage points; work out what a correlation can and cannot show; read forecast ranges; and redraw misleading charts honestly. Data come from public open-data portals and synthetic reports. The primer ends with a scenario test and an AI-written summary of a dashboard in which the participant must find the planted errors.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Identify the source, owner, date, unit, definition and filter scope of a chart, table or dashboard before using its numbers.
- Compute mean, median, percentage change and percentage-point change to check a stated headline figure.
- Distinguish correlation from causation and name the likely confounder or selection effect behind a stated link.
- Analyse a display for misleading design such as a truncated axis, dual axes, a selective time window or a missing denominator, and redraw it honestly.
- Classify the statements in a report or AI summary as fact, opinion, prediction, assumption or AI-generated content, and test each factual statement against the underlying table.
- Explain what a forecast range, margin of error or sample size says about how far a number can be trusted.

## Prerequisites

- Opens a spreadsheet, sorts a table and writes a simple formula

## Format and days

### Day 1: قبل أن تقرأ الرقم

- قبل أن تقرأ الرقم

### Day 2: الملخصات والمتوسطات

- الملخصات والمتوسطات

### Day 3: العلاقات والأسباب

- العلاقات والأسباب

### Day 4: التنبؤات وعدم اليقين

- التنبؤات وعدم اليقين

### Day 5: العروض الأمينة والمضللة

- العروض الأمينة والمضللة

### Day 6: الادعاءات وملخصات الذكاء الاصطناعي

- الادعاءات وملخصات الذكاء الاصطناعي

## Topics

### Before you read the number

- Source, owner, date and refresh
- Units, definitions and denominators
- Filters and scope in dashboards
- Using filters without changing the data

### Summaries and averages

- Mean versus median on skewed data
- Percentage change versus percentage points
- Absolute versus relative change in risk
- Rates per population
- Totals that do not add up

### Relationships and causes

- Correlation and causation
- Confounders and selection effects
- Small samples and chance
- Survivorship
- A pattern that reverses when groups are combined

### Forecasts and uncertainty

- Ranges, margins of error and scenarios
- What a trend line assumes
- Forecasts as decision support, not fact

### Honest and misleading displays

- Truncated and dual axes
- Selective time windows
- Area, three-dimensional and cumulative distortions
- Missing baselines and comparisons

### Claims about data, including AI summaries

- Claim, evidence, assumptions, limitations
- Fact, opinion, prediction, assumption and AI content
- Checking an AI summary against the table

# USE-FLU-103 · How AI Systems Learn and Where They Fail

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Everyone](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-FLU.md)
- Level: Level 100 · Explain
- Format: Primer: one facilitated day of six sessions or six self-paced modules, with a scenario test
- Total hours: 6 h
- Audience: beginner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-103/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-103/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-103/practice.html

## Description

A non-technical primer on how learned systems are made and why they fail. Participants trace the path from data to model to decision for a workplace tool, train a small classifier without code and watch it break on shifted data, work out why a high detection rate and a high accuracy figure both mislead when the event is rare, look for leakage and bias in dataset descriptions, and collect fluent but wrong answers from a language model. The course ends with a written critique of a vendor's accuracy claim that names the evidence still missing.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Describe the path from data to model to decision for a workplace AI system and mark where people make choices.
- Explain why a fluent language model answer can be wrong, including next-word prediction, missing or outdated knowledge and the tendency to agree with the user.
- Compute the false alarms, misses and share of real flags that stated detection rates imply when the event is rare, and show why overall accuracy misleads.
- Describe how overfitting and data shift lower a model's performance on new data.
- Analyse a dataset description for leakage, unrepresentative coverage and unreliable labels, and state who could be harmed by each problem.
- Draft a critique of a vendor accuracy claim that asks for the missing evidence: test data, base rate, error types, subgroup results and conditions of use.
- Distinguish a model from the system around it, including rules, retrieval, tools and human review, and identify where a human must stay in the loop.

## Prerequisites

- Basic arithmetic with percentages; no programming or statistics

## Next courses

- [USE-SEC-201 · AI in Health Systems](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-SEC-201.md)
- [USE-SEC-202 · AI in Energy and Petrochemicals](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-SEC-202.md)
- [USE-SEC-203 · AI in Government Services](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-SEC-203.md)
- [USE-SEC-204 · AI in Education Systems](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-SEC-204.md)
- [USE-SEC-205 · AI in Mobility and Logistics](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-SEC-205.md)
- [USE-SEC-206 · AI in Financial Services](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-SEC-206.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: من البيانات إلى القرار

- الطريق من البيانات إلى القرار

### Day 2: التعلم والتعميم

- نموذج نجح في اختباره ثم أخفق

### Day 3: الأخطاء والمعدلات الأساسية والعتبات

- ما لا يقوله معدل الكشف

### Day 4: التسرب والتحيز

- حين تختبئ الإجابة في البيانات

### Day 5: النماذج اللغوية: السلاسة لا تعني الصحة

- السلاسة لا تعني الصحة

### Day 6: مساءلة الادعاء

- الأدلة التي يدين لك بها الادعاء

## Topics

### From data to decision

- Task types: classify, forecast, recommend, generate
- Features, labels and examples
- Model versus system: rules, retrieval, tools, human review
- Who chooses what in the pipeline

### Learning and generalising

- Training and testing
- Overfitting
- Data shift and stale models
- Why more data is not always better data

### Errors, base rates and thresholds

- False positives and false negatives
- Base rates and rare events
- Why accuracy alone misleads
- Thresholds as policy choices

### Leakage and bias

- Leakage: when the answer hides in the data
- Representation, label and proxy bias
- Historical patterns repeated
- Results by subgroup

### Language models: fluent is not correct

- Next-word prediction
- Knowledge cut-off and missing local knowledge
- Invented sources and figures
- Agreeing with the user

### Questioning a claim

- What was tested, on whom, under which conditions
- Error types and who bears their cost
- Further evidence to ask for
- Automation bias: people deferring to the system
- Human oversight and the right to challenge

# USE-FLU-104 · Safe Use of AI at Work: Data, Privacy and Deception

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Everyone](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-FLU.md)
- Level: Level 100 · Explain
- Format: Primer: one facilitated half-day or four self-paced modules, with a scenario test
- Total hours: 4 h
- Audience: beginner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-104/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-104/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-104/practice.html

## Description

Participants practise the safe-use decisions that most often go wrong at work. They classify ten work items and decide which tool tier may receive each, compare provider terms on storage and training use, minimise a request that contains personal data, find hidden instructions planted in an email, a web page and a shared file that an assistant will read, and run a call-back check on a simulated deepfake voice and video request for a payment. They finish with an incident report for a case in which confidential data reached an unapproved tool.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Classify workplace material against a data classification scheme and decide which tool tier, if any, may receive it.
- Explain how prompts, uploaded files and outputs may be stored, reviewed or used for training under provider and organisational terms.
- Prepare a minimised version of a request that keeps the task intact while removing or pseudonymising personal data.
- Identify signs of prompt injection in content that an assistant or agent reads, and describe the safe response.
- Apply an out-of-band verification routine to a suspected deepfake request involving money, credentials or data.
- Describe the response to a data or AI incident: stop, record, report to the right contact and prevent a repeat.

## Prerequisites

- None; USE-FLU-101 is recommended first

## Format and days

### Day 1: صنّف قبل أن تشارك

- أي أداة يجوز أن تستقبل هذه المادة؟

### Day 2: مصير ما تكتبه، وكيف تقلّله

- ماذا يحدث لما تكتبه؟
- قلّل ورمّز: أبقِ المهمة وأخرج الشخص

### Day 3: تعليمات مخفية في ما يقرؤه المساعد

- المحتوى الذي يأمر مساعدك

### Day 4: الخداع والإفصاح والحوادث

- التزييف العميق والطلب العاجل
- الإفصاح، وما تفعله بعد الخطأ

## Topics

### Classify before you share

- Four-level data classification schemes
- Personal and sensitive personal data
- Tool tiers: public consumer, approved enterprise, local or on-premises
- Matching data to tool tier

### What happens to what you type

- Storage, logs and retention
- Use of inputs for model training
- Who can see shared chats and files
- Settings that change what is kept
- Where data are processed and rules on transfer abroad
- Meeting note-takers, browser extensions and plug-ins that read mail, files or screens

### Minimise and pseudonymise

- Remove, generalise or replace identifiers
- Keep the task, drop the person
- When not to use AI at all

### Prompt injection for users

- Hidden instructions in emails, pages, files and images
- Why assistants and agents follow them
- Safe responses: stop, do not follow, report
- Permissions that limit the damage

### Deepfakes and AI-enabled fraud

- Voice clones and video impersonation
- Urgent requests for money, credentials or data
- Out-of-band verification and agreed code words
- Synthetic documents and screenshots

### Disclosure and incidents

- Disclosing AI assistance and labelling synthetic media
- Provenance labels and watermarks, and why a missing label proves nothing
- What to do after a mistake
- Reporting routes

# USE-FLU-201 · Working with AI Assistants: Delegate, Describe, Judge, Own

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Everyone](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-FLU.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: one day of six sessions, each with concepts and a lab, plus guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 8 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-201/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-201/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-201/practice.html

## Description

A one-day workshop on the habits that separate useful AI help from polished mistakes. Participants break a realistic task into steps and decide which to delegate; try the assistant on a new task type against a known answer before relying on it; describe goals, context, audience and success criteria; iterate over several turns; and test finished-looking outputs for invented facts, missing context and flattering agreement. They practise deciding when not to use AI, write a disclosure note, and in a tracked follow-up apply a delegation card to one of their own recurring tasks twice. Standing context and custom assistants follow in USE-FLU-202.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Analyse a work task into steps and assign each to the person, the assistant, both or neither, with a reason based on risk, skill and accountability.
- Prepare a request that gives the assistant the goal, context, audience, constraints, success criteria and an example, and refine it over at least three turns.
- Test the assistant on a task type that is new to the participant by comparing its output with a known-good answer before deciding to delegate that task.
- Test a polished AI output for invented facts, missing context, faulty reasoning and agreement with a wrong premise.
- Decide whether to use, limit or refuse AI help for a task and defend the decision, including cases where AI should not be used.
- Draft a disclosure note that states what the assistant did, what the participant checked and who is accountable.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-FLU-101 · Data and AI Literacy Baseline for Everyone at Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-101.md)
- Uses documents, email and spreadsheets in daily work
- Has access to an approved AI assistant, or uses the one provided in class

## Format and days

### Day 1: أربع عادات: فوِّض وصِف واحكم وتحمَّل

- التفويض: ما الذي تسلّمه للمساعد؟
- الحد المتعرج: اختبر قبل أن تفوّض
- الوصف: السياق والمعايير
- التكرار: التحسين على جولات
- الحكم: التحقق من المخرج المصقول
- المسؤولية: القرار والإفصاح

## Topics

### Delegate: what to hand over

- Automation, augmentation and agency
- The uneven frontier: test AI task by task against a known answer
- Tasks to keep: judgement, accountability, skills you must retain
- Confidential and high-impact work

### Describe: context and criteria

- Goal, audience, constraints and success criteria
- Examples and counter-examples
- Asking the assistant to ask questions first
- Giving source material instead of relying on the model's memory

### Iterate

- Critique-and-revise cycles
- Asking for alternatives and for the reasoning
- Structured outputs such as tables and checklists
- When to start again

### Judge: verifying polished output

- Why finished artefacts get checked less
- Invented facts, figures and citations
- Missing context and wrong premises
- Agreement with the user rather than the evidence

### Own: responsibility and disclosure

- Accountability stays with the author
- Disclosure notes
- Low-quality output passed on to colleagues
- Keeping data within approved tools

# USE-FLU-202 · AI Productivity for Knowledge Work

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Everyone](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-FLU.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked 30-day follow-up task
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-202/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-202/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-202/practice.html

## Description

The Academy's published four-day course plus a capstone day, delivered Arabic-first. Day one covers where AI helps and harms, safe use, and structured requests with persistent context. Day two applies them to Arabic and English writing, reading and extraction, spreadsheets and presentations. Day three covers deep research with verification, source-grounded notebooks, custom assistants and workflow redesign. Day four introduces agents with connectors and approvals, and building a small tool from a requirements document. In the capstone each participant redesigns one real recurring task and measures the gain over two trials against a baseline.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Apply a structured request pattern with persistent context to writing, summarising and extraction tasks in Arabic and English.
- Use an assistant to analyse a spreadsheet and produce a chart and a summary, with every reported figure checked by recalculation.
- Prepare a research brief with a deep-research tool and a source-grounded notebook, tracing each key claim to a source that exists and supports it.
- Configure a custom assistant with instructions, reference files and test questions for a recurring team task.
- Configure an agent run that uses a connector under least-privilege permissions with a human approval step, and identify the prompt-injection risk in its inputs.
- Draft a requirements document for a small internal tool and produce a working prototype with a generative coding platform, tested against three checks.
- Design an AI-assisted version of a real recurring task and measure the change in time and quality against a baseline over two trials.
- Prepare a personal adoption plan over one, seven and thirty days, including tasks kept AI-off to preserve skill and checks that stop unverified work reaching colleagues.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-FLU-101 · Data and AI Literacy Baseline for Everyone at Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-101.md)
- Uses documents, email and spreadsheets in daily work
- Brings one real recurring task from their own job, described without confidential details

## Next courses

- [USE-FLU-301 · Redesigning a Team Workflow with AI and Measuring the Gain](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-301.md)
- [USE-FLU-302 · Team Build-and-Own Studio: One Application for One Entity](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-302.md)
- [USE-FLU-303 · Leading AI Adoption in a Team: Champions and Trainers](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-303.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: الأساس: أين يساعد الذكاء الاصطناعي وأين يضرّ

- أين يساعد وأين يضرّ
- التصنيف قبل المشاركة
- الطلب المهيكل
- الحوار والسياق الدائم

### Day 2: المهام اليومية

- الكتابة والمستوى اللغوي
- القراءة والاستخراج
- الجداول والتحقق من الأرقام
- العروض والصور

### Day 3: البحث والمعرفة الموثوقة

- البحث المعمق والتحقق
- الدفاتر المستندة إلى المصادر
- المساعدات المخصصة
- إعادة تصميم سير العمل

### Day 4: الوكلاء والأدوات الصغيرة والتبنّي المسؤول

- الوكلاء والموصِّلات
- من الفكرة إلى المتطلبات
- ابنِ واختبر وشارك
- التبنّي المسؤول

### Day 5: عروض المشروع الختامي


## Topics

### Foundations: where AI helps and where it harms

- Task-level evidence and the uneven frontier
- Delegation, description, discernment and diligence
- Classification before sharing
- Structured requests, dialogue and persistent context

### Everyday tasks

- Arabic and English writing, editing and register
- Reading, summarising and extraction
- Spreadsheets and data analysis
- Presentations and images

### Research and trustworthy knowledge

- Deep research and verification
- Source-grounded notebooks and projects
- Custom assistants and reusable skills
- Workflow redesign

### Agents and small tools

- Agents and scheduled tasks
- Connectors, permissions and prompt injection
- From idea to requirements document and agent instruction file
- Build, test and share a prototype; production deployment belongs to developers

### Responsible adoption

- The cost of unchecked output passed to colleagues
- Keeping your own skill: deliberate AI-off practice
- Disclosure and records
- The one, seven and thirty day plan

### Measuring value

- Baselines before change
- Time and quality measures
- Two trials and honest reporting
- Costs of checking and rework

# USE-FLU-203 · Research and Verification with AI

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Everyone](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-FLU.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days of four sessions, each with a 25-minute lab, plus a tracked research task and a live spot-check
- Total hours: 12 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-203/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-203/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-203/practice.html

## Description

Participants run research with AI tools and practise standing behind every claim they pass on. They write a research brief, classify the claims in an AI-generated report by type, read laterally to judge unfamiliar sources, trace statistics and quotations to their origin, audit citations for existence and support, and test how often a source-grounded notebook's answers are supported by the passage they cite. They finish with a verified brief on a question from their own work, built from public sources, with a verification log and a confidence statement for each key finding.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare a research brief that sets the question, scope, source standards and the decision it will inform.
- Classify the claims in an AI-generated report by type and choose the check that each type needs.
- Apply lateral reading to judge the reliability of unfamiliar sources and trace each claim to its original.
- Test every citation in an AI answer for existence, correct attribution and support for the claim it is attached to.
- Use a source-grounded notebook on a curated document set and measure how often its answers are supported by the cited passage.
- Deliver a verified research brief with a verification log and a confidence statement for each key finding.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-FLU-201 · Working with AI Assistants: Delegate, Describe, Judge, Own](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-201.md)
- Participants who completed USE-FLU-202 meet the USE-FLU-201 prerequisite
- Searches the web confidently and reads sources in English as well as Arabic

## Format and days

### Day 1: قبل البحث وأثناءه: الموجز والادعاءات والمصادر

- موجز البحث قبل أي بحث
- أنواع الادعاءات وفحص كل نوع
- القراءة الجانبية
- التتبع إلى الأصل

### Day 2: الاستشهادات وأدوات البحث والتقرير

- استشهادات موجودة وتقول ما نُسب إليها
- أدوات البحث: الوكيل والدفتر
- قياس دعم الإجابات
- اكتب ما تحققت منه

### Day 3: الموجز المتحقق منه والفحص المباشر بالعينة


## Topics

### Framing the research

- Research briefs: question, scope, decision, deadline
- What counts as evidence for this question
- A search plan across languages, including Arabic sources

### Claim types and their checks

- Facts, statistics, causal claims, quotations, rules and predictions
- Matching each claim type to a check
- Primary versus secondary sources

### Lateral reading

- Stop, investigate the source, find better coverage, trace to the original
- Judging unfamiliar sites, authors and outlets
- Outdated and superseded official pages

### Citations that exist and say what is claimed

- Resolving digital object identifiers (DOIs) and links
- Archived versions of changed pages
- Misattribution and quotation drift
- Invented references
- Retracted papers and predatory outlets

### Working with AI research tools

- How deep-research agents plan and where they fail
- Source-grounded notebooks over a curated document set
- Measuring whether answers are supported
- Images and screenshots: reverse search and provenance

### Reporting what you verified

- The verification log
- Confidence statements and remaining limitations
- Disclosure of AI assistance
- Keeping personal and classified data out of research tools

---

# USE-FLU-204 · Supervising AI Agents in Knowledge Work

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Everyone](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-FLU.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days of four sessions with labs, guided pre-work and a tracked agent task
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-204/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-204/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-204/practice.html

## Description

Participants hand multi-step work to an AI agent that acts on mail, files and calendars through connectors and on a schedule, and stay in charge. In a sandbox of synthetic data they brief the agent, grant permissions stepwise, gate irreversible actions, catch planted injections and review transcripts, then supervise a task of their own over two runs.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare a delegation brief with goal, standing context, permitted sources, forbidden actions, stop conditions and result format.
- Configure least-privilege connector permissions and approval before every send, delete, payment or publication.
- Test an agent against hidden instructions and apply a stop, contain and report routine.
- Analyse agent transcripts for skipped steps, invented facts, actions beyond the brief and unsupported claims of success.
- Design and supervise an agent task from the participant's own work and decide to keep, change or stop it.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-FLU-201 · Working with AI Assistants: Delegate, Describe, Judge, Own](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-201.md)
- USE-FLU-202 also meets the prerequisite
- Classifies work material before sharing it (USE-FLU-104)

## Format and days

### Day 1: التفويض والصلاحيات

- محادثة أم مسار ثابت أم وكيل؟
- موجز التفويض
- قراءة وكتابة وتصرّف
- الموافقات والتشغيل المجدول

### Day 2: الأمن والمراجعة

- التعليمات المخفية
- أوقف، واحتوِ، وبلّغ
- قراءة السجل خطوة خطوة
- وكلاء متوازيون وسجل الموافقات

### Day 3: مناقشة مهمة الوكيل


## Topics

### Choosing and briefing

- Chat, fixed workflow or agent
- Partial versus complete task success
- Standing instructions, project files and skills

### Permissions and approvals

- Read, write and act scopes
- Time-limited access and revocation
- Scheduled and background runs

### Security for the delegator

- Hidden instructions in mail, pages, files and images
- Untrusted content, private data and an outbound channel
- Poisoned memory and standing context

### Reviewing agent work

- Reading a transcript step by step
- Parallel agents and review time
- Records of who approved what

---

# USE-FLU-205 · Building Small Tools without Code

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Everyone](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-FLU.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days of four sessions with labs, guided pre-work and a tracked build task
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-205/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-205/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-205/practice.html

## Description

Participants who do not program turn a team need, such as a request tracker, into a small, tested internal tool with a generative coding platform. They specify users, data, rules and access levels, direct the coding agent through an instruction file, accept each change only after a test, check for exposed data, secrets and missing access control, and write a hand-over note. Production deployment belongs to developers (DEV-SWE-201).

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish a team prototype from a production system and identify requests that need developers.
- Draft a one-page specification with users, data fields, rules, access levels and acceptance tests.
- Use a generative coding platform and an instruction file to build the tool in small, tested, reversible steps.
- Test a prototype for exposed personal data, hard-coded secrets, missing access control and wrong calculations.
- Deliver a tested internal tool with a hand-over note naming owner, permitted data, access levels, limits and when developers take over.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-FLU-201 · Working with AI Assistants: Delegate, Describe, Judge, Own](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-201.md)
- USE-FLU-202 also meets the prerequisite
- Keeps data in spreadsheet tables; no programming needed

## Format and days

### Day 1: من الحاجة إلى نموذج يعمل

- أصغر أداة نافعة
- اختبارات القبول ومستويات الوصول
- ملف التعليمات وسياق المشروع
- خطوات صغيرة ونقاط حفظ وتراجع

### Day 2: اختبر، وافحص، وسلّم

- الحالات الطرفية والحساب باليد
- الاختبار بكل دور
- البيانات والأسرار والروابط العامة
- الملكية ومذكرة التسليم

### Day 3: عروض الأدوات الحية


## Topics

### From need to specification

- The smallest useful tool
- Acceptance tests before building
- Who sees, edits and administers

### Directing a coding agent

- Instruction files and project context
- Small steps, checkpoints and undo
- When to start again

### Testing without code

- Edge cases and hand-checked calculations
- Testing in each user role
- Arabic text and right-to-left screens

### Safety and ownership

- No real personal or classified data
- Secrets, keys and public links
- Owner, support and retirement

# USE-FLU-206 · Creating Images, Audio and Video with AI Responsibly

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Everyone](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-FLU.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: one day of six short sessions with labs, guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up
- Total hours: 8 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants produce images, voice-overs and short videos for work and publish them responsibly. They brief and refine assets, check text, Arabic lettering, symbols and cultural detail, decide when consent or rights clearance is needed, refuse impersonation, apply labels and provenance metadata, inspect received media, and add captions, alternative text and transcripts. A tracked follow-up applies the method to one real communication need.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare a media brief and use generation tools to produce matching assets, logging prompts and settings.
- Test generated assets for factual, textual, cultural and visual errors, including Arabic lettering.
- Classify a media use by consent, rights and impersonation risk and decide whether it may proceed.
- Apply labels, provenance metadata, captions, alternative text and transcripts to finished assets.
- Explain what provenance metadata and watermarks can and cannot prove about a received file.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-FLU-201 · Working with AI Assistants: Delegate, Describe, Judge, Own](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-201.md)
- USE-FLU-104 recommended
- Prepares internal or public communication

## Topics

### Briefing and checking

- Purpose, audience and message first
- Text, hands, symbols and Arabic script
- Cultural and religious sensitivities

### Rights and consent

- Likeness and voice of real people
- Photos of identifiable people as personal data
- Tool licences and copyright

### Labelling and provenance

- Visible labels and content credentials
- Removable watermarks
- Checking received media

### Accessible media

- Alternative text
- Captions and transcripts

---

# USE-FLU-207 · Arabic Writing, Translation and Dialect Work with AI

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Everyone](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-FLU.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: one day of six short sessions with labs, guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up
- Total hours: 8 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-207/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-207/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-flu-207/practice.html

## Description

Participants produce and check Arabic work with AI assistants: official letters, summaries of English reports, bilingual text and dialect transcripts. They set register for formal and plain-language Arabic, control translation in both directions with a glossary, compare two assistants, find where dialect output fails, check names, numbers, Hijri and Gregorian dates against the source, and fix bidirectional text faults. A tracked follow-up checks one real document.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare requests that set register, tone, audience and terminology for formal and plain-language Arabic.
- Draft a bilingual glossary and use it to control an AI translation in both directions.
- Test AI translations and summaries against the source for wrong names, numbers, dates, units and omissions.
- Analyse two assistants on the same Arabic tasks and record where neither is usable without a native reviewer or translator.
- Analyse and fix bidirectional faults such as reversed numbers and misplaced punctuation.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-FLU-201 · Working with AI Assistants: Delegate, Describe, Judge, Own](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-201.md)
- Writes formal Modern Standard Arabic and reads English documents

## Format and days

### Day 1: العربية مع المساعد: اضبط وقابل وراجع

- المستوى اللغوي قبل الصياغة
- المسرد يضبط الترجمة
- الأسماء والأرقام والتواريخ أمام المصدر
- اللهجات وحدود المساعدين
- النص في اتجاهين
- قبل أن يحمل النص اسمك

## Topics

### Register and tone

- Formal and plain public Arabic
- Official letter conventions
- Arabic that reads as translated

### Glossary-driven translation

- Supplying a term list
- Back-translation checks
- When a professional translator is required

### Dialects, names and dates

- Saudi and other regional dialects
- Names, digits and units
- Hijri and Gregorian dates

### Bidirectional text

- Direction marks and mixed runs
- Spreadsheets, slides and forms

# USE-FLU-301 · Redesigning a Team Workflow with AI and Measuring the Gain

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Everyone](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-FLU.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Studio: five-week coached team project with three workshops, two coach reviews, two pilot runs and a panel defence
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Teams from one unit redesign a recurring workflow, such as handling enquiries or a monthly report, under coaching. They baseline time, quality and errors, map the workflow, assign each step to a person, assistant, agent or fixed rule on a delegation card with the check each AI step needs, and pilot the redesign twice against the baseline. They report the measured result, including checking and rework time, decide to scale, change or stop, and defend it before a panel. Organisation-wide redesign is LDS-EXE-203.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Measure a baseline for a team workflow: time per case, rubric quality, error rate and rework.
- Analyse the workflow into steps with input data, classification, decision and accountable person.
- Design a delegation card assigning each step to a person, assistant, agent or rule, with the check each AI step needs.
- Evaluate the redesign in two pilot runs against the baseline, counting checking and rework time and errors passed on.
- Decide whether to scale, change or stop the redesign and defend the decision with evidence.
- Prepare a 30-day plan with owners, measures, AI-off practice for skills to keep and a stop rule.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-FLU-202 · AI Productivity for Knowledge Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-202.md)
- USE-FLU-201 with USE-FLU-204 is accepted instead
- A team of three to six from one unit, with a sponsoring manager

## Topics

### Choosing and baselining

- Frequent, bounded, checkable work
- Time, quality, error and rework measures
- What a small sample can show

### Mapping and splitting

- Steps, inputs, decisions and owners
- Data classification per step
- Person, assistant, agent or rule

### Designing the checks

- Verification by step and risk
- Unchecked output passed to colleagues
- Skills the team must keep

### Running the pilot

- Fixed samples and two runs
- Logging checking time
- Blind quality scoring

### Deciding and sustaining

- Scale, change or stop
- Tool cost against time saved
- Stop rules

---

# USE-FLU-302 · Team Build-and-Own Studio: One Application for One Entity

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Everyone](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-FLU.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Studio: four-week coached team project with mentor engineers, weekly reviews, a supervised trial and a defence
- Total hours: 40 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Teams of two to four from one organisation take one sponsor-owned problem, such as answering staff questions from a policy handbook, to a working assistant or agent with mentor engineers. They frame the problem, agree data rules with the data owner, build on an approved low-code or hosted platform, test with questions written with users, run a supervised trial and hand the application to a named owner with a support routine and a retirement condition. Production engineering belongs to DEV-LLM-201 and DEV-SEC-201.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Draft a problem statement with users, process, success measures, risk tier and constraints.
- Prepare a data-use record classifying each source and stating what the application may read, store and send.
- Build a working assistant or agent on an approved platform within the data rules.
- Test the application with user-written questions, including required refusals, hidden instructions in documents and data-extraction attempts.
- Evaluate a supervised user trial and decide whether to continue, change or stop.
- Deliver a hand-over pack naming owner, technical contact, support routine, limits, retirement condition and cases for developers.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-FLU-202 · AI Productivity for Knowledge Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-202.md)
- One member has completed USE-FLU-205 or built a custom assistant
- A sponsor who owns the problem and a data owner who approves data use

## Topics

### Framing the problem

- Problems an assistant can solve
- Risk tier and problems to turn down
- Sponsor and decision rights

### Data rules

- Classification of every source
- Read, store and send permissions
- Minimisation and owner approval

### Building on a platform

- Reference files, tools and connectors
- Answers that cite their source
- Limits of low-code platforms

### Testing and trial

- User-written question sets
- Refusal, leak and injection tests
- Usage logs

### Ownership

- Support and update routines
- Retirement conditions
- Hand-over to developers

# USE-FLU-303 · Leading AI Adoption in a Team: Champions and Trainers

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Everyone](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-FLU.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Workshop: two days of four sessions with labs, an observed practice clinic and a tracked 30-day follow-up
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

A train-the-trainer workshop for nominated AI champions. Participants plan and run a 45-minute clinic on colleagues' real tasks, teach a short lesson with AI-off practice and give feedback on requests and checks. They curate a shared library of requests and delegation cards, measure use and value beyond self-report, and agree how to handle low-quality AI output passed between colleagues. Leaders' adoption programmes are LDS-EXE-204.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare a 45-minute clinic plan with a short lesson, a worked example, an AI-off task and safe task collection.
- Lead a clinic and give feedback that improves colleagues' requests and checks.
- Configure a shared library of requests, standing context and delegation cards with owner, data rules and review date.
- Measure use and value with indicators, a survey and a time sample rather than self-report alone.
- Deliver a 30-day adoption report on clinics, library use, measured change and a unit agreement on checking AI work before sharing it.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-FLU-202 · AI Productivity for Knowledge Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-202.md)
- Uses AI assistants weekly in own work
- Nominated by a manager who agrees to the follow-up

## Topics

### The champion role

- Champion, trainer and manager
- Organisational conditions over individual skill
- Escalation beyond the role

### Teaching adults

- Worked examples, then AI-off practice
- Tutor mode versus answer mode
- Reluctant and over-confident colleagues

### Clinics and libraries

- Collecting tasks without confidential data
- Review dates and retirement

### Measuring and sharing

- Why self-report overstates gains
- Time samples
- Returning low-quality output without blame

# USE-EDU-101 · Data and AI Fluency for University Students

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Learners and Educators](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-EDU.md)
- Level: Level 100 · Explain
- Format: Extended: 10 weeks part-time, one two-hour class with a lab each week, tracked weekly tasks and a use-case capstone
- Total hours: 40 h
- Audience: beginner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-edu-101/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-edu-101/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-edu-101/practice.html

## Description

Students from any discipline work through the six components of the national cross-disciplinary curriculum, from AI concepts and data as evidence to verification and applied use in their own field. Weekly labs on synthetic or public data end in a tracked artefact. The capstone is a use-case plan with a justified AI or non-AI choice, a risk tier, safeguards and a cost rationale.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish AI, machine learning, deep learning, generative AI and AI agents, and a model from the system around it.
- Identify the evidence, assumptions and limitations behind a data-based claim, including correlation presented as cause.
- Explain how data quality, representativeness and labelling drive a learned system's errors, using false positives, false negatives and base rates.
- Use structured requests with audience, constraints and quality criteria, and score generative output against them.
- Apply a verification and disclosure routine to AI-assisted work, classifying the data and sanitising the prompt first.
- Prepare a use-case plan for a bounded discipline task that justifies AI, data analysis, both or neither, with risk tier, safeguards, evaluation and cost.

## Prerequisites

- None: open to undergraduates in any discipline; no programming is required

## Next courses

- [USE-EDU-202 · Delivering the Cross-Disciplinary Data and AI Curriculum](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-EDU-202.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: ما الذكاء الاصطناعي وما حدوده

- خمس كلمات وأربع مهام

### Day 2: النموذج والنظام والمسؤولية

- النموذج جزء من نظام

### Day 3: البيانات دليل: اقرأ الادعاء قبل أن تصدّقه

- من الجدول إلى الادعاء

### Day 4: كيف تتعلم الآلة ومتى تخطئ

- السمات والوسوم والتعميم

### Day 5: لماذا تضلّل الدقة

- ما لا تقوله نسبة الدقة

### Day 6: الذكاء الاصطناعي التوليدي: احتمالي وغير متساوٍ

- ما يولّده وما لا يضمنه

### Day 7: الطلب المهيكل وتقييم المخرج

- من أمر عابر إلى طلب مهيكل

### Day 8: التحقق والإفصاح والنزاهة

- تحقق ثم أفصح

### Day 9: حوكمة البيانات ومخاطر الأدوات

- صنّف ونقّح ثم ضع بوابة

### Day 10: من المهمة إلى خطة حالة الاستخدام

- خطة تُراجَع وتُناقَش

### Day 11: مناقشة خطط حالات الاستخدام


## Topics

### AI concepts and limits

- Task types: classification, forecasting, recommendation, generation
- Model versus system: retrieval, tools, people in the loop
- Assistant to agent: permissions and approval gates
- Automation bias and the accountability boundary

### Data as evidence and how machines learn

- Provenance, quality dimensions, sampling and measurement bias
- Data lifecycle, roles and classification
- Training and testing, overfitting, data shift, leakage
- Why accuracy misleads

### Generative AI, verification and safe use

- Probabilistic output and the confidence gap
- Task, audience, constraints, quality criteria, verification request
- Deepfakes, intellectual property and academic integrity
- Prompt injection, analysed but never attempted

### Applied use in a discipline

- Avoiding unnecessary automation
- Risk tiers, including unacceptable uses
- Cost and sustainability, including the hidden costs of free tools
- Tracks: the curriculum's five plus health, business, law, engineering and education

# USE-EDU-102 · Learning with AI without Losing the Skill

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Learners and Educators](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-EDU.md)
- Level: Level 100 · Explain
- Format: Primer: a half-day, facilitated or self-paced, with a scenario test
- Total hours: 4 h
- Audience: beginner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-edu-102/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-edu-102/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-edu-102/practice.html

## Description

Learners see trial evidence that open assistants lower later unaided performance while a hint-only tutor does not. They compare answer and tutor modes, sort interaction patterns, set an assistant to tutor, and plan two weeks of AI-off-first practice with retrieval.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish interaction patterns that build understanding from those that replace it, citing trial evidence.
- Configure an assistant to give one hint at a time, ask for explain-back and withhold final answers.
- Prepare a two-week practice plan with AI-off first attempts, retrieval and spacing.

## Prerequisites

- None

## Format and days

### Day 1: من وضع الإجابة إلى وضع الإرشاد

- الأدلة: مكسب التدرب ليس تعلّمًا
- أنماط تساعد وأنماط تضر
- وضع الإرشاد وخطة الأسبوعين

## Topics

### The evidence

- Practice gains versus unaided performance
- Why effortful practice feels worse

### Patterns that help and harm

- Delegation, repeated AI debugging
- Conceptual questions, generate-then-explain
- Polished answers get checked less

### Tutor mode

- Study modes and their limits
- Retrieval, spacing, disclosure

---

# USE-EDU-201 · Teaching and Assessing in the AI Era

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Learners and Educators](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-EDU.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days with labs, guided pre-work and a tracked redesign task
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-edu-201/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-edu-201/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-edu-201/practice.html

## Description

Educators stress-test a course's assessments with assistants and redesign them in two lanes: secure tasks that certify unaided skill, and open tasks with guided, disclosed and defended AI use. They see why detectors fail, practise orals and process-evidence review, and write a course AI policy. Credential policy is LDS-EXE-302.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain why AI-text detectors cannot support an integrity decision.
- Analyse each graded task for what it certifies and how far an assistant completes it.
- Classify tasks into secure and open lanes and draft a course AI policy with per-task use labels.
- Prepare a short oral check and a process-evidence review.
- Design a replacement for an exposed assignment that rewards judgement, process and defence.

## Prerequisites

- Teaches or assesses learners in any setting
- Brings one course's assessment briefs, without student data

## Format and days

### Day 1: ما الذي تشهد به تقييماتك؟

- اختبار الصمود: ما الذي تشهد به كل مهمة؟
- لماذا تفشل أدوات الكشف
- نموذج المسارين: مؤمَّن حيث تشهد، ومفتوح حيث تعلّم
- تصنيف الاستخدام في كل مهمة وسياسة المقرر

### Day 2: أدلة لا يكتبها أحد عن المتعلم

- الأدلة الإجرائية: المسودات وسجل الإصدارات وسجل المحادثة
- الاختبار الشفهي القصير
- مهام تحتاج إلى حكم وسياق محلي ونقد للذكاء الاصطناعي
- أعد الاختبار ودافع عن تصميمك

### Day 3: مراجعة خطط التقييم المعاد تصميمها


## Topics

### Why detection fails

- Error rates at cohort scale
- Bias against non-native writers
- Human review before any finding

### The two-lane model

- Secure tasks at stage gates
- Open tasks with an AI-use menu and disclosure
- Why unenforceable bans damage validity
- Tasks needing judgement, local context or critique of AI

### Oral and process evidence

- Orals: single questions, randomised cases, think time
- Drafts, version history, transcripts
- Accessible alternatives to voice orals

---

# USE-EDU-202 · Delivering the Cross-Disciplinary Data and AI Curriculum

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Learners and Educators](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-EDU.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days with labs, guided pre-work and a micro-teach
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-edu-202/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-edu-202/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-edu-202/practice.html

## Description

Faculty prepare to teach the national cross-disciplinary data and AI curriculum: they choose stand-alone, embedded or distributed delivery and map it to the outcomes, adapt the recommended labs, build a discipline track pack, calibrate marking of use-case plans and teach one component. Wider assessment redesign is USE-EDU-201.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain the six components, the six intended learning outcomes and their mapping to international frameworks.
- Prepare an alignment matrix from a chosen delivery model to the intended and component outcomes.
- Adapt one recommended lab and build a track pack with a local case and synthetic mini-dataset.
- Apply the curriculum's assessment principles to mark student use-case plans.
- Deliver a ten-minute hands-on micro-teach of one component.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-EDU-101 · Data and AI Fluency for University Students](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-EDU-101.md)
- Or an AI-off entry check on the six components
- Teaches or will teach a university course

## Format and days

### Day 1: المنهج والتدريس بالممارسة

- المنهج وخياراته
- مقارنة التوقع بالواقع
- تمرين الفرق الحمراء
- اختبار التغطية
- نمط التقديم ومصفوفة المواءمة

### Day 2: من الخطة إلى القاعة

- تكييف مختبر وتنفيذه مع الزملاء
- حزم المسارات
- التقييم ومعايرة التقدير

### Day 3: التدريس المصغر وخطة التقديم


## Topics

### The curriculum and its options

- Intended and component outcomes
- Stand-alone, embedded or distributed delivery
- Optional enrichment topics

### Teaching by doing

- Prediction versus reality, red-team challenge, coverage test
- Workflow map, prompt tournament, data-governance and tool-risk labs
- Effortful labs feel less effective

### Track packs

- The five listed tracks and their rules
- New packs for health, business, law, engineering and education

### Assessment

- Verification, disclosure, data safety, cultural and context sensitivity
- Marking calibration and moderation

---

# USE-EDU-203 · AI Literacy for School Teachers

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Learners and Educators](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-EDU.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: three three-hour sessions, guided pre-work and a tracked trial lesson
- Total hours: 12 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-edu-203/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-edu-203/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-edu-203/practice.html

## Description

Teachers of any subject map competence frameworks for teachers and pupils, run age-banded activities as pupils would (unplugged sorting, training and breaking a classifier, checking a chatbot), plan a lesson for their subject, apply safeguarding rules, write to families about the class's AI rules, and teach the lesson once for review.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compare the competence frameworks for teachers and pupils and identify those a lesson addresses.
- Use age-appropriate activities to teach how AI learns, fails and is checked.
- Prepare a lesson for one's subject with an AI-literacy objective and an AI-off understanding check.
- Apply safeguarding rules for pupils' data, tool age limits and generated images of real people.
- Draft a plain-language letter to families on how AI is and is not used in class.

## Prerequisites

- Teaches or leads in a primary or secondary school
- Has used an AI assistant for a few tasks

## Format and days

### Day 1: الأطر، وكيف يتعلم الذكاء الاصطناعي

- الأطر: الإلمام بالذكاء الاصطناعي ليس استخدام الأدوات
- الصفوف الأولية: لعبة تصنيف دون حاسوب
- الصفوف العليا: درّب مصنِّفًا ثم أفشِله

### Day 2: التحقق، ثم درس في مادتك

- المرحلة الثانوية: تحقق من روبوت محادثة
- التحيز والوسائط الاصطناعية
- خطة درس في مادتك

### Day 3: حماية الطلاب، والأسر، والدرس التجريبي

- حماية الطلاب: البيانات والأدوات والصور
- الأسر: رسالة واضحة عن قواعد الصف
- الاختبار القصير والدرس التجريبي

### Day 4: مراجعة الدرس التجريبي


## Topics

### Frameworks

- UNESCO teacher and student competences
- OECD and European Commission domains: engage, create, manage, shape
- AI literacy versus tool use

### Activities by age band

- Early primary: unplugged sorting games
- Upper primary: train and break a classifier
- Secondary: check a chatbot, spot bias and synthetic media

### Safeguarding and families

- Pupils' data and approved tools
- Synthetic images of real people and reporting
- Homework, unequal home access and disclosure

---

# USE-EDU-204 · Designing AI Tutors and Course Assistants

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Learners and Educators](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-EDU.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two half-days with labs, guided pre-work and a tracked pilot
- Total hours: 12 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Educators configure a course assistant that tutors rather than solves and test it before learners meet it: hint-ladder and explain-back instructions, worked solutions and a rubric for accurate hints, guardrails, and learner-style probes including answer extraction. They then plan how to measure its effect on unaided performance. Building tutor software is Developers work.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain what separates a tutor from an answer engine.
- Configure a hint-only tutor with standing instructions, worked solutions and a rubric.
- Test the tutor with learner-style questions, including answer-extraction attempts.
- Implement guardrails for learner privacy, AI disclosure and escalation to the teacher.
- Design a small evaluation of whether the tutor improves unaided performance.

## Prerequisites

- Can supply a course's worked solutions, rubric and practice problems
- Has written standing instructions for an assistant, or completed USE-FLU-201

## Topics

### What makes a tutor work

- Tutor trials versus open-assistant trials
- Worked solutions and rubrics in context
- Hint ladders and explain-back in Arabic and English

### Guardrails and testing

- Answer extraction and instruction override
- Retention and teacher oversight
- Leak and error rates, retest after each fix

### Measuring learning effect

- Practice scores versus unaided post-tests
- Crossover and comparison groups, consent
- AI that supports a human tutor instead

---

# USE-PRO-201 · AI for Public Servants and Policy Work

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Professions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-PRO.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days of labs on one synthetic case, plus a tracked baseline
- Total hours: 12 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-pro-201/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-pro-201/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-pro-201/practice.html

## Description

A synthetic ministry is consulting the public on a new licensing rule. Participants do its drafting and analysis with an approved assistant, classifying material before it enters a tool and tracing every factual statement to an official source.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Identify AI drafting errors typical of government work: superseded rules, invented article numbers, misattributed positions.
- Classify case documents by sensitivity and match each to the tools its level allows.
- Prepare a consultation summary with theme counts that keeps minority positions and flags duplicate campaign comments.
- Draft an options brief and a citizen notice in which every factual statement cites an official source.
- Redesign one recurring task from the participant's work and measure time and errors before and after.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-FLU-201 · Working with AI Assistants: Delegate, Describe, Judge, Own](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-201.md)
- Drafts official correspondence, briefs or minutes in current work

## Format and days

### Day 1: اعرف أين يخطئ المساعد، وصنّف قبل أن تكتب الأمر

- أخطاء المساعد في أعمال السياسات
- التحقق من المصادر الرسمية
- مستويات التصنيف والأدوات المصرح بها
- البيانات الشخصية والأمر المنقّح

### Day 2: حلّل الاستشارة واكتب ما يمكن تتبّعه

- ترميز التعليقات وعدّها
- مواقف الأقلية والحملات والتعليمات المخفية
- إحاطة الخيارات بعمود للمصادر
- الإشعار للمواطن والإفصاح وقياس إعادة التصميم

### Day 3: بطاقة إعادة التصميم والمراجعة المباشرة


## Topics

### Policy work and its AI failure modes

- Superseded rules and unsourced figures
- Summaries that drop minority views
- Campaign comments and instructions hidden in submissions

### Checking against official sources

- Gazettes, legislation portals and statistics releases
- Effective dates and consolidated texts

### Government data rules

- Classification levels and approved tools
- Personal data in case files
- Freedom of information and disclosure of AI use

---

# USE-PRO-202 · AI for Human Resources and Talent Work

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Professions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-PRO.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days of labs on one synthetic case, plus a tracked baseline
- Total hours: 12 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-pro-202/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-pro-202/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-pro-202/practice.html

## Description

A synthetic organisation is hiring an analyst and planning team learning. Participants prepare adverts, interviews and learning plans with an assistant and test it for bias with matched curricula vitae (CVs), under one rule: AI helps prepare, people decide about people.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain why ranking candidates with a general assistant is high-risk and which HR decisions stay with people.
- Analyse an AI-drafted job description for exclusionary wording and inflated requirements, and revise it.
- Test a screening prompt for bias with applications that differ only in name, gender or age.
- Prepare an interview guide and learning plans without passing identifiable data to unapproved tools.
- Redesign one recurring HR task and measure time, errors and fairness before and after.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-FLU-201 · Working with AI Assistants: Delegate, Describe, Judge, Own](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-201.md)
- Works in recruitment, talent, learning or employee relations, or manages those who do

## Format and days

### Day 1: أين يساعد الذكاء الاصطناعي في الموارد البشرية، وأين يدخل التحيز

- مهام الموارد البشرية وموضع الذكاء الاصطناعي فيها
- الوصف الوظيفي: الصياغة والمتطلبات
- كيف يدخل التحيز، واختبار الأزواج المتطابقة
- قراءة النتيجة: الفرق أمام التباين

### Day 2: تقييم منصف، وبيانات موظفين محمية، وإعادة تصميم تُقاس

- الأسئلة المرتبطة بالوظيفة وسلالم التقدير المرتكزة
- بيانات الموظفين قبل أي أمر
- خطط تعلم مبنية على الفجوات
- إعادة تصميم مهمة وقياسها

### Day 3: بطاقة إعادة التصميم والمراجعة المباشرة


## Topics

### HR tasks and where AI fits

- Decisions that stay with people
- Candidates' AI use and unreliable detectors

### Bias and screening risk

- How bias enters through data, wording and instructions
- Matched pairs and repeat runs
- Employment as a high-risk use
- Fairness in the redesign measure

### Fair assessment and employee data

- Job-related questions and anchored scales
- Explaining and contesting decisions
- Special-category employee records
- Pseudonymising before prompting

# USE-PRO-203 · AI for Finance, Accounting and Audit Work

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Professions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-PRO.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days of labs on one synthetic case, plus a tracked baseline
- Total hours: 12 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-pro-203/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-pro-203/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-pro-203/practice.html

## Description

Participants close a synthetic organisation's month under one rule: figures come from formulas or code someone can re-run, never from an assistant's prose. They reconcile, repair a budget model, write cell-tied commentary and draw an audit sample.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish figures computed by code or formulas from figures generated as text, and state the check each needs.
- Implement a bank-to-ledger reconciliation with generated code or formulas, proved by control totals.
- Test and repair a budget model with an assistant against hand-worked cases.
- Draft variance commentary and a reproducible audit sample, leaving causes and exceptions to the person's judgement.
- Redesign one recurring finance or audit task and measure time and errors before and after.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-FLU-201 · Working with AI Assistants: Delegate, Describe, Judge, Own](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-201.md)
- Knows double-entry bookkeeping, lookups and conditional sums; notebooks are prepared, so no coding is needed

## Format and days

### Day 1: أرقام يعاد تشغيلها

- محسوب أم مولَّد؟
- رموز مولَّدة تقرؤها وتثبتها
- من البنود غير المتطابقة إلى قائمة المطابقة
- ثق بجدول البيانات أقل

### Day 2: التعليق والعينة وإعادة التصميم

- اختبار لكل إصلاح
- تعليق مرتبط بالخلايا
- عينة يستطيع غيرك إعادة سحبها
- قواعد البيانات وإعادة التصميم المقيسة

### Day 3: مراجعة المهام المعاد تصميمها


## Topics

### Why language models get numbers wrong

- Arithmetic in prose versus computed results
- AI functions in cells that change on recalculation

### Spreadsheets and generated code

- Tracing precedents and dependants
- Running and reading generated code
- Test cases and change logs

### Commentary, audit support and data rules

- Variance explanations tied to cells
- Documented sampling with recorded seeds
- Scepticism towards AI output
- Confidential and payroll data in approved tools

---

# USE-PRO-204 · AI for Legal, Regulatory and Compliance Work

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Professions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-PRO.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days of labs on one synthetic case, plus a tracked baseline
- Total hours: 12 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-pro-204/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-pro-204/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-pro-204/practice.html

## Description

Participants act as the legal team of a synthetic company engaging a data-processing supplier. With an assistant they research, review the contract against a playbook and map a regulation to obligations, checking every authority at source and deciding handling before documents enter a tool.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Identify how AI legal research fails: invented authorities, wrong jurisdiction, repealed provisions, misstated holdings.
- Apply a contract playbook with an assistant to flag deviations, missing clauses and changes between drafts.
- Prepare an obligations register mapping provisions to owners, controls and evidence.
- Classify matter documents for confidentiality, privilege and personal data, and choose the tool and redaction each allows.
- Redesign one recurring legal task and measure time and errors before and after.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-FLU-201 · Working with AI Assistants: Delegate, Describe, Judge, Own](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-201.md)
- Reads contracts, regulations or policies at work and knows how laws are cited locally

## Format and days

### Day 1: المراجع والعقود

- المراجع القانونية: أين يخطئ المساعد وكيف تتحقق
- العقود: دليل المواقف والمقارنة المستقلة

### Day 2: الالتزامات والمستندات

- من الحكم النظامي إلى سجل الالتزامات
- السرية وامتياز السرية المهنية وقرار التعامل

### Day 3: بطاقة إعادة التصميم والمراجعة المباشرة


## Topics

### Where legal AI fails

- Invented cases, articles and quotations
- Agreeing with a leading question

### Checking authorities and contracts

- Legislation portals and consolidated texts
- Authoritative versions and unofficial translations
- Playbook positions, fallbacks and red lines

### Regulatory mapping

- From provision to obligation
- Owners, controls and evidence

### Confidentiality and privilege

- Privilege and third-party tools
- Redaction and pseudonymisation
- Disclosing AI use to clients and courts

---

# USE-PRO-205 · AI for Communications, Media and Content Work

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Professions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-PRO.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days of labs on one synthetic case, plus a tracked baseline
- Total hours: 12 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-pro-205/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-pro-205/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-pro-205/practice.html

## Description

Participants run the content desk for a synthetic public-service launch, drafting in Arabic and English with an assistant, then fact-checking, clearing rights, labelling synthetic media and signing off as separate logged steps. Media generation is USE-FLU-206; translation craft is USE-FLU-207.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Identify editorial risks in AI content: invented quotes and statistics, copy echoing the brief and unlabelled synthetic media.
- Implement an editorial workflow in which drafting, fact checking, rights review and sign-off are separate, logged steps.
- Prepare Arabic and English versions of a release and three posts with identical facts, names and figures.
- Test statistics, quotations and images for source and provenance, and classify synthetic items by required label and consent.
- Redesign one recurring content task and measure time, errors and post-sign-off corrections.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-FLU-201 · Working with AI Assistants: Delegate, Describe, Judge, Own](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-201.md)
- Writes or edits content for publication in Arabic, English or both

## Format and days

### Day 1: اكشف الخطأ ثم افصل الخطوات

- مخاطر النص: الاقتباس والرقم وترديد الموجز
- مخاطر الوسائط: الوسم والموافقة والترخيص
- مسار العمل: أربع خطوات لا يؤديها شخص واحد
- سجل المحتوى والاعتماد المسمّى وما يُقاس

### Day 2: نسختان بحقائق واحدة ووسائط معروفة المنشأ

- حقائق متطابقة في العربية والإنجليزية
- فحص التطابق وانحراف صوت الجهة
- المصادر الأصلية للأرقام والاقتباسات
- منشأ الصور والوسم والموافقة

### Day 3: بطاقة إعادة التصميم والمراجعة المباشرة


## Topics

### Editorial workflows with AI

- Separating drafting from checking and sign-off
- Facts identical across Arabic and English
- Brand voice drift

### Fact checks and provenance

- Primary sources for numbers and quotes
- Reverse image search and Content Credentials
- Why watermarks and missing credentials prove nothing

### Synthetic media, rights and consent

- Labelling generated and edited content
- Likeness, voice and consent
- Licence terms of generated assets
