# USE-PRO-206 · AI for Customer and Citizen Service Work

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Professions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-PRO.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days of labs on one synthetic case, plus a tracked baseline
- Total hours: 12 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-pro-206/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-pro-206/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-pro-206/practice.html

## Description

Participants staff a synthetic municipal service centre where an automated agent answers first and hands cases to people. They draft grounded replies, route escalations including impersonation attempts and sample a week of conversations for quality.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish grounded from ungrounded replies and identify their failures, such as invented policies and promises staff cannot keep.
- Use a grounded assistant to draft courteous Arabic and English replies, checked against cited articles.
- Apply escalation rules to route complaints, vulnerable people, rights, safety, refunds above a limit and suspected impersonation.
- Measure reply quality by sampling, rubric scoring and error rates by category.
- Redesign one recurring service task and measure handling time, errors and escalations before and after.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-FLU-201 · Working with AI Assistants: Delegate, Describe, Judge, Own](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-201.md)
- Handles customer or citizen enquiries in Arabic, English or both, or supervises people who do

## Format and days

### Day 1: أجب من المصدر، واعرف ما يبقى لك

- العمل في الخدمة إلى جانب الوكيل الآلي
- الإجابة من قاعدة المعرفة وحدها
- اللباقة واللهجة والإفصاح
- التصعيد وفق القواعد

### Day 2: تسلَّم وتحقَّق، ثم عايِن وقِس

- تسليم الحالة وانتحال الشخصية
- خطة المعاينة وسلم التقدير
- المقيِّم الثاني وإيصال الإصلاحات
- إعادة تصميم مهمة وقياسها

### Day 3: بطاقة إعادة التصميم والمراجعة المباشرة


## Topics

### Service work beside AI

- Handover from agent to person
- What staff own: promises, exceptions, apologies

### Grounding, tone and transparency

- Answering only from the knowledge base
- Stale articles and agreeing with a wrong premise
- Courtesy and dialect in Arabic and English
- Telling people when AI is involved

### Escalation and fraud

- Complaints, vulnerability, rights and safety
- Impersonation and cloned voices

### Quality sampling

- Sampling plans, rubrics and second raters
- Feeding fixes to the knowledge-base owner

---

# USE-PRO-207 · AI for Project, Procurement and Operations Work

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Professions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-PRO.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days of labs on one synthetic case, plus a tracked baseline
- Total hours: 12 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants use AI on project and purchasing paperwork for one synthetic facilities upgrade: a charter, meeting recordings, a risk log and three supplier proposals. They recheck an AI-drafted plan, trace meeting actions to the transcript, compute status from task data and score proposals against preset weights. Buying AI systems is LDS-EXE-205.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Identify AI drafting failures in project documents: invented owners and dates, lost dependencies, inflated status, wrong totals.
- Prepare a project plan with an assistant and test its dependencies, durations and calendar.
- Use a meeting-to-action pipeline to turn recordings into decisions, owned actions and risk updates.
- Apply a weighted evaluation to supplier proposals, with AI extracting values and code computing scores.
- Redesign one of their own recurring tasks with AI and measure time and errors on two runs.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-FLU-201 · Working with AI Assistants: Delegate, Describe, Judge, Own](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-201.md)
- Works in projects, purchasing or operations and uses spreadsheets

## Topics

### Where AI fails here

- Drafting versus deciding and signing
- Polished output gets less checking
- Low-quality output passed between colleagues

### Plans, status and risks

- Dependency and calendar checks
- Status computed under written rules
- Challenging an AI-drafted risk log

### Meetings and suppliers

- Actions traced and confirmed by owners
- Scores computed in code, not by the model
- Bid confidentiality and conflicts of interest

### Measuring a task redesign

- Baseline and delegation card
- Comparing two runs

---

# USE-PRO-208 · AI for Researchers and Scientific Work

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Professions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-PRO.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days of labs on one synthetic case, plus a tracked baseline
- Total hours: 12 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-pro-208/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-pro-208/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-pro-208/practice.html

## Description

Researchers in any discipline use AI on one synthetic project, a scoping question on heat exposure in outdoor workers with 200 retrieved records and a public dataset, from screening and summary checks to a reproducible analysis and a disclosure statement. Research practice for AI scientists is SPC-RSP-301.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish acceptable, disclosable and prohibited research uses of AI.
- Use scholarly databases and an AI screening assistant to map a literature with a recorded search.
- Test AI-written paper summaries for misreported populations, methods, effect sizes and conclusions.
- Implement an AI-assisted analysis from a pre-stated plan and reproduce it from a clean run.
- Redesign one research task with AI, measure it on two runs and disclose the AI use.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-FLU-201 · Working with AI Assistants: Delegate, Describe, Judge, Own](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-201.md)
- Has worked on a research project and can run a provided notebook

## Format and days

### Day 1: النزاهة وخريطة الأدبيات

- ما يُقبل وما يُفصح عنه وما يُحظر
- خريطة الأدبيات: بحث موثّق وفرز يُقاس

### Day 2: الملخصات والتحليل

- اقرأ المصدر لا الملخص
- خطة قبل الأمر، وتشغيل نظيف

### Day 3: جلسة المراجعة: البطاقة والإفصاح والدفتر


## Topics

### Integrity and disclosure

- Misconduct rules applied to AI
- Disclosure rules
- Confidential manuscripts and reviews

### Literature mapping

- Search strategies across databases
- Screening recall and stopping rules
- Checking references and retractions

### Analysis and writing

- Plan before prompt
- Forking paths at machine speed
- Drafting only from own outputs

### Data and participants

- Sensitive and government data
- Ethics approval conditions

---

# USE-PRO-209 · AI for Clinical and Health Professionals

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Professions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-PRO.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days of labs on one synthetic case, plus a tracked baseline
- Total hours: 12 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-pro-209/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-pro-209/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/use-pro-209/practice.html

## Description

Clinicians use AI on the work around care, not the clinical decision, in one synthetic diabetes clinic: notes from scripted consultations, patient information in Arabic and English, evidence lookup, and which patient data may enter which tool. Health-system strategy is USE-SEC-201.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Test an AI-drafted note against its consultation for omissions, fabrications, negation, laterality and dose errors.
- Prepare plain-language Arabic and English patient information and check it against the source guidance.
- Use an evidence assistant and verify each claim against the guideline or trial cited.
- Apply health-data rules to choose a tool per task and de-identify a case.
- Redesign one recurring documentation task with AI, measuring accuracy and time on two runs and keeping one unassisted step.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-FLU-201 · Working with AI Assistants: Delegate, Describe, Judge, Own](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-201.md)
- Practises or trains in a clinical or allied health profession

## Format and days

### Day 1: ما يحيط بالرعاية: الملاحظة وورقة المريض

- حدود الذكاء الاصطناعي في العمل السريري
- أخطاء مساعد التدوين والمراجعة قبل التوقيع
- درجة الضرر والملاحظة المصححة
- ورقة المريض بلغتين

### Day 2: الدليل عند مصدره، والبيانات الصحية

- البحث عن الأدلة: افتح المصدر
- الحداثة والانطباق والخلاف ودرجة اليقين
- البيانات الصحية والأدوات المعتمدة
- إزالة المعرِّفات وحدودها

### Day 3: بطاقة إعادة التصميم والمراجعة المباشرة


## Topics

### Limits of AI in clinical work

- Where decision support becomes a medical device
- Automation bias and deskilling

### Documentation and communication

- Scribe errors and review before signing
- Consent for recording
- Arabic register and reading level

### Evidence lookup

- Guidelines, trials and reviews
- Currency, applicability and disagreement

### Health data protection

- Health data as sensitive data
- De-identification limits
- Approved tools and retention

---

- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants use AI on commercial work for one synthetic home-appliance retailer, with a customer extract, 2,000 Arabic and English reviews and a campaign brief, keeping figures in code, every claim substantiated and every contact consented. Producing synthetic media is USE-FLU-206.

- Analyse customer feedback with an assistant into counted themes, validated against a hand-coded sample.

- Claim types and substantiation
- Bilingual brand voice
- Labels and likeness rights for synthetic images

- Minimising customer data in prompts

- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days of labs on one synthetic case, plus a tracked baseline
- Total hours: 12 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Engineers and technicians use AI on the documents of one synthetic pumping station, from manuals, procedures and logs to inspection photos and a piping and instrumentation diagram, checking every output before it reaches equipment. Sector strategy is USE-SEC-209.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Identify field tasks where AI output must never drive action, and the check each needs.
- Use a source-grounded assistant to update a procedure, checking each step, value and unit against the current revision.
- Analyse free-text maintenance logs with AI-assisted coding and computed counts for recurring faults.
- Test a multimodal assistant's reading of inspection photos, gauges and drawings against known values.
- Redesign one field documentation task, such as voice notes to a report, and measure it on two runs.

- Works in engineering, maintenance or operations and reads procedures and drawings

### Safety and data limits

- Drafting support versus control actions
- Permit to work and management of change
- Sensitive drawings and photos; local models

### Manuals, procedures and logs

- Grounded answers and revision control
- Units, tolerances and bilingual terms
- Fault counts from code

### Images and drawings

- Gauges, small text and symbols
- Voice notes to structured reports

# USE-PRO-212 · AI for Security and IT Operations Staff

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [Fluency for Professions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-PRO.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days of labs on one synthetic case, plus a tracked baseline
- Total hours: 12 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Operations and security staff use AI on one synthetic company network with logs, tickets and runbooks: triaging redacted alerts, catching injected instructions, testing runbooks and generated scripts, and checking AI-made phishing and voice clones. Building AI-assisted detection is DEV-SEC-305.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Use an assistant to triage redacted alerts and verify each verdict against the raw events.
- Draft a runbook from a closed incident and test each step in a disposable environment.
- Test AI-generated administration scripts by reading, static analysis and dry run.
- Analyse suspicious messages and calls for AI-made phishing and cloning, then verify and report them.
- Redesign one recurring operations task with AI and measure time and errors on two runs.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-FLU-201 · Working with AI Assistants: Delegate, Describe, Judge, Own](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-201.md)
- Works in IT support, administration or monitoring and runs shell commands

## Topics

### AI in the operations workflow

- Confident wrong verdicts and invented flags
- Accountability for every change

### Triage and injection

- Redacting secrets, or local models instead
- Evidence lines over verdicts
- Instructions hidden in logs and tickets

### Runbooks and scripts

- Testing in a disposable environment
- Read before run: lint and dry run

### Social engineering with AI

- AI-written phishing
- Voice and video clones
- Out-of-band verification and reporting

# USE-SEC-201 · AI in Health Systems

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [AI in Sectors](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-SEC.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days of labs, tracked pre-work and a defended map
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Managers and clinical leads who choose and supervise health AI work on a fictional regional network with synthetic and public data. They compute what a triage alert means at local prevalence, trace a risk score to its label, check generated notes against transcripts and classify products under medical-device rules, ending with a defended opportunity-and-risk map. Individual clinical use is USE-PRO-209.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish AI products regulated as medical devices from administrative tools and explain what each requires.
- Compute predictive value, alert volume and missed cases for an imaging-triage tool at local prevalence.
- Analyse a population-health risk score for label choice and error by patient subgroup.
- Prepare a local validation and silent-trial plan for an ambient documentation tool.
- Build an opportunity-and-risk map ranking health use cases by value, data readiness and risk tier.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-FLU-103 · How AI Systems Learn and Where They Fail](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-103.md)
- Works in or advises a health organisation

## Topics

### Uses

- Ambient documentation
- Imaging triage
- Population health risk scores

### Clinical evidence

- Predictive value at local prevalence
- External validation across sites
- Silent trials, alert fatigue, monitoring

### Data and rules

- Health data as sensitive data
- Coded data and interoperability standards
- De-identification limits
- Software as a medical device and change control
- Clinical accountability

# USE-SEC-202 · AI in Energy and Petrochemicals

- Track: Data & AI Fluency
- Path: [AI in Sectors](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/USE-SEC.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days of labs, tracked pre-work and a defended map
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Managers and engineers who decide where AI is safe and worth using work on a fictional integrated energy company with public and synthetic data. They test a load forecast against baselines, price maintenance and fault-detection false alarms and draft the AI part of a safety case, ending with a defended opportunity-and-risk map.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Identify each energy AI application as advisory, supervisory or closed-loop and the evidence it needs.
- Test a learned load forecast against seasonal-naive and persistence baselines.
- Measure lead time, missed events and false alarms of maintenance and fault-detection models and price them.
- Draft the AI part of a safety case covering hazards, operating envelope, override and fallback.
- Build an opportunity-and-risk map ranking energy use cases by value, data readiness, control level and risk tier.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-FLU-103 · How AI Systems Learn and Where They Fail](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-103.md)
- Works in or advises an energy operation

## Topics

### Uses

- Seismic and reservoir modelling
- Soft sensors and process optimisation
- Load and renewable forecasting
- Predictive maintenance and fault detection

### Methods and data

- Naive baselines
- Physics-informed and hybrid models
- Rare failures and scarce labels
- Historian data quality

### Safety

- Advisory to closed-loop control
- Safety cases (depth in DEV-PHY-401)
- Operational technology cybersecurity
- Energy use of AI itself

- Distinguish legal AI uses that assist a lawyer from those that inform decisions about people.

- Level: Level 200 · Apply

- Status: In development

## Description

Broadcast, publishing, studio and platform managers test dubbing, generation and moderation tools on Arabic and English material, check assets for consent, rights and provenance and build an opportunity-and-risk map for a synthetic media group. Individual editorial work is USE-PRO-205.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain which rights, consents and labels each AI use in the media value chain needs.
- Measure a machine dubbing and subtitling workflow for meaning, timing, names and dialect.
- Test whether assets carry provenance data that survives common edits.
- Set a moderation threshold per dialect by weighing harm missed against lawful speech removed.
- Build an opportunity-and-risk map ranking media AI uses by value, quality risk, rights exposure and audience trust.

## Prerequisites

- [USE-FLU-201 · Working with AI Assistants: Delegate, Describe, Judge, Own](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/USE-FLU-201.md)
- Knows how content is commissioned, licensed and distributed; uses a spreadsheet

## Topics

### Uses

- Script and asset generation
- Dubbing, voice cloning and subtitling
- Archive tagging and search
- Moderation and recommendation

### Arabic content

- Standard Arabic and dialects
- Names, numbers and diacritics
- Right-to-left subtitles

### Rights and provenance

- Copyright in training data and outputs
- Voice and likeness consent
- Content credentials versus watermarks
- Synthetic-media labelling duties

### Moderation and mapping

- Over-removal and appeals
- Cost per finished minute
- Pilot, scale or stop criteria

- Inspector disagreement

### Reading results

- Miss versus false-reject rates
- Operating points set by cost

# LDS-EXE-101 · AI for Executives: A Hands-On Briefing

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Executive Leadership](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-EXE.md)
- Level: Level 100 · Explain
- Format: Primer: half a day, hands-on, with a scenario test
- Total hours: 4 h
- Audience: leadership
- Status: In development

## Description

Executives do one task from their own work with and without an assistant and check it claim by claim, watch an agent attempt two similar multi-step jobs and note where it fails, and leave with questions for any team proposing AI.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Describe where assistants and agents succeed and fail on similar tasks.
- Compare assisted and unassisted results on one task, checking facts, figures and sources.
- Prepare questions on task, evidence, data, cost, oversight and owner for an AI proposal.

## Prerequisites

- None; tracked pre-work: pick and classify one non-confidential task from own work

## Topics

### What current systems do

- Assistants, reasoning models, agents
- Uneven capability; partial credit is not finished work

### Reading the claims

- Benchmark and adoption denominators
- Self-reported versus measured productivity

### Questions for a team

- Evidence on own cases; cost per completed task
- Which data may enter which tool; who owns and stops it
- Use AI only where someone can challenge it

---

# LDS-EXE-201 · AI Strategy and Use-Case Portfolio

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Executive Leadership](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-EXE.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 24 h
- Audience: leadership
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants build an AI strategy and use-case portfolio for a fictional organisation from synthetic strategy, process and financial records. They score its maturity, triage use cases by ambiguity and risk, prototype two candidates on hosted models to test feasibility, choose build, buy or partner, and trace expected value to the accounts. The capstone is a portfolio and two business cases defended before a mock investment committee.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Analyse an organisation's AI maturity across strategy, governance, data, infrastructure, people, applications and impact.
- Classify use cases by ambiguity and risk and assign each a mode: automate, manage with guardrails, enable exploration or keep human-led.
- Test feasibility claims by prototyping two use cases on a hosted model against ten realistic cases each.
- Compare build, buy and partner options on capability fit, total cost of ownership, data control, lock-in and time to value.
- Build a portfolio sequenced by horizon, with funding gates and value traced to income-statement lines.

## Prerequisites

- Has used AI assistants on own work and checked their output (LDS-EXE-101 or equivalent)
- Reads an income statement and a departmental budget

## Next courses

- [LDS-EXE-301 · AI in Public Policy and Public Service Delivery](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-EXE-301.md)
- [LDS-EXE-401 · Leading the Enterprise AI Office](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-EXE-401.md)

## Topics

### Where value comes from

- Redesigned work and decisions, not deployed tools
- Measuring value, not adoption
- Reading surveys: samples, sponsors, definitions (figures in a dated annex)

### Maturity and readiness

- Maturity dimensions scored from evidence
- Data readiness as the usual constraint
- Advisory maturity assessment is LDS-ADV-202

### Triaging use cases

- Sources: pain points, decisions, documents, contacts
- Ambiguity-by-risk triage and its four modes
- Where agents work: an environment, full context, verifiable results
- Risk level and a named owner as filters

### Build, buy or partner

- Capability fit and proof of concept
- Total cost of ownership, lock-in and exit (procurement is LDS-EXE-205)

### Portfolio and business cases

- Baselines, value hypotheses and tracing to revenue, cost and risk lines
- Horizons, funding gates and stop criteria
- Presenting the strategy to a board

---

# LDS-EXE-202 · Economics of AI and Agents

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Executive Leadership](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-EXE.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: one and a half days with labs and a tracked follow-up
- Total hours: 12 h
- Audience: leadership
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants cost AI the way it is billed and used. From 50 labelled runs of a hosted agent workflow they compute cost per successful task as a distribution, price it under token, capacity and per-outcome schemes, measure which levers change cost and quality, and write a cost governance plan.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain why billed tokens exceed user input and why price per token misstates workflow cost.
- Compute cost per successful task, including retries, failed runs and human review time.
- Compare token, capacity and per-seat or per-outcome pricing for one workflow at three volumes.
- Measure how routing, caching, shorter context and fewer retries change cost and success rate.
- Design a cost governance plan with unit-cost indicators, budgets, alerts and decision rights.

## Prerequisites

- Builds spreadsheet models with formulas and scenarios
- Has seen an agent complete a multi-step task (LDS-EXE-101 or equivalent)

## Topics

### How AI is priced

- Input, output, cached and reasoning tokens
- Capacity and utilisation
- Seats, credits, outcomes, commitments (prices in a dated annex)

### Unit economics

- Cost per successful outcome: median and tail
- Hidden costs: review, integration, evaluation, monitoring
- Build versus run budgets

### Why agents cost more

- Loops, tool calls, growing history, retries
- Falling unit prices, rising spend

### Levers and governance

- Routing, smaller models, caching, batching
- Spend limits on runaway runs
- Governance stages; unit costs in leadership reports

---

# LDS-EXE-203 · Redesigning Work for Human and Agent Teams

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Executive Leadership](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-EXE.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days with labs and a tracked follow-up
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: leadership
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants redesign one process of a fictional organisation for people and agents: they split it into tasks, decide what to automate, augment or keep human, design hand-offs and escalation, and test the design with a hosted agent on synthetic cases. They then plan agent review, three-year role changes and how expertise survives when entry-level tasks move to agents.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Analyse a process into tasks and assign each to a person, an agent or both.
- Test an agent on part of the redesign and revise for observed failures.
- Draft an agent onboarding and review plan covering scope, permissions, supervision, measures and retirement.
- Prepare a three-year scenario for roles, skills, hiring and redeployment.
- Design a plan that protects expertise and the entry-level pipeline through apprenticeship tasks and practice without AI.

## Prerequisites

- Has used AI assistants and checked their output (LDS-EXE-101 or equivalent)
- Manages or advises on a team or process

## Topics

### Tasks, not jobs

- Automate, augment or keep human
- Verifiability, reversibility, judgement
- Measured versus perceived productivity

### Hand-offs and oversight

- What passes and who accepts it
- Risk-tiered approvals people read
- Escalation and stopping

### Agents as team members

- Scope, least privilege, onboarding
- Review on quality, cost, incidents; a named owner

### Workforce and expertise

- Role scenarios and staff consultation
- Deskilling and the entry-level pipeline
- Expertise to challenge AI output

---

# LDS-EXE-204 · Leading AI Adoption and Change

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Executive Leadership](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-EXE.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: one and a half days with labs and a tracked 30-day follow-up
- Total hours: 12 h
- Audience: leadership
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants design an AI adoption programme for a fictional organisation whose staff use AI unevenly and mostly without guidance. From synthetic usage, survey and help-desk data they find shallow, unsafe or blocked use, then write role-based literacy outcomes, a manager kit, incentives that reward value rather than activity, a champions plan, an adoption dashboard and a 90-day plan.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Analyse adoption data to find shallow, unsafe or blocked use and its barrier.
- Draft role-based literacy outcomes, each with a check, for what staff must do with AI.
- Prepare a manager support kit and incentives that reward measured value and safe use.
- Configure a dashboard reporting use, skill and value separately, each defined.
- Design a 90-day adoption plan with champions, a community of practice, measures and decision points.

## Prerequisites

- Has used AI assistants on own work (LDS-EXE-101 or equivalent)
- Leads a unit, a function or a change programme

## Topics

### Why adoption stalls

- Use is not value
- Unguided and unsanctioned use
- Managers and culture decide

### Literacy by role

- The all-professionals baseline
- Outcomes for staff, managers, specialists
- Checking skill with and without AI

### Managers, rules and incentives

- Manager time, permission and examples
- Data rules people can follow
- Rewarding value and safe use

### Champions and measurement

- Champion networks (training champions is USE-FLU-303)
- Baselines and comparison groups
- Scale, fix or stop

---

# LDS-EXE-205 · Buying AI: Procurement, Evaluation and Contracts

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Executive Leadership](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-EXE.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 24 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants run an AI procurement for a fictional organisation from problem statement to agreed terms. They write requirements from the problem rather than the product, build a fixed test set of the buyer's own synthetic cases and test two hosted models on it, draft terms on data use, change notice, rollback, audit, price and exit, and negotiate them in a timed simulation against instructors playing the vendor. The capstone is a solicitation pack and evaluation report.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare requirements and weighted criteria from the business problem, covering quality thresholds, data handling, oversight and exit.
- Test two hosted models or services on a fixed set of the buyer's cases, prepared before vendors are seen.
- Draft terms for data use, no training on buyer data, portability, change notice, rollback, audit, price, fourth parties and exit.
- Decide a negotiation position and defend it in a timed simulation with a vendor team.
- Deliver a solicitation pack and award recommendation that a tender committee could approve.

## Prerequisites

- Has taken part in a procurement as requester, evaluator or approver
- Has used AI assistants and checked their output (LDS-EXE-101 or equivalent)

## Topics

### AI procurement as a process

- Stages: problem, solicitation, evaluation, negotiation, monitoring, exit
- A cross-functional buying team
- Public rules: life-cycle cost, quality and risk; local content

### Requirements and evaluation

- Requirements from the problem, not the product
- Test sets the buyer holds and the vendor never sees
- Testing a service without access to its code or weights
- Scoring responses and assurance evidence

### Contract terms

- Data rights, no training on buyer data, residency
- Model-change notice, version pinning, rollback
- Service levels, audit and independent testing rights
- Fourth parties, portability, exit and sunset

### Price, negotiation and monitoring

- Total cost over the contract life (economics is LDS-EXE-202)
- Positions, walk-away points and trade-offs
- Re-testing when the vendor ships a new model (licences and supply chain are LDS-AIG-203)

---

# LDS-EXE-206 · Governing AI in the Organisation: Boards and Executives

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Executive Leadership](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-EXE.md)

- Escalation and disclosure
- National rules first, foreign regimes for exporters

# LDS-EXE-207 · Scaling AI from Pilots to Production

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Executive Leadership](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-EXE.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: one and a half days with labs and a tracked follow-up
- Total hours: 12 h
- Audience: leadership
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants find why a fictional organisation's AI pilots stalled and plan how the best two reach production: they re-test one on realistic cases, score data readiness, choose an operating model, set scaling gates and redesign the process around one pilot so its value does not rest on workarounds.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Identify why pilots stall: problem choice, data, integration, evaluation, ownership or unchanged processes.
- Test a pilot's claimed performance on realistic cases against its demonstration.
- Analyse two pilots' data readiness for access, quality, classification, lineage and refresh.
- Compare central, federated and hub-and-spoke operating models for size, skills and risk.
- Design scaling gates on evaluation results, governance approval, cost per successful task and process redesign.

## Prerequisites

- Has sponsored, managed or reviewed an AI pilot
- Has used and checked AI assistants (LDS-EXE-101 or equivalent)

## Topics

### Why pilots stall

- No path to production
- Demonstration versus realistic cases
- Ownership and funding after the pilot

### Readiness

- Data access, quality, classification, lineage
- Integration with systems of record
- Agent identity; run cost at volume

### Operating model

- Central, federated, hub-and-spoke
- One owner for the path to production
- Hand-over to operations (delivery is LDS-PRD-204)

### Gates and redesign

- Evaluation thresholds on realistic sets
- Approval by risk level; monitoring, rollback
- Redesign the process, not add a tool
- Scale, fix or stop against a baseline

---

# LDS-EXE-208 · Sovereignty, Infrastructure and Dependency Decisions

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Executive Leadership](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-EXE.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: one day, three labs and a defended memo
- Total hours: 8 h
- Audience: leadership
- Status: In development

## Description

Leaders decide where their organisation's AI runs, whose models it relies on and what happens if access is lost. Participants place synthetic workloads by data class, compare a hosted closed model with a local open-weight model on one bilingual task set, rehearse losing their main provider, and defend a sourcing memo. Contracts are in LDS-EXE-205; architecture in DEV-INF-405.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Classify workloads by data class and personal data, assigning each a permitted model type and placement.
- Compare a hosted closed model with a local open-weight model on quality, latency, cost and data path.
- Analyse withdrawal risk from export restrictions, model retirement, price change, outage and compute or energy limits.
- Decide a sourcing and hosting position for three workloads with exit triggers and a tested fallback.

## Prerequisites

- Places a described dataset in a data classification scheme
- Has used AI assistants and checked their output (LDS-EXE-101 or equivalent)

## Topics

### Sovereignty as control

- Control of data, operations, models and jurisdiction
- Domestic hosting does not mean control of the model

### Models and hosting

- Closed, open-weight and open-source models
- Public API, in-country region, government cloud, on-premises
- Placement by classification and transfer rules
- Self-hosting versus API cost by volume

### Dependency, compute and energy

- Export controls, retirement and price change
- Portability, routing and exit drills
- Accelerator supply, energy and site outages

# LDS-EXE-209 · AI Incident Simulation for Leadership Teams

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Executive Leadership](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-EXE.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Simulation: one facilitated day with a briefing, a four-phase tabletop with timed injects and a structured debrief
- Total hours: 6 h
- Audience: leadership
- Status: In development

## Description

Leadership teams rehearse an AI incident before they face one. In a sandbox, participants first read the traces of a fictional public-service entity's assistant and procurement agent to see how the facts of a failure are found. They then run a timed four-phase tabletop: a harmful Arabic answer spreads on social media; a prompt injection in a supplier email makes the agent send personal data outside the entity; the data protection authority writes; the press and the board demand answers. Teams keep a decision log and each participant writes an after-action memo. Board escalation basics are in LDS-EXE-206; operational incident handling is LDS-AIG-305.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Describe incident roles, decision rights and escalation thresholds, from technical lead to accountable executive.
- Use agent traces and logs to establish what happened, what data moved and what is still unknown.
- Classify each incident by severity and identify the notifications it triggers under data protection law, sector rules and contracts.
- Decide containment, disclosure and recovery actions under time pressure, such as pausing the agent or rolling back a model version.
- Prepare an after-action memo with control changes, owners and dates.

## Prerequisites

- Reads a one-page incident summary and a likelihood and impact matrix
- Has read the sample incident procedure sent as pre-work

## Topics

### How AI incidents differ

- Harmful or false output at scale
- Agents that act: tool misuse after prompt injection
- Evidence in prompts, traces and tool calls
- Vendor models and shared responsibility

### Roles and thresholds

- Incident roles and decision rights
- Severity matrix and escalation
- Using the AI inventory and risk register at the start

### Decisions under pressure

- Containment options and their costs: pause, roll back, switch off a tool
- Preserving evidence
- Notifying with incomplete facts
- Holding statements for the public, staff, regulator and board

### After the exercise

- After-action review
- Control, inventory and risk-register changes
- Re-testing before restart

---

# LDS-EXE-210 · AI Regulation Update: National and Global Briefing

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Executive Leadership](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-EXE.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Primer: half-day briefing, reissued every six months
- Total hours: 4 h
- Audience: leadership
- Status: In development

## Description

A dated briefing on what changed in AI regulation since the last edition, national instruments first, then the foreign regimes that matter to exporters. Participants verify an AI summary of a new instrument against its text and write a one-page applicability note. Detailed mapping is LDS-AIG-202.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Identify each change in national and main foreign instruments as binding, advisory or draft.
- Analyse an AI summary of a new instrument and verify each claim against the primary text.
- Prepare an applicability note listing obligations, owners and dates.

## Prerequisites

- Lists the unit's AI systems and the markets it serves

## Topics

### National instruments first

- Data protection enforcement and cybersecurity controls
- Advisory frameworks and drafts

### Foreign regimes for exporters

- European Union AI Act and its moved dates
- United States, Chinese and treaty instruments

### Acting on change

- Now, next and watch
- Owners and review dates

---

# LDS-EXE-301 · AI in Public Policy and Public Service Delivery

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Executive Leadership](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-EXE.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 25 h
- Audience: leadership
- Status: In development

## Description

Senior public servants practise choosing the instruments a government uses to shape AI and making the case for AI in a public service on public-value terms. Participants appraise options for one policy problem, from guidance and standards to procurement, funding, sandboxes and shared compute; build a public-value case for a citizen-facing assistant; test it on a fixed Arabic and English case set with hosted models; and assemble the accountability pack the public is owed. Sector use cases are in USE-SEC-203 and contract terms in LDS-EXE-205.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Analyse regulation, guidance, standards, procurement, funding, sandboxes, data sharing and shared compute as policy instruments by reach, cost and speed.
- Analyse the public value, costs, risks and effects by user group of an AI-enabled public service.
- Test a citizen-facing assistant for accuracy, refusals, escalation and equal treatment across languages.
- Design the accountability arrangements for a public AI system: inventory entry, transparency record, impact assessment, human review and appeal.
- Evaluate a ministry's AI competence needs and set a role-based development plan.
- Defend a policy brief and public-value case before a mock ministerial committee.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-EXE-201 · AI Strategy and Use-Case Portfolio](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-EXE-201.md)
- Has drafted or reviewed a policy paper or public-service business case
- Reads a cost-benefit table

## Topics

### The state's roles in AI

- Regulator, funder, buyer, operator and data steward
- Instruments and their trade-offs: sandboxes, standards, shared compute
- Life-cycle cost, local content and independent testing in public procurement

### Public value

- Public value versus private return
- Cost-benefit with distributional effects
- Service outcomes, not adoption
- When a public decision should not be automated

### Accountability to the public

- Use-case inventories and transparency records
- Impact assessment and independent review
- Human review, contestability and redress
- Equal service in Arabic and English

### Civil-service capability

- Accountable AI officers in government
- Role-based competence and training duties
- Evaluating capability programmes

# LDS-EXE-302 · Assessing and Certifying Skills in the AI Era

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Executive Leadership](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-EXE.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Workshop: one day, three labs and a pre-task
- Total hours: 8 h
- Audience: leadership
- Status: In development

## Description

Learning and talent leaders decide which assessments can still certify skill when every candidate has an AI assistant. Participants watch a hosted model attempt a synthetic version of their own unsupervised test, redesign it into a supervised lane and an open, defended lane, map credentials to what each can honestly claim, and plan how to measure a programme's effect. Classroom assessment is USE-EDU-201.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Test how much of an existing assessment a hosted model can pass without the candidate's own skill.
- Design a two-lane assessment with a supervised check and an open task backed by process evidence and a defence.
- Classify credentials by what they evidence, how they are verified and what they may claim.
- Design an evaluation of a programme's effect on job performance with a comparison group.

## Prerequisites

- Has designed, commissioned or run a training or assessment programme
- Reads a pass-rate table and says what a gap between two groups shows

## Topics

### What AI changed

- AI-written answers in unsupervised exams
- Why detectors fail and whom they harm
- Unguided AI practice and later unaided skill

### Secure where you certify, open where you teach

- Supervised checks, practical exams and oral defences
- Process evidence and AI rules per activity

### Credentials and claims

- Completion, assessed, stacked and proctored credentials
- Verifiable badges with skills alignment and evidence
- AI in marking and proctoring: disclosure and human review
- Cut scores and reliability near the pass mark

### Evaluating training effect

- Levels from reaction to results and return
- Comparison groups and selection effects

---

# LDS-EXE-401 · Leading the Enterprise AI Office

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Executive Leadership](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-EXE.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Extended: 10-week part-time cohort with weekly labs, two simulation days and a panel defence
- Total hours: 60 h
- Audience: leadership
- Status: In development

## Description

A cohort programme for the officer who runs, or will run, an organisation's AI office. Each week participants write one section of an office plan for their organisation or a fictional entity, from roadmap and mandate to agent governance, literacy, incidents and the board. Labs keep leaders hands-on: they build and measure a small agent workflow and sit on portfolio and incident simulations.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Design a three-horizon AI roadmap with budgets to build, run and retire, sequenced from a maturity profile.
- Design the AI office's mandate, operating model and decision rights alongside data, technology, security and risk functions.
- Build an AI portfolio with stage gates, kill criteria and value traced to the accounts by cost per successful outcome.
- Design governance for generative AI and agents: approved tools, data rules, agent permissions, evaluation ownership and coding agents.
- Evaluate an agent workflow by building it on a hosted model and measuring success rate, cost and failure modes.
- Lead the leadership team's response to an AI incident and a regulator inquiry.
- Defend an AI office plan covering roadmap, portfolio, governance, people and budget.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-EXE-201 · AI Strategy and Use-Case Portfolio](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-EXE-201.md)
- [LDS-EXE-206 · Governing AI in the Organisation: Boards and Executives](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-EXE-206.md)
- LDS-AIG-201 may replace LDS-EXE-206
- Has prepared and defended a budget for a function or programme

## Topics

### Mandate and operating model

- Reporting line and links to data, technology, security and risk
- Central, hub-and-spoke and federated models
- Decision rights by ambiguity and risk

### Strategy and portfolio

- Roadmaps by horizon on a national adoption framework
- Stage gates, kill criteria and value tracing
- Build, buy or partner; budgets to build, run and retire

### Generative AI and agent governance

- Approved tools and data rules
- Agent permissions and human approval
- Evaluation suites owned by the business
- Coding agents and staff-built tools
- Supplier and model-version review after each release

### People, incidents and the board

- Role-based literacy and protecting expertise
- Incident oversight and model risk review
- Regulator engagement and board reporting

# LDS-EXE-402 · Leading the Enterprise Data Office

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Executive Leadership](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-EXE.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Extended: 10-week part-time cohort with weekly labs, a committee simulation and a panel defence
- Total hours: 60 h
- Audience: leadership
- Status: In development

## Description

A cohort programme for the officer who runs, or will run, an organisation's data office. Week by week, participants write a data office plan: strategy and indicators, governance operating model, maturity and compliance, data readiness for AI, and value. Labs include an AI-readiness review of datasets for a retrieval assistant, a committee simulation on sharing requests and generative AI tool approvals, and a data product value case. Specialist depth is in LDS-DMG-201, LDS-DMG-207 and LDS-DMG-301.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Design a data strategy with targets and indicators traced to business objectives and national data indicators.
- Design the governance operating model: office, committee, owners, stewards, decision rights and escalation.
- Analyse data management maturity and compliance against national specifications.
- Evaluate whether datasets are ready for training, retrieval or agent access by classification, personal data, quality, lineage and permissions.
- Decide data sharing requests and generative AI tool approvals as chair of a data committee.
- Prepare a value case for a data product with break-even and sensitivity analysis.
- Defend a data office plan covering strategy, operating model, compliance, AI readiness, value and budget.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-DMG-101 · Data Management Foundations](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-DMG-101.md)
- Has prepared and defended a budget for a function or programme
- Reads a data governance policy and names the owner, control and evidence for each requirement

## Topics

### Strategy and operating model

- Indicator trees tied to business and national objectives
- Office, committee, officers and stewards required by national controls

### Maturity and compliance

- Maturity models and national data index assessments
- Evidence packs and internal audit
- Personal data, classification, sharing and open data duties

### Data readiness for AI

- What may be used for training, retrieval and agents
- Quality, lineage and permission-aware access
- Approving generative AI tools against privacy and sharing terms

### Value and running the function

- Improve, wrap and sell: three routes to value
- Budget, team, board reporting and change

# LDS-PRD-201 · AI Product Discovery and Specification

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [AI Product and Delivery](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-PRD.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 24 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants take a fictional permits service from a vague request to add AI to a specification engineers can build and test against. They mine synthetic interviews and 500 synthetic tickets, choose a problem by frequency, value and cost of error, test feasibility with a prompt-level prototype on 30 cases, and write behaviour rules, pass or fail acceptance criteria, a first evaluation set and a data-needs statement.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish problems suited to generative models, predictive models, rules or no automation.
- Analyse research material into jobs, pain points and workarounds ranked by frequency and cost of error.
- Test a candidate feature with a prompt-level prototype on representative cases.
- Draft a behaviour specification with scope, refusal and escalation rules and pass or fail acceptance criteria.
- Prepare a first evaluation set covering normal, edge and must-refuse cases.
- Defend a specification pack and its statement of data sources, access, classification and gaps.

## Prerequisites

- Has written user stories or requirements for a digital product or service
- Can say in plain words why a language model's output can be fluent and wrong

## Next courses

- [LDS-PRD-202 · Evaluation, Experiments and Economics for AI Products](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-PRD-202.md)
- [LDS-PRD-301 · Responsible AI by Design for Product Teams](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-PRD-301.md)

## Topics

### Framing AI product problems

- Outcome before feature
- A value metric and its baseline before build
- What models do well: draft, extract, classify, rank, act
- When rules or no automation win
- Cost of a wrong answer

### Discovery with users

- Interviews and observation
- Mining tickets, searches and logs
- Synthesis with and without AI

### Feasibility with a prototype

- Prompt-level prototypes
- Representative cases versus demonstrations
- Surfacing uneven capability
- Build approach: prompting, retrieval, adaptation or buying

### Evaluation criteria as the specification

- Behaviour rules, refusals and escalation
- Acceptance criteria as binary checks
- Defining success early versus writing checks for observed errors

### Data needs

- Data for grounding, evaluation and adaptation
- Classification and personal data in sources
- Access owners and lead times

---

# LDS-PRD-202 · Evaluation, Experiments and Economics for AI Products

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [AI Product and Delivery](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-PRD.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 24 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants own the evidence for an AI assistant in pilot. With 300 synthetic traces, a 20,000-session experiment log and three price sheets, they code failure modes, turn them into a versioned evaluation set with graders and thresholds, plan and read an online experiment, and model cost per successful task against quality and latency, ending in a defended launch recommendation. DEV-EVL-301 builds the harness; this course trains its owner.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain why variable outputs need repeated trials, binary criteria and validated graders.
- Analyse traces into a failure taxonomy with frequency and severity.
- Prepare a versioned evaluation set that assigns a code check, model grader or human review and a release threshold to each criterion.
- Analyse an online experiment against primary, guardrail and cost metrics planned in advance.
- Compute cost per successful task and latency percentiles for alternative model configurations.
- Decide whether to launch, iterate or stop by weighing quality, cost, latency and risk.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-PRD-201 · AI Product Discovery and Specification](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-PRD-201.md)
- Computes proportions and percentage differences in a spreadsheet
- Reads a chart that shows a confidence interval

## Topics

### Reading traces

- What a trace records
- Open and axial coding with engineers
- Frequency against severity

### Owning the evaluation set

- Code checks, model graders and human review
- Grader agreement with human labels
- Versioning, leakage and refresh from production
- Consistency over repeated trials

### Online experiments

- A/B tests and shadow deployments
- Guardrail and cost metrics
- Minimum effect, sample size and peeking; depth in SPC-EXP-301

### Cost and latency

- Billed tokens versus user input
- Cost per successful task, not per call
- Model tiers, routing and caching as product levers
- Pricing models and cost governance are LDS-EXE-202

### The launch decision

- Cost as a distribution under volume scenarios
- Release criteria and their owners
- Usage, cohort and feedback analysis after launch

---

# LDS-PRD-203 · Human-AI Interaction and Experience Design

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [AI Product and Delivery](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-PRD.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 24 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants design how people work with a bilingual assistant and an appointment-booking agent for a fictional utility. They audit interaction patterns, set expectations from measured capability, show sources and uncertainty, add confirmation and undo for agent actions, design hand-off to a person, and check accessibility and Arabic right-to-left text, ending with a prototype tested with users. Front-end building is DEV-SWE-203.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Describe interaction patterns for assistants and agents and the trust risk each carries.
- Draft onboarding, source display and uncertainty cues that match measured capability.
- Prepare recovery and escalation flows with confirmation and undo graded by how reversible each agent action is.
- Test the prototype against Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) criteria with a screen reader and keyboard only.
- Test Arabic and mixed-direction layouts with numbers, dates, Latin names and code-switched input.
- Evaluate the design in a moderated usability test measuring task success, over-reliance on seeded errors and recovery time.

## Prerequisites

- Has designed, specified or usability-tested a digital interface or service
- Has used an AI assistant and an agent that acts on the user's behalf

## Topics

### Patterns for assistants and agents

- Conversation, inline, draft-and-review, delegated and background work
- When free text is the wrong input
- Autonomy matched to reversibility

### Trust calibration

- Over-reliance and under-use
- Sources, confidence and stated limits
- Disclosing AI involvement
- Memory and data controls users can see
- Approval prompts people click through

### Errors and recovery

- Wrong, refused and slow responses
- Confirm, preview and undo
- Hand-off to a person with context
- Feedback and corrections as evaluation data

### Accessibility and right-to-left design

- Streamed text, live regions and focus order checked against WCAG
- Mirrored layouts and bidirectional text
- Arabic register, dialect and typography

### Testing with people

- Think-aloud sessions
- Seeded errors to measure over-reliance
- Task success and recovery time

---

# LDS-PRD-204 · Managing AI Projects and Delivery Teams

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [AI Product and Delivery](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-PRD.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days with labs and a delivery simulation, plus a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants steer delivery of an AI document-processing service for a fictional ministry whose target accuracy may be unreachable. They plan increments with exit criteria, assign roles, estimate in ranges, keep a risk log, decide gates on evidence and write the operations hand-over, while a simulation injects a model deprecation and a delayed data-sharing approval.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare a plan of time-boxed increments, each with a hypothesis and an exit criterion.
- Prepare range estimates, a responsibility matrix and a risk log covering model, data, vendor and adoption risks.
- Decide go, no-go or pivot at delivery gates from evaluation, cost and risk evidence.
- Draft an operations hand-over covering monitoring, model change, rollback and retirement.

## Prerequisites

- Has planned or coordinated a project or delivery team
- Reads an evaluation summary of pass rates against acceptance criteria

## Topics

### Delivering under uncertainty

- Experiments before commitments
- Evaluation cycles as the unit of progress
- Stopping as a valid result; scaling is LDS-EXE-207

### Teams and estimates

- Roles, vendors and decision rights
- Range estimates and reference classes
- Backlogs that hold evaluation and data work

### Risk and gates

- Risk logs for AI work
- Gates decided on evidence
- Status reports that show uncertainty

### Hand-over to operations

- Service levels and monitoring
- Model change and vendor deprecation
- Rollback and retirement

# LDS-PRD-205 · Prototyping AI Products with Coding Agents

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [AI Product and Delivery](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-PRD.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days with labs, guided pre-work and a five-user test
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Product and design staff direct a coding agent to build a web prototype that calls a hosted model on synthetic data, add acceptance checks, test it with five users, find where agent-built prototypes mislead, and hand engineering what to keep and discard. No-code tools are USE-FLU-205; engineering with agents is DEV-SWE-201.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare a brief and context file stating the question, scope, data, constraints and done criteria.
- Use a coding agent to build a prototype that calls a language model, in small verified steps under version control.
- Test the prototype against acceptance checks and a limits checklist for hard-coded paths, exposed secrets, unvetted dependencies, real data and accessibility.
- Deliver a hand-over that separates validated learning, specification and evaluation cases from code to discard.

## Prerequisites

- Has written a product requirement or user story
- Runs a terminal command by following written steps

## Topics

### What a prototype is for

- Question-driven prototypes and fidelity
- Prototype, pilot and product

### Directing a coding agent

- Briefs and context files
- Small steps, run and check, version control as undo
- Sandboxes, capped keys and synthetic data

### Limits and hand-over

- Happy-path illusions
- Secrets, unvetted packages, accessibility and right-to-left gaps
- Licences of generated assets
- What engineering keeps

# LDS-PRD-301 · Responsible AI by Design for Product Teams

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [AI Product and Delivery](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-PRD.md)

- Format: Workshop: one and a half days with a simulated launch review
- Total hours: 12 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants take a fictional benefits assistant that drafts eligibility decisions for caseworkers to a launch review: ranked harms, tested safeguards with owners, disclosure and appeal, a measured oversight model, and a go, conditional go or no-go decision. - Stakeholders who never use the product
- Failure, misuse, scale and bias harms
- Safeguards as requirements with tests and owners
- Subgroup slices in release criteria

### Disclosure and contestability

- Telling people AI is involved
- Usable explanations and appeal routes

### Oversight and launch review

- Real oversight versus oversight in name only
- Override logs and automation bias
- Conditional launches and rollback triggers

# LDS-ADV-201 · AI Use-Case Feasibility and Business Cases

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Advisory and Value](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-ADV.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 24 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants take one use case of a fictional municipal services agency through a feasibility study: a baseline from synthetic service logs, a data readiness score, and a timeboxed spike in which a retrieval-grounded prototype is measured on 30 labelled Arabic and English questions. They screen risk, compare four options including one without AI, and write a costed business case. Portfolio triage of many use cases is LDS-EXE-201.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare a problem statement with a measured baseline, a value hypothesis and a success threshold.
- Analyse data readiness: coverage, quality, rights of use, classification and personal data.
- Test technical feasibility by adapting a retrieval-grounded prototype and measuring it on labelled questions.
- Classify the use case's risk level and identify the controls and human oversight it needs.
- Build a costed business case comparing four options, including one without AI, with sensitivity analysis.

## Prerequisites

- [DEV-LLM-201 · Building Applications on Language Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-LLM-201.md)
- USE-FLU-302 is accepted in place of DEV-LLM-201 for participants who do not program
- Builds a spreadsheet model with formulas and scenarios

## Topics

### Framing and value

- The decision behind the request
- Baselines from process data
- Value hypotheses and stop criteria

### Data readiness

- Coverage, quality and rights of use
- Classification and personal data
- Permissions that retrieval must respect

### Technical feasibility

- Designing a timeboxed spike
- Small labelled test sets, pass rates and their uncertainty
- Failure types, and when the answer is not AI

### Risk screening

- Risk levels and prohibited uses
- Effects on people and human oversight
- Vendor and cross-border data exposure

### Options and the costed case

- Change the process, buy, build or partner
- Total cost of ownership, including evaluation and human review
- Break-even, sensitivity and the recommendation
- Benefit tracking and review points after launch

# LDS-ADV-202 · Data and AI Maturity Assessment and Roadmaps

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Advisory and Value](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-ADV.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days with labs and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants run a data and AI maturity assessment of a fictional water utility: they plan the evidence, interview two role-played managers, review a document pack and a staff survey, and score each dimension from triangulated evidence. They turn gaps into a roadmap by horizon and present it to a sponsor. Compliance audits against national data specifications are LDS-DMG-207.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare an evidence plan of interview guides, a document request and a survey for a chosen maturity model.
- Analyse interviews, documents and survey results to score each dimension with a confidence rating.
- Design a roadmap that turns gaps into initiatives sequenced by dependency, budget and capacity.
- Prepare and deliver a sponsor readout of findings, roadmap and decisions requested.

## Prerequisites

- Names the main data management knowledge areas (LDS-DMG-101 or equivalent)
- Describes how AI systems learn and fail (USE-FLU-103 or equivalent)

### Maturity models

- Data management knowledge areas and capability models
- AI adoption dimensions from strategy to impact
- Maturity is not compliance

### Evidence

- Interviews, documents, surveys and walkthroughs
- Triangulation, confidence and self-assessment inflation
- Calibration between assessors

### Roadmaps and reporting

- Targets from strategy, not the top of the scale
- Data foundations before AI use
- Readouts that ask for decisions

# LDS-ADV-301 · Data Products, Valuation and Monetisation

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Advisory and Value](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-ADV.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants take a fictional transport authority's synthetic ridership, ticketing and fleet-location data from asset to priced product. They score assets for readiness, analyse demand, design a product, value an asset three ways and set licence terms and prices. They test each proposal's lawfulness, including a re-identification test on a supposedly anonymised extract, and model break-even and sensitivity. The capstone is a business case defended before a mock approvals committee.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Classify data assets by expected value and assess their readiness for productisation.
- Analyse demand, beneficiary segments and substitutes to define use cases for a data product.
- Compute the value of a data asset by cost, market and income approaches and reconcile them.
- Design a product, licence and pricing model that balances cost, value, demand and service level.
- Evaluate product proposals against personal data, classification, sharing and intellectual property conditions and decide approvability.
- Build a business case with forecast, costs, break-even, sensitivity and portfolio indicators, and recommend launch, redesign or stop.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-DMG-101 · Data Management Foundations](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-DMG-101.md)
- Builds a spreadsheet financial model with net present value and scenarios
- States what data classification and sharing rules permit

## Topics

### Data as products

- Improve, wrap and sell
- Datasets, interfaces, analytical products and insight services
- Products rather than raw data

### Readiness and demand

- Asset inventory and readiness criteria
- Beneficiary segments, demand evidence and substitutes
- Partners and delivery channels

### Valuation and pricing

- Cost, market and income approaches
- Non-rival goods with near-zero marginal cost
- Subscription, tiered, usage-based and licence pricing

### Licences and regulatory conditions

- Licence terms, including use for AI training
- Anonymisation limits and re-identification risk
- Classification, sharing rules and intellectual property
- Monetisation governance: roles, approval paths and escalation

### Business case and portfolio

- Forecasts, break-even and sensitivity
- Portfolio indicators: revenue, cost, usage, satisfaction
- Repricing and retirement

---

# LDS-ADV-302 · Advisory Practice for Data and AI Engagements

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Advisory and Value](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-ADV.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Workshop: two days of simulated engagement with role-played clients and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants run a simulated engagement for a fictional department asking whether to build a citizen-facing assistant: they scope the request, facilitate a decision workshop, write an options paper, review an AI-drafted deliverable seeded with errors and resolve conflict-of-interest dilemmas. Feasibility and maturity methods are LDS-ADV-201 and LDS-ADV-202.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Draft an engagement scope with the decision to inform, deliverables, exclusions and acceptance criteria.
- Design and facilitate a decision workshop that brings stakeholders with conflicting aims to a recorded decision.
- Evaluate three options against stated criteria and recommend one in an options paper that states uncertainty.
- Review a deliverable for traceable claims, consistent numbers, real citations and disclosed AI use.
- Apply independence, confidentiality and conflict-of-interest principles to advisory dilemmas.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-ADV-202 · Data and AI Maturity Assessment and Roadmaps](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-ADV-202.md)
- Has written a recommendation for a decision-maker

## Topics

### Scoping and stakeholders

- The decision behind the request
- Exclusions, assumptions and scope change
- Stakeholder maps
- Proposals, work plans and quality checkpoints

### Workshops and options papers

- Diverge, converge, decide
- Facilitating conflict and quieter voices
- Evidence versus judgement

### Quality and conduct

- Verifying AI-drafted analysis and citations
- Disclosing AI use and protecting client data
- Vendor ties, follow-on work and when to decline
