# LDS-AIG-201 · AI Governance Foundations: Principles, Roles and Lifecycle Controls

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [AI Governance, Risk and Assurance](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-AIG.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 24 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants turn responsible AI principles into controls that a team can operate and an auditor can check. Working on one fictional public-sector organisation with 30 AI systems in use or in development, they build an AI inventory, tier each system by risk, assign accountability with a responsibility matrix, design review gates for every lifecycle stage from intake to retirement, and draft an acceptable-use policy with prohibited categories. They finish with a governance starter pack that they defend before a mock governance committee.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain how principles, policies, standards, controls and evidence relate, and where each sits in an AI governance framework.
- Prepare an AI system inventory with the fields needed for ownership, purpose, data, model source, risk tier and lifecycle stage.
- Classify AI systems into four risk levels and record the factors that decided each level.
- Draft a responsibility matrix that assigns who is accountable, responsible, consulted and informed for each governance decision.
- Draft an acceptable-use policy with prohibited and restricted application categories, exception handling and a review date.
- Design lifecycle review gates from intake to retirement, with entry criteria, required evidence and the approving role for each risk level.

## Prerequisites

- Describes in plain words how a machine learning model and a language model assistant are built, tested and put into use
- Reads an organisational policy and identifies who must do what, and when

## Next courses

- [LDS-AIG-202 · AI Regulation and Standards in Practice](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-AIG-202.md)
- [LDS-AIG-203 · Third-Party AI: Licences, Supply Chain and Retirement](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-AIG-203.md)
- [LDS-AIG-204 · AI Risk Management in Practice](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-AIG-204.md)
- [LDS-AIG-302 · Generative AI and Agent Controls Laboratory](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-AIG-302.md)
- [LDS-AIG-303 · AI Impact Assessment and System Documentation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-AIG-303.md)
- [LDS-AIG-304 · AI Management Systems and Internal Audit](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-AIG-304.md)
- [LDS-AIG-305 · AI Incident Response and Compliance Monitoring](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-AIG-305.md)
- [LDS-AIG-306 · Privacy, Intellectual Property and Content Provenance in AI](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-AIG-306.md)
- [LDS-AIG-307 · Human Oversight and Ethics Review Design](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-AIG-307.md)
- [LDS-AIG-401 · Designing and Running an AI Governance Programme](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-AIG-401.md)

## Topics

### From principles to controls

- National AI ethics principles and their four risk levels
- Principles, policies, standards, procedures, controls and evidence
- International frameworks as support: OECD principles, NIST AI Risk Management Framework functions, AI management system structure
- What makes a control operable: owner, trigger, frequency, test

### Accountability and roles

- Developer, provider, deployer and operator responsibilities
- Governance committee, system owner, risk, legal, privacy and security roles
- Responsibility matrices and decision rights
- Escalation paths
- Three lines of defence applied to AI

### The AI inventory

- What counts as an AI system, including features inside purchased software
- Inventory fields and ownership
- Finding undeclared AI use through procurement, expense and network records
- Keeping the inventory current

### Risk tiering

- Four-level categorisation from little or no risk to unacceptable
- Tiering factors: impact on people, autonomy, scale, reversibility, data sensitivity
- Proportionality: what each level triggers

### Lifecycle gates

- Intake and use-case screening
- Design and data approval
- Evaluation and deployment approval
- Monitoring, change and re-approval
- Retirement as a gate (retirement planning in depth is LDS-AIG-203)

### Policy set and documentation

- Acceptable-use policy and prohibited categories
- Staff rules for generative AI tools, coding agents and staff-built automations
- Data classification and residency rules for external model services
- Documentation minimums per risk level (full impact assessment is in LDS-AIG-303)
- Records and retention

### Making governance work

- Governance as a service to delivery teams
- Governance as an enabler in the national AI adoption framework
- Entity-level evidence: national AI ethics badges and accreditation of AI service providers
- Measures: inventory coverage, gate cycle time, open exceptions
- Signs of governance in name only

---

# LDS-AIG-202 · AI Regulation and Standards in Practice

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [AI Governance, Risk and Assurance](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-AIG.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days with labs, guided pre-reading and a tracked post-course mapping task
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants practise reading AI-relevant law, guidance and standards the way a governance specialist must: who is in scope, in which role, for which systems, with what duties and from when. The Kingdom's instruments are the reference case; participants then map the same obligations to international management and risk standards and to the main foreign regimes an exporting organisation meets. The product is an obligations register and a one-page multi-jurisdiction map for a fictional company selling three AI products in three markets. The six-monthly briefing LDS-EXE-210 keeps the map current after the course.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish binding law, implementing regulation, advisory framework, voluntary code and international standard, and state what each requires of an organisation.
- Analyse an instrument to extract scope, roles, risk classes, duties, deadlines and enforcement into a structured obligations register.
- Apply tests of territorial reach, provider or deployer role and risk class to a described AI product.
- Prepare a crosswalk from regulatory duties to clauses of an AI management system standard and a risk management framework.
- Prepare a horizon-scanning log for pending instruments with source, status, expected effect, owner and review date.
- Deliver a one-page multi-jurisdiction map with the controls that close the highest-priority gaps.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-AIG-201 · AI Governance Foundations: Principles, Roles and Lifecycle Controls](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-AIG-201.md)
- Reads a regulatory or policy text in English and extracts who must do what by when

## Topics

### How AI is regulated

- Horizontal AI law, sector rules and data protection law
- Risk-based structure: prohibited, high-risk, transparency and minimal classes
- Binding, advisory and voluntary instruments
- How guidance hardens into obligation

### The Kingdom's instruments as the reference case

- No AI-specific statute: how data, cybersecurity and sector law combine with advisory national AI instruments
- Personal data protection law and its regulations applied to training, retrieval and inference
- Data classification, sharing and secondary-use rules
- National AI ethics principles and risk levels
- National AI risk management framework and its advisory status
- Registration, impact assessment and AI service-provider accreditation through the national data governance platform
- Cybersecurity controls and draft AI cybersecurity guidelines
- Sector regulators for health devices, finance, telecoms and cloud

### Reading an instrument

- Scope and definitions
- Roles: developer, provider, deployer, operator
- Duties, deadlines and penalties
- Guidance, answers to frequent questions and enforcement decisions as interpretation

### International standards and frameworks

- AI management systems (ISO/IEC 42001)
- AI risk management (ISO/IEC 23894) and impact assessment (ISO/IEC 42005)
- NIST AI Risk Management Framework and its generative AI profile
- Harmonised standards and presumption of conformity, starting with the first harmonised AI quality management standard

### Foreign regimes for exporters

- The European Union AI Act, its 2026 amendments and staged application dates
- United States federal policy and state laws on automated decisions
- Chinese rules on generative AI, labelling and anthropomorphic AI
- Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI
- OECD and G20 AI principles

### Crosswalks and the multi-jurisdiction map

- One control, many duties
- Gap analysis and prioritisation
- Presenting obligations on one page

### Keeping current

- Horizon scanning and ownership
- Primary sources over commentary
- Dated annexes and review cycles
- Re-verifying assistant summaries of law against the source

---

# LDS-AIG-203 · Third-Party AI: Licences, Supply Chain and Retirement

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [AI Governance, Risk and Assurance](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-AIG.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: one and a half days with labs and a tracked follow-up review
- Total hours: 12 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants review the parts of AI that their organisation does not build: open-weight and proprietary models, datasets, code, prompts, tool servers and hosted services. They read model and dataset licences and acceptable-use terms, check provenance records and bills of materials, assess a supplier's assurance evidence, set change-notice and exit conditions, and plan the controlled retirement of a model. Labs follow a fictional organisation adopting three external models and one hosted agent service. Contract negotiation is in LDS-EXE-205; pipeline signing is in DEV-SEC-304.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compare permissive, copyleft, restricted open-weight and proprietary terms for models, datasets and code.
- Analyse the provenance of a model and its training data using model cards, dataset cards and a bill of materials, and record unresolved gaps.
- Prepare a supplier assurance review from a standard questionnaire, a management-system certificate and the supplier's evaluation results.
- Draft change-notice, evaluation-on-change and exit clauses for an AI service, and an exit plan with data return and replacement steps.
- Design a retirement plan for an AI model covering rollback, archiving, record retention, user communication, dependency removal and residual risk.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-AIG-201 · AI Governance Foundations: Principles, Roles and Lifecycle Controls](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-AIG-201.md)
- Reads a contract clause or terms of service and identifies the obligations on each party
- Runs provided commands in a terminal or a notebook cell and reads their output

## Topics

### What third-party AI includes

- Foundation models called through an API
- Open-weight models
- Datasets and benchmarks
- Libraries, plugins, tool servers and prompt libraries
- AI features inside purchased software

### Licences and terms

- Permissive and copyleft code licences
- Open-weight model licences with use restrictions and thresholds
- Dataset licences and terms of collection
- Acceptable-use policies of hosted services
- Data use, retention and training on customer data
- Data residency and cross-border transfer for hosted services

### Provenance and integrity

- Model and dataset cards
- Bills of materials for AI and machine learning
- Signatures and hashes
- Mislabelled or poisoned artefacts in public hubs

### Supplier assurance

- Assurance questionnaires and controls matrices
- Reading AI management-system certificates, their scope and the accreditation of the certifying body
- National accreditation of AI service providers and entity ethics badges as supplier evidence
- Supplier evaluation evidence and its independence
- Assurance after signature

### Change and exit

- Silent model updates and deprecation
- Re-evaluation on change
- Portability, data return and lock-in
- Exit plans and how to test them

### Retirement and decommissioning

- Triggers for retirement
- Rollback, archiving and record retention
- Dependency removal and user communication
- Residual-risk sign-off

---

# LDS-AIG-204 · AI Risk Management in Practice

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [AI Governance, Risk and Assurance](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-AIG.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants run the full AI risk cycle on realistic cases: set context and scope, identify risks with structured techniques, score likelihood and impact, choose treatments, sign off residual risk and define the indicators that show when a risk is moving. The national AI risk management framework is the primary method, with crosswalks to international frameworks. The capstone is a complete risk assessment of a fictional government service assistant and an internal procurement agent, presented to a mock risk committee and followed by a tracked monitoring task.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Describe the phases of the national AI risk management cycle and map them to the functions of two international risk frameworks.
- Apply structured identification techniques, including stakeholder harm mapping, misuse cases and failure-mode analysis, to an AI use case.
- Compute likelihood and impact scores on a four-by-four matrix with written justifications, then calibrate them with peers.
- Draft an AI risk appetite and tolerance statement that sets limits per risk category and the escalation route.
- Prepare a treatment plan that selects avoid, reduce, transfer or accept for each priority risk, with control owners, cost and expected residual score.
- Configure key risk indicators and early-warning thresholds with data sources, review frequency and the action each triggers.
- Deliver a complete AI risk assessment and defend the residual-risk recommendation before a risk committee.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-AIG-201 · AI Governance Foundations: Principles, Roles and Lifecycle Controls](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-AIG-201.md)
- Describes the main failure modes of machine learning and language model systems, such as bias, drift, hallucination and prompt injection
- Uses a spreadsheet to compute, sort and filter a scored table

## Next courses

- [LDS-AIG-401 · Designing and Running an AI Governance Programme](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-AIG-401.md)

## Topics

### Risk foundations for AI

- Risk, hazard, harm and uncertainty
- Enterprise risk management and where AI risk fits
- Developer, operator and policymaker roles in the national framework
- Adopting an advisory framework into enterprise policy
- Lessons from model risk management in financial services: inventory, validation, effective challenge
- Risk appetite and tolerance

### Context and scope

- System boundaries and intended use
- Stakeholders and affected people
- Legal and contractual context
- Assumptions and dependencies

### Identifying AI risks

- The seven risk categories of the national framework and their mapping to international taxonomies
- Stakeholder harm mapping
- Misuse and abuse cases
- Failure-mode analysis
- Risks specific to generative systems and agents
- Third-party and supplier risk
- Learning from public incident records

### Assessing and scoring

- Likelihood and impact scales
- Four-by-four matrix and score bands
- Calibration among assessors
- Inherent and residual risk
- Aggregation and its pitfalls

### Treatment

- Treatment options
- Control selection and design
- Human oversight as a control, and its limits
- Cost and proportionality
- Residual-risk acceptance and sign-off

### Monitoring and review

- Key risk indicators and early warning
- Control testing
- Triggers for reassessment: change, incident, drift
- Reporting to committees and boards

### Crosswalks and links

- NIST AI Risk Management Framework and its generative AI profile
- ISO/IEC 23894 risk management guidance
- Hand-offs to impact assessment (LDS-AIG-303) and incident response (LDS-AIG-305)

---

# LDS-AIG-301 · Assessing Models and Systems: Fairness, Robustness and Safety Evidence

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [AI Governance, Risk and Assurance](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-AIG.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants produce and judge the technical evidence that a risk or governance function relies on. In provided notebooks they measure subgroup error rates with uncertainty, test models under distribution shift and input perturbation, measure harmful and ungrounded outputs of a bilingual language model assistant, and audit a supplier's evaluation report for gaps. Data are synthetic credit, hiring and service-assistant cases with planted defects. The capstone is an independent assessment report and model card for one system, defended live. Building evaluation pipelines is DEV-EVL-301; research methods for robustness and fairness are SPC-TRU-304.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain why common group fairness criteria cannot all hold at once and which criterion suits which decision context.
- Compute subgroup performance and fairness metrics with confidence intervals and flag differences that exceed a stated tolerance.
- Test model behaviour under distribution shift and input perturbation, including Arabic and English text variants.
- Measure harmful, ungrounded and policy-violating outputs of a language model assistant with a test set and a calibrated grader.
- Prepare post-deployment checks for drift and subgroup degradation with thresholds, data sources and owners.
- Audit a supplier's evaluation report for contamination, test awareness, missing subgroups, unreported uncertainty and mismatch with intended use.
- Evaluate whether a system's evidence supports deployment at its risk level and recommend approval with conditions, or rejection.

## Prerequisites

- Computes and interprets a confidence interval and a difference between two proportions
- Reads a confusion matrix and computes precision, recall and false positive rate
- Runs, edits and re-runs cells in a provided Python notebook
- Places an AI system on a risk level and states what that level requires (LDS-AIG-201, or LDS-AIG-204 for risk analysts)

## Topics

### Evidence for assurance

- What assurance needs from evaluation
- Intended use, risk level and strength of evidence
- Independence and conflicts of interest
- The gap between test results and deployed behaviour
- Explanation methods as evidence, and their limits

### Fairness measurement

- Group criteria: demographic parity, equalised odds, calibration within groups
- Incompatibility results and choosing a criterion
- Small subgroups and intervals
- Intersectional slices
- Proxies, missing protected attributes and the lawful use of sensitive data for bias testing
- Mitigation options and their side effects

### Reliability under change

- Distribution shift and temporal drift
- Input perturbation, including dialect, spelling and script variation
- Uncertainty and calibration
- Stress and edge cases

### Evaluating generative systems

- Harm categories and test-set design
- Groundedness and hallucination checks
- Model-graded checks calibrated against people
- Red-team results as evidence
- Contamination and test awareness

### Reading evaluation reports

- Model cards and system cards
- Benchmark claims and what they omit
- Vendor and third-party reports
- Requesting the missing evidence

### From results to decisions

- Tolerance thresholds per risk level
- Conditions of approval
- Monitoring requirements
- Writing the assessment report, model card and fairness position statement

---

# LDS-AIG-302 · Generative AI and Agent Controls Laboratory

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [AI Governance, Risk and Assurance](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-AIG.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 24 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

In containerised labs on synthetic targets, participants configure and test the controls that make generative AI and agents governable: input and output guardrails, groundedness checks, sandboxes with egress limits, tool allow-lists and scoped credentials, approval gates, rate limits, a kill-switch and audit logging. They attack a provided staff helpdesk agent with open red-team tools, map findings to public risk lists and a threat knowledge base, harden the agent and assemble a control evidence pack for a risk committee. Cross-listed with DEV-SEC; building these controls into application code is DEV-SEC-301, and full red-team programmes are DEV-SEC-302.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Identify the main risk classes of language model and agent applications and distinguish model-as-component risks from model-as-actor risks.
- Configure input and output guardrails, groundedness checks and content filters, and measure their effect on blocked attacks and false refusals.
- Configure an agent sandbox with tool allow-lists, scoped credentials, egress limits, rate limits, human approval for high-impact actions and a kill-switch.
- Implement audit logging of prompts, retrieved content, tool calls, approvals and policy decisions, with filtering of personal data.
- Design and run a red-team exercise against an agent, with scope, rules of engagement, attack scenarios and severity scoring.
- Evaluate whether the hardened agent's residual risk is acceptable for its risk level and assemble the control evidence pack.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-AIG-201 · AI Governance Foundations: Principles, Roles and Lifecycle Controls](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-AIG-201.md)
- Uses a terminal to run provided commands and edits YAML or JSON configuration files
- Describes how a language model assistant calls tools and retrieves documents
- Scores a risk by likelihood and impact against a stated appetite (LDS-AIG-204 or equivalent)

## Topics

### Threat model for generative systems

- Untrusted input everywhere: direct, indirect and cross-modal prompt injection
- Poisoned retrieval content and agent memory
- Model as component versus model as actor
- Public risk lists for language model and agentic applications
- Threat knowledge bases of adversary tactics and techniques

### Guardrails

- Input and output filters
- Safety classifiers and their error rates
- Groundedness and citation checks
- Structured output validation
- False refusals as a cost

### Agent containment

- Sandboxes and egress control
- Tool allow-lists, agent identity and scoped credentials
- Memory boundaries
- Approval gates for high-impact actions
- Rate limits, budgets and kill-switches

### Tool servers and connectors

- What a tool server can reach
- Reviewing tool descriptions for poisoning
- Least privilege for connectors

### Red teaming

- Scope and rules of engagement
- Manual and automated probing
- Scoring severity and likelihood
- Turning findings into regression tests

### Logging and evidence for audit

- What to log and what not to log
- Trace schemas and retention
- Reconstructing an incident
- Control evidence packs and residual-risk sign-off

---

# LDS-AIG-303 · AI Impact Assessment and System Documentation

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [AI Governance, Risk and Assurance](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-AIG.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Workshop: two days with labs
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

On a fictional hospital referral-prioritisation system, participants scope an impact assessment, rate impacts on each affected group, write a datasheet, model card, system card and plain-language notice, and assemble an evidence file linking every claim to its source. Risk scoring is LDS-AIG-204; test evidence is LDS-AIG-301; the personal data impact assessment is LDS-DMG-206.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish impact, risk, personal data and conformity assessments by their triggers.
- Analyse impacts on each affected group by severity, scale and reversibility, and assign owned mitigations.
- Draft a datasheet and a model card that state data origin, subgroup results and untested conditions.
- Build a system card and a plain-language notice telling affected people how to question a result.
- Review a peer's evidence file and decide whether it supports approval at its risk level.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-AIG-201 · AI Governance Foundations: Principles, Roles and Lifecycle Controls](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-AIG-201.md)
- Reads a model evaluation summary and names what is untested

## Topics

### Assessments and triggers

- Assessment types and triggers
- Light and full assessments by risk level
- The national ethical impact assessment and ISO/IEC 42005

### Impact analysis

- Affected groups, including non-users
- Rights at stake and impact rating
- Consulting front-line staff and affected people

### Documents by reader

- Datasheets and model cards
- System cards
- Notices and explanations for affected people, in Arabic and English

### Evidence files

- Claim-to-source links
- Reassessment on change
- Audit sampling

# LDS-AIG-304 · AI Management Systems and Internal Audit

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [AI Governance, Risk and Assurance](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-AIG.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up audit
- Total hours: 24 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

For a fictional logistics company that builds two AI products and buys three AI services, participants set up an AI management system: scope, AI policy, objectives and a statement of applicability. They then plan and run an internal audit with role-played interviews and record sampling, grade findings and plan corrective action. The course builds implementation and internal audit skill; it does not certify.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain how the clauses of an AI management system standard call on risk and impact assessment standards.
- Prepare the scope, AI policy and measurable objectives of an AI management system.
- Prepare a statement of applicability that justifies each control from the risk assessment.
- Design a risk-based internal audit programme for one cycle and the plan for one audit.
- Audit a function by interview and record sampling, and grade each finding.
- Analyse the root cause of a nonconformity and prepare a corrective action with a success measure.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-AIG-201 · AI Governance Foundations: Principles, Roles and Lifecycle Controls](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-AIG-201.md)
- Describes how a plan-do-check-act management system works, for example for quality or information security
- Reads an AI risk register and its scoring (LDS-AIG-204 or equivalent)

## Topics

### Management-system logic

- Plan, do, check, act
- The clause structure shared with quality and security systems
- What certification does and does not prove

### Scope, policy and controls

- Roles as developer, provider or user
- Scope, exclusions and objectives
- Statement of applicability, linked to LDS-AIG-204 and LDS-AIG-303
- Controls for bought services, agents and staff-built tools

### Internal audit practice

- Risk-based programmes following management-system audit guidance (ISO 19011)
- Interviewing, sampling and objective evidence
- Grading findings
- Auditor independence

### Improvement and external assurance

- Corrective action and management review
- Certification bodies and the rules on them
- The harmonised AI quality management standard
- National provider accreditation and entity ethics badges

# LDS-AIG-305 · AI Incident Response and Compliance Monitoring

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [AI Governance, Risk and Assurance](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-AIG.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Workshop: one and a half days with labs and a follow-up control test
- Total hours: 12 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

On a fictional insurer's claims assistant and document agent, participants triage incident reports, reconstruct an agent data leak from traces, decide who must be notified, lead a blameless review and test controls by sampling. Trace logging design is LDS-AIG-302; leadership rehearsal is LDS-EXE-209; reliability incidents are DEV-OPS-401.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Classify incident reports by type, harm, severity and failed component.
- Analyse traces and change records to reconstruct an incident and the controls that failed.
- Draft the notices a breach requires to the data protection regulator, affected people and a supplier.
- Lead a blameless post-incident review and decide corrective actions.
- Design a compliance monitoring plan of control tests, thresholds and escalation.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-AIG-201 · AI Governance Foundations: Principles, Roles and Lifecycle Controls](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-AIG-201.md)
- Reads a log or trace table and filters it by time and identifier

## Topics

### Incidents and triage

- Incidents, near misses, breaches and non-compliance
- AI-specific types: harmful output, unfair outcome, undisclosed AI use, agent overreach
- Reporting frameworks and incident databases
- Containment: rollback, switch-off, human-only mode

### Investigation and notification

- Evidence preservation and chain of custody
- Reconstruction from traces
- Breach duties and deadlines
- Telling affected people and suppliers

### Learning and monitoring

- Blameless review
- Incidents as test cases
- Control testing by sampling
- Reporting to the committee

# LDS-AIG-306 · Privacy, Intellectual Property and Content Provenance in AI

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [AI Governance, Risk and Assurance](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-AIG.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Workshop: one and a half days with labs and a follow-up review
- Total hours: 12 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

For a fictional publishing group, participants map personal data through a fine-tuning and retrieval pipeline, probe a small fine-tuned model for memorised records, answer a deletion request, decide which training sources may be used, and verify and strip content credentials on generated images. Data access design is LDS-DMG-301; model licences are LDS-AIG-203; privacy-enhancing technologies are DEV-SEC-303.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare a personal data map of a fine-tuning and retrieval pipeline with lawful basis and transfers.
- Test a model for disclosure of planted records, with and without an output filter.
- Analyse a deletion request against weights, index, logs and backups.
- Decide for each training source whether to use, exclude or license it, and set output-use rules.
- Design a provenance and labelling scheme for generated media and test where it fails.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-AIG-201 · AI Governance Foundations: Principles, Roles and Lifecycle Controls](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-AIG-201.md)
- Explains lawful basis and data subject rights (LDS-DMG-206 or equivalent)
- Runs provided notebook cells

## Topics

### Personal data in AI

- Training, retrieval, memory and logs
- Lawful basis and secondary use
- Sensitive data for bias testing
- External model services and transfer

### Leakage and rights

- Memorisation and extraction
- Output filters
- Deletion against weights; unlearning claims

### Intellectual property

- Text and data mining exceptions and rights reservations
- Output ownership and infringement

### Provenance

- Signed content credentials
- Removable watermarks
- Labels and deepfake rules

# LDS-AIG-307 · Human Oversight and Ethics Review Design

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [AI Governance, Risk and Assurance](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-AIG.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Workshop: one and a half days with labs, a mock review board and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 12 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants act as reviewers in a simulated permit queue where an AI system recommends decisions with seeded errors, and measure what they catch. From that evidence they set oversight models and agent approval thresholds, design appeal routes, and run an ethics review procedure as a mock board. Configuring approval gates in software is LDS-AIG-302; product safeguards are LDS-PRD-301.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Measure the effectiveness of a human review step with seeded errors and review time.
- Configure approval thresholds for an agent's actions by impact and reversibility.
- Design a contestability route from notice to human re-decision and redress.
- Design an ethics review procedure with triggers, independent members, criteria and records.
- Decide as a board member whether to approve, approve with conditions or reject a proposed AI use.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-AIG-201 · AI Governance Foundations: Principles, Roles and Lifecycle Controls](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-AIG-201.md)
- Describes where people intervene when an AI system recommends or acts

## Topics

### Oversight models

- In the loop, on the loop, in command
- Authority, competence and time
- Approval gates and stop rights for agents

### Why oversight fails

- Automation bias and workload
- Oversight in name only
- Measuring with seeded errors
- Override and escalation rates as monitoring signals

### Contestability

- Notice and explanation
- Appeal and redress

### Ethics review

- Triggers and membership
- Criteria from national principles
- Dissent and conditions

---

# LDS-AIG-401 · Designing and Running an AI Governance Programme

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [AI Governance, Risk and Assurance](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-AIG.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Studio: eight weeks part-time, coached design with three milestone reviews, a committee simulation and a panel defence
- Total hours: 40 h
- Audience: leadership
- Status: In development

## Description

Each participant designs, and rehearses running, an AI governance programme for their own organisation or a fictional ministry with 60 AI systems, agents in pilot and many staff-built tools. Week by week they diagnose the current state, set the mandate and operating model, build a tiered policy set and review gates with service levels, write committee terms of reference and define metrics, resourcing and training. They chair a simulated committee and defend the programme before a panel. Policy drafting technique is LDS-DMG-302; the wider AI office is LDS-EXE-401.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Analyse an organisation's AI governance against its obligations and a maturity model.
- Design the mandate, operating model and decision rights, choosing central, federated or hub-and-spoke.
- Design a tiered policy set and proportionate review gates with service levels and exceptions.
- Lead a governance committee to decisions on contested cases, recording reasons and dissent.
- Design programme metrics, board reporting and a resourcing plan.
- Defend the programme and its 18-month roadmap before a panel and revise it under challenge.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-AIG-201 · AI Governance Foundations: Principles, Roles and Lifecycle Controls](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-AIG-201.md)
- [LDS-AIG-204 · AI Risk Management in Practice](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-AIG-204.md)
- Has produced at least two artefacts of the kind taught in LDS-AIG-202 to LDS-AIG-307
- Takes a policy through review and approval

## Topics

### Diagnosis and mandate

- Maturity models and evidence
- Obligations and risk appetite
- Charter and links to risk, privacy, security and audit

### Operating models

- Central, federated, hub-and-spoke
- Committee, office, system owners and champions
- Governance as a service

### Policies and gates

- Policy, standard and procedure tiers
- Rules for agents and staff-built tools
- Gates with service levels and exceptions

### Committees

- Terms of reference and quorum
- Decisions, dissent and conflicts of interest
- Escalation to the board

### Measuring and sustaining

- Effectiveness over activity counts
- Capacity and budget
- Training by role and annual review
- Internal audit, certification and entity ethics badges

---

# LDS-DMG-101 · Data Management Foundations

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Data Management and Governance Professions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-DMG.md)
- Level: Level 100 · Explain
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 24 h
- Audience: beginner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants learn the knowledge areas of data management by producing the first artefact of each for a fictional public services agency. From synthetic system extracts and interview notes they build an asset register, write glossary entries, trace one dataset's lineage, run simple quality checks and propose provisional classifications, placing each artefact against the domains of a national standard. They finish with a maturity snapshot and a first-year improvement plan.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Describe the knowledge areas of data management with the main artefact and accountable role for each.
- Distinguish the roles of a governance structure, from the committee to business and technical stewards.
- Prepare a data asset register and business glossary entries for one business domain.
- Apply quality dimensions and provisional classification levels to registered assets.
- Apply a six-level maturity scale to score an organisation's data management and prepare a ranked list of first-year actions.

## Prerequisites

- Uses a spreadsheet to sort, filter and summarise a table

## Next courses

- [LDS-EXE-402 · Leading the Enterprise Data Office](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-EXE-402.md)
- [LDS-ADV-301 · Data Products, Valuation and Monetisation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-ADV-301.md)
- [LDS-DMG-201 · Data Governance Operating Model and Stewardship](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-DMG-201.md)
- [LDS-DMG-202 · Metadata, Catalogues and Lineage](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-DMG-202.md)
- [LDS-DMG-203 · Data Quality Management](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-DMG-203.md)
- [LDS-DMG-204 · Data Classification in Practice](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-DMG-204.md)
- [LDS-DMG-205 · Data Sharing, Open Data and Freedom of Information](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-DMG-205.md)
- [LDS-DMG-206 · Personal Data Protection in Practice](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-DMG-206.md)
- [LDS-DMG-207 · Compliance Evidence and Data Maturity Assessment](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-DMG-207.md)
- [LDS-DMG-208 · Master and Reference Data Management](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-DMG-208.md)

## Topics

### What data management is

- Data as an asset: value, cost and risk
- Knowledge areas and how a national standard groups them into domains
- Governance versus management
- The lifecycle from creation to disposal

### Roles

- Data management office and committee
- Chief data officer and governance, compliance, privacy and open data officers
- Data owners, business stewards and technical stewards

### Core artefacts

- Asset register and catalogue
- Business glossary and data dictionary
- Lineage diagrams
- Quality rules, issue log and classification register

### Protecting and sharing data

- Classification by impact of disclosure
- Personal data principles: lawful basis, purpose limitation, minimisation
- Sharing, open data and information requests
- What staff may enter into AI tools

### Measuring progress

- Maturity scales and evidence
- Compliance versus maturity
- Data readiness for AI use cases

# LDS-DMG-201 · Data Governance Operating Model and Stewardship

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Data Management and Governance Professions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-DMG.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 24 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants design how governance will run in a fictional organisation of 4,000 staff whose data office exists on paper. They choose an operating model, write charters for the governance bodies, assign decision rights for 20 recurring data decisions, design the steward network and map national requirements to internal controls. They then write a three-year data strategy tied to business objectives and a costed business case for the office, and defend both before a mock executive committee. Policy drafting craft is LDS-DMG-302.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compare centralised, federated and hybrid governance operating models and when each works.
- Prepare charters for the committee, the data office and the steward network.
- Apply a decision-rights matrix to recurring data decisions.
- Prepare a governance scorecard that traces national requirements to controls, owners and indicators.
- Build a data strategy and a costed business case for a data office.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-DMG-101 · Data Management Foundations](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-DMG-101.md)
- Describes the main business processes and systems of one organisation they know

## Next courses

- [LDS-DMG-207 · Compliance Evidence and Data Maturity Assessment](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-DMG-207.md)
- [LDS-DMG-302 · Drafting Data and AI Policies and Standards](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-DMG-302.md)

## Topics

### Foundations

- Board-level principles from the international standard on governance of data (ISO/IEC 38505-1)
- Capability frameworks and benchmarks for data offices
- Operating models: centralised, federated, hybrid

### Structures and stewardship

- Committee and office charters
- Owners, business stewards and technical stewards
- Selecting stewards and protecting their time

### Decision rights and controls

- Recurring decisions and who holds them
- Responsibility matrices and escalation
- Policy hierarchy, exceptions and waivers
- From requirement to control and indicator

### Strategy and business case

- Data objectives tied to business objectives
- Use cases as the unit of value
- Costs, benefits, assumptions and sensitivity

### Running the programme

- Key performance and key risk indicators
- Compliance and maturity cycles
- Building a governance culture
- First committee rulings on data used by AI (depth in LDS-DMG-301)

# LDS-DMG-202 · Metadata, Catalogues and Lineage

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Data Management and Governance Professions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-DMG.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days with labs, plus a short follow-up task
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants run an open-source catalogue over a fictional agency's synthetic database and file store. They harvest technical metadata, add what machines cannot (glossary terms, owners, classifications), measure how many machine-drafted descriptions need correction, judge a change through lineage and prepare records for a national or open catalogue.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Configure scheduled harvesting of technical metadata from a database and a file store.
- Prepare glossary terms and link them to columns, owners and classifications.
- Measure the error rate of machine-drafted asset descriptions under steward review.
- Analyse the downstream impact of a schema change using captured lineage.
- Prepare dataset records in a standard vocabulary for an external catalogue.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-DMG-101 · Data Management Foundations](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-DMG-101.md)
- Reads a table schema and explains what each column holds

## Topics

### Metadata foundations

- Descriptive, structural and administrative metadata
- Dataset vocabulary standards

### Catalogue automation

- Connectors and scheduled harvesting
- Sample values: when to hide them
- Tag propagation
- Machine-drafted descriptions and review queues

### Glossary and lineage

- Definitions that settle disputes
- Approval and versioning
- Lineage as events from pipelines
- Column-level impact analysis

### The catalogue in operation

- Coverage, completeness and freshness
- Publishing to national and open catalogues
- The catalogue as context for AI assistants

---

# LDS-DMG-203 · Data Quality Management

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Data Management and Governance Professions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-DMG.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 24 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants run a quality programme for one service domain of a fictional agency whose monthly report disagrees with its source systems. They turn requirements into measurable rules, profile synthetic tables, execute the rules and log issues. They trace a recurring error to its origin, agree corrective and preventive actions with owners, and judge whether a dataset and a document collection are fit to train or ground an AI system. Pipeline-level contracts and observability are DEV-DAT-204.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare measurable quality rules with scope, method, threshold and frequency.
- Analyse column, relationship and dependency profiles to find anomalies.
- Implement rules as executable checks and report results by dimension.
- Diagnose the root cause of a recurring issue and define corrective and preventive actions.
- Measure the fitness of data for training or grounding an AI system.
- Design a quality plan covering priorities, rules, monitoring and issue workflow for a domain.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-DMG-101 · Data Management Foundations](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-DMG-101.md)
- Writes simple SQL with filters, joins and grouping (FND-DAT-101 or the provided SQL pre-work)

## Topics

### Requirements and rules

- Dimensions: accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, validity, uniqueness
- Critical data elements
- Thresholds, tolerances and exceptions
- Cost and service impact of poor quality

### Profiling and measurement

- Column, relationship and dependency profiling
- Sampling when full checks cost too much
- Scorecards that do not mislead

### Issue management

- Lifecycle, severity and escalation
- Five whys, cause-and-effect diagrams, lineage tracing
- Prevention at entry and integration points

### Quality in operation

- Pre-release checks before sharing or publication
- Quality clauses in sharing agreements
- Settling priority disputes with owners

### Data used by AI

- Quality characteristics for analytics and machine learning data (ISO/IEC 5259)
- Representativeness, label noise, duplication, leakage
- Currency and conflicting versions in retrieval collections
- AI-suggested rules under review

---

# LDS-DMG-204 · Data Classification in Practice

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Data Management and Governance Professions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-DMG.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: one and a half days with labs, plus a short follow-up task
- Total hours: 12 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants classify a fictional agency's data end to end: scope structured and unstructured assets, rate disclosure impact, map ratings to levels, set handling controls and record owner-approved decisions in a register. They then measure how often a machine-labelling pipeline misses against their own decisions, and set rules for human review.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Apply an impact assessment to propose a classification level for each asset.
- Prepare handling requirements per level for storage, transfer, sharing, retention and disposal.
- Prepare register entries with owner approval, exceptions and declassification dates.
- Evaluate an assisted classification pipeline and set when a person must review.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-DMG-101 · Data Management Foundations](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-DMG-101.md)
- Explains in plain words what access control and encryption protect against

## Next courses

- [LDS-DMG-301 · Governing Data for AI: Training, Retrieval and Agent Access](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-DMG-301.md)

## Topics

### Scope

- Structured, semi-structured and unstructured data
- Discovery from registers and file shares
- Classification versus personal data sensitivity

### Impact and levels

- Categories: national interest, organisational activities, individuals, infrastructure
- Ratings mapped to four levels, public to top secret
- Restricted sub-categories; older texts say confidential
- Aggregation raising a level

### Controls and register

- Labelling files, records and fields
- Access, encryption, anonymisation, retention, disposal
- Exceptions, declassification and review

### Assisted classification

- Pattern and model-based detection
- Misses and false alarms, notably in Arabic text
- Human review rules and audit trail

---

# LDS-DMG-205 · Data Sharing, Open Data and Freedom of Information

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Data Management and Governance Professions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-DMG.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days with labs, plus a short follow-up task
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants staff a fictional agency's access desk. They triage sharing requests and draft an agreement, decide a research request, answer information requests with justified redactions, and prepare a dataset for open publication with a re-identification test, metadata and licence. Impact assessment is LDS-DMG-206; anonymisation in depth is DEV-SEC-303.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Apply a sharing test to requests and draft an agreement for an approved one.
- Decide a research request for linked records under secondary-use rules.
- Prepare a dataset for open publication with a re-identification risk test.
- Draft responses to information requests with recorded grounds for withholding.
- Measure access performance from response times, usage and reuse.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-DMG-101 · Data Management Foundations](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-DMG-101.md)
- Applies classification levels to datasets (LDS-DMG-204 or equivalent)

## Topics

### Sharing

- Legitimate purpose, minimisation, single source of truth
- Routes: service bus, marketplace, secure research environment
- Agreements and signatories by level
- Onward use, including training AI models
- Secondary use for research and public interest

### Open data

- Open by default and grounds to withhold
- Quasi-identifiers, k-anonymity and its limits, small cells
- Formats, metadata and licences

### Freedom of information

- The right to information and exemptions
- Deadlines, partial disclosure, redaction

### Performance

- Response time, approval rate, reuse
- Publication plans and user feedback

# LDS-DMG-206 · Personal Data Protection in Practice

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Data Management and Governance Professions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-DMG.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants act as the protection officer of a synthetic telehealth provider and build its case file: records of processing, an impact assessment for a new symptom-checker assistant, answers to rights requests, a transfer assessment and a breach response. Each artefact is reviewed as a regulator would. Privacy-enhancing engineering is DEV-SEC-303; personal data in model training is LDS-AIG-306.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain the lawful bases, data subject rights and controller and protection officer duties, and identify which apply to a processing activity.
- Prepare records of processing from a data-flow map, with purpose, legal basis, categories, recipients, retention and transfers.
- Apply an impact assessment method to an AI-assisted service, rating risks to individuals and selecting proportionate controls.
- Analyse data subject requests and draft responses that meet scope, identity, exemption and deadline rules.
- Decide whether a cross-border transfer may proceed, and under which safeguard or exemption.
- Lead the response to a personal data breach from containment to notice to the authority and to individuals.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-DMG-101 · Data Management Foundations](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-DMG-101.md)
- Reads a regulation and extracts who must do what, by when

## Topics

### The law and the protection officer

- Lawful bases, consent and legitimate interest
- Rights and controller duties
- Officer appointment triggers, independence, indicators and staff awareness
- Draft amendments: not in force until gazetted

### Records and data flows

- Flows across systems, processors and countries
- Records of processing and their upkeep
- Privacy notices and processor contracts
- Minimisation, retention and destruction

### Impact assessment

- Triggers: sensitive data, large scale, new technology
- Pseudonymisation, anonymisation and re-identification tests
- AI features: conversation logs, training on user data, automated decisions

### Rights, transfers and breaches

- Request intake, identity checks, exemptions and deadlines
- Adequacy, standard clauses, binding rules and transfer risk assessment
- Breach assessment, notice content and timing

# LDS-DMG-207 · Compliance Evidence and Data Maturity Assessment

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Data Management and Governance Professions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-DMG.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 24 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants act as the compliance specialist of a synthetic public entity preparing for its annual national data assessment. They judge a repository of realistic evidence (policies, minutes, screenshots, logs), score maturity, compute operational metrics, and measure how often an AI assistant maps documents to the wrong specification. The result is an audit-ready evidence pack, a risk-ranked findings register and a corrective plan, tested in a mock audit. Roadmaps for sponsors belong to LDS-ADV-202.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Describe how a national data assessment scores compliance, maturity and operational excellence, and what evidence each part needs.
- Prepare acceptance criteria stating what must exist, who approved it and what proves it operates.
- Classify evidence as sufficient, partial or insufficient, recording the reason and the gap.
- Compute maturity scores and operational metrics, tracing every level claimed to its evidence.
- Evaluate an AI-assisted mapping of documents to specifications and decide where the compliance process may use it.
- Deliver an evidence pack with a risk-ranked findings register and a corrective plan with owners and dates.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-DMG-101 · Data Management Foundations](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-DMG-101.md)
- [LDS-DMG-201 · Data Governance Operating Model and Stewardship](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-DMG-201.md)
- Tells a control from a specification in a data management standard

## Topics

### Assessment methods

- Inventory of applicable instruments and obligations
- Binary scoring of specifications and priorities
- Maturity questionnaires and level descriptors
- Operational metrics from national platforms
- Comparison with DAMA-DMBOK and DCAM maturity models

### Evidence

- Existence, approval, implementation, effectiveness
- Sufficiency, currency and scope
- Sampling and walk-throughs

### Findings and the audit cycle

- Findings, root causes and risk ranking
- Corrective plans and verified closure
- Readiness calendar and reporting to the data management committee

### AI in compliance work

- Assisted evidence mapping
- Measuring assistant errors against a key
- Human sign-off and audit trail

# LDS-DMG-208 · Master and Reference Data Management

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Data Management and Governance Professions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-DMG.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: 2 days with labs and a stewardship mini-project
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants consolidate supplier records from three synthetic systems, with Arabic and English names, spelling variants and conflicting addresses. They produce measured matching rules, golden records, a stewardship queue and a versioned reference code list, using provided notebooks and a visual tool.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compare registry, consolidation, coexistence and centralised implementation styles.
- Configure matching rules with Arabic and English name normalisation and measure their precision and recall.
- Implement survivorship rules that form golden records from source trust, recency and completeness.
- Prepare a versioned reference code list with owner, definitions and a crosswalk from source codes.
- Design a stewardship workflow for uncertain matches and code changes, with roles, service levels and indicators.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-DMG-101 · Data Management Foundations](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-DMG-101.md)
- Has profiled a table for completeness and duplicates (LDS-DMG-203 or equivalent)
- Runs a provided notebook; no programming

## Topics

### Concepts and styles

- Master, reference and transactional data
- Implementation styles and ownership

### Matching

- Standardisation and blocking
- Arabic name normalisation and transliteration
- Deterministic and probabilistic rules
- Precision, recall and thresholds

### Golden records and reference data

- Survivorship, cross-references and history
- Standard code sets and hierarchies
- Versioning and crosswalks

### Stewardship

- Queues and decision rights
- Quality indicators for core entities
- Language-model match suggestions under human review

# LDS-DMG-301 · Governing Data for AI: Training, Retrieval and Agent Access

- Track: Executives & Leaders
- Path: [Data Management and Governance Professions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/LDS-DMG.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Workshop: 2 days with labs on provided AI systems
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants decide what data AI systems may train on, retrieve, expose to agents or send to external models, then test those decisions on a provided assistant and agent over synthetic data. Pipelines are DEV-DAT-302; agent sandboxes LDS-AIG-302; personal data and copyright in training LDS-AIG-306.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Classify proposed AI data uses by data class, purpose and hosting as allowed, conditional or prohibited.
- Test a retrieval assistant for permission leaks and specify the label filter that closes them.
- Configure per-tool agent permissions as scoped, read-only or approval-gated.
- Review provider terms on retention, training on inputs, residency and deletion, and decide which data classes may be sent.
- Defend a data-for-AI standard with logging and retention rules, and a decision record for one case.

## Prerequisites

- [LDS-DMG-204 · Data Classification in Practice](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/LDS-DMG-204.md)
- Explains how an assistant retrieves documents and calls tools (FND-AIC-102 or equivalent)

## Topics

### Uses and eligibility

- Training, evaluation, retrieval, agent context and logs
- Derived data inherits source rules; training cannot be undone
- Classification, purpose, secondary use and source licences
- Hosting tiers: local, sovereign cloud, external service

### Permission-aware access

- Labels at indexing, filters at retrieval
- Least privilege and approvals for agents
- Access through semantic layers and tool servers

### External models and evidence

- Provider terms, transfers and residency
- Prompt and output logs
- AI data-use register

# FND-PRG-101 · Python Programming for Data and AI

- Track: Data & AI Foundations
- Path: [Programming and Software Practice](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/FND-PRG.md)
- Level: Level 100 · Explain
- Format: Extended: 12 weekly three-hour sessions with labs, graded assignments and a final project
- Total hours: 60 h
- Audience: beginner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants write Python from first principles and learn to read it as carefully as they write it. Each week opens with an AI-off tracing drill, then a lab on one synthetic dataset of municipal service requests in comma-separated values (CSV) and JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) files. The labs grow into a small command-line program that loads, validates, summarises and reports on the data, built from typed functions, classes and modules rather than one long notebook.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Read a short program and state its output and the value of each variable at marked lines.
- Distinguish lists, tuples, dictionaries and sets by mutability, ordering and lookup cost, and name the right one for a task.
- Explain when work belongs in a notebook and when in a script or module, including the risk of hidden state.
- Implement functions with type hints, docstrings and explicit handling of invalid input.
- Use classes, files and the standard library to read, transform and write delimited and JSON data, including Arabic text.
- Build a small command-line program that loads, validates, summarises and reports on a dataset, and explain its structure.

## Prerequisites

- No programming experience assumed

## Next courses

- [FND-PRG-103 · Data Structures, Algorithms and Complexity](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-PRG-103.md)
- [FND-PRG-104 · Software Testing, Code Review and Documentation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-PRG-104.md)
- [FND-PRG-105 · Computer Systems and Cloud Essentials for AI Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-PRG-105.md)
- [FND-PRG-106 · Code Reading and Debugging without Assistance](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-PRG-106.md)
- [FND-AIC-101 · How Machine Learning Works](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-AIC-101.md)
- [FND-AIC-105 · Classical AI: Search, Planning and Knowledge Representation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-AIC-105.md)
- [DEV-INF-201 · Machine Learning Systems on One Machine](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-INF-201.md)

## Topics

### Values, names and control flow

- Types, operators and expressions
- Names, references and mutation
- Conditionals and loops
- Tracing a program by hand

### Functions and modules

- Parameters, return values and scope
- Decomposing a task into small functions
- Modules and the standard library
- Docstrings and type hints

### Collections and iteration

- Lists, tuples, dictionaries and sets
- Comprehensions and generators
- Sorting with keys and grouping

### Files, errors and text

- Text, delimited and JSON files
- Encodings and Arabic text
- Exceptions, validation and failing loudly
- Reading tracebacks

### Program structure and habits

- Classes and data classes
- Notebooks versus scripts and modules
- A command-line entry point
- Committing to a course repository
- Using an AI tutor without handing over the thinking

# FND-PRG-102 · Command Line, Git and Reproducible Environments

- Track: Data & AI Foundations
- Path: [Programming and Software Practice](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/FND-PRG.md)

- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 24 h
- Audience: beginner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants set up work that another person can rebuild from a clean machine. They script the shell, use Git with branches, pull requests and review on a shared repository, resolve a merge conflict, lock dependencies, run a project in a container without administrator rights, and keep secrets out of history.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain how Git records history as commits, branches and remotes, and what each everyday command changes.
- Use the shell to inspect and transform files, combining commands with pipes and a short script.
- Apply a branch, pull request and review workflow, including resolving a merge conflict.
- Configure an isolated environment with locked dependencies and run the project in a container without administrator rights.
- Prepare a repository that keeps secrets out of history, and carry out the response when one leaks.
- Deliver a repository that a peer reproduces on a clean machine using only its README.

## Prerequisites

- Writes and runs a short program in Python or another language

## Topics

### The shell

- Paths and permissions
- Pipes, redirection and filters
- Environment variables and exit codes
- Remote login with secure shell (SSH) keys

### Version control

- Commits, staging and history
- Branches, merges and conflicts
- Pull requests and review etiquette
- Undoing mistakes

### Reproducible environments

- Virtual environments
- Declared dependencies and lock files
- One documented command to rebuild and run
- Keeping data and outputs out of the code

### Containers at user level

- Images, containers and volumes
- A short container definition
- What a container does not isolate

### Secrets and hygiene

- Scanning before each commit
- After a leak: rotate, then clean history

# FND-PRG-103 · Data Structures, Algorithms and Complexity

- Track: Data & AI Foundations
- Path: [Programming and Software Practice](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/FND-PRG.md)
- Level: Level 100 · Explain
- Format: Extended: 12 weekly three-hour sessions with labs, graded problem sets and a final project
- Total hours: 60 h
- Audience: beginner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants implement the core data structures and algorithms in Python, measure them, and connect each to the data and model code they will write later. They build a dynamic array, a hash map, a heap, a search tree and a graph, analyse sorting and search by counting operations and by timing, and explain why a join, a deduplication or a nearest-neighbour lookup is fast or slow. The emphasis is reasoning about time and memory on realistic inputs, not interview puzzles.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain big-O notation and identify the cost class of a given piece of code.
- Compare arrays, linked structures, hash tables, heaps and trees by operation cost and memory layout.
- Implement a dynamic array, a hash map with collision handling, a binary heap and a binary search tree.
- Implement and measure sorting, binary search and graph traversal, and relate the timings to predicted complexity.
- Analyse a slow data-processing function and change its structure or algorithm to remove the bottleneck.
- Design and build a small in-memory index and defend its structures against a time and memory budget.

## Prerequisites

- [FND-PRG-101 · Python Programming for Data and AI](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-PRG-101.md)
- Uses school algebra, including powers and logarithms

## Topics

### Cost models

- Counting operations and big-O
- Best, average and worst case
- Amortised cost
- Recursion, divide and conquer, and simple recurrences

### Sequences and hashing

- Dynamic arrays and memory layout
- Linked lists and when they lose
- Hashing, collisions and load factor
- How Python's dictionaries work

### Ordering and searching

- Comparison sorts and stable sort keys
- Binary search
- Heaps and top-k selection

### Trees and graphs

- Search trees and balance
- Tries for text prefixes
- Breadth-first and depth-first search
- Shortest paths with Dijkstra's algorithm

### Memory and data code

- Object overhead and contiguous data
- Streaming data that does not fit in memory
- Joins as hashing or sorting
- Nearest-neighbour search and why indexes approximate
- Edit distance by dynamic programming

---

# FND-PRG-104 · Software Testing, Code Review and Documentation

- Track: Data & AI Foundations
- Path: [Programming and Software Practice](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/FND-PRG.md)
- Level: Level 100 · Explain
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: beginner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants take a small, untested data-cleaning library and make it trustworthy. They write unit and integration tests, design cases from a specification, isolate files, time and network calls with fixtures and test doubles, review each other's pull requests against a checklist, write a README and reference documentation, and package the library so it installs and passes its tests in a clean environment. Property and mutation testing and the verification of agent-written code follow in DEV-SWE-204.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish unit, integration and end-to-end tests, and explain what each can and cannot show.
- Design test cases from a specification using equivalence partitions, boundary values and error cases.
- Implement unit and integration tests with fixtures and test doubles for files, time and network calls.
- Review a pull request for correctness, tests, readability and security, and write actionable comments.
- Prepare a README and reference documentation, and package the library for installation.
- Deliver a tested, reviewed and documented release with automated checks on every change.

## Prerequisites

- [FND-PRG-101 · Python Programming for Data and AI](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-PRG-101.md)
- [FND-PRG-102 · Command Line, Git and Reproducible Environments](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-PRG-102.md)

## Next courses

- [DEV-SWE-204 · Testing and Verification of AI-Assisted Code](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-SWE-204.md)

## Topics

### What to test

- Tests as executable specification
- Test levels and their costs
- What coverage hides

### Designing tests

- Partitions and boundary values
- Empty, missing and mixed-script text
- Regression tests from bug reports

### Test tooling

- Fixtures and parametrised tests
- Test doubles for files, time and network
- Tests in CI on each pull request

### Code review

- Checklists and small pull requests
- Giving and receiving comments
- Assistant-generated code held to the same standard

### Documentation and packaging

- README and quick start
- Docstrings and generated reference pages
- Semantic versioning and a change log
- Building and installing a package

# FND-PRG-105 · Computer Systems and Cloud Essentials for AI Work

- Track: Data & AI Foundations
- Path: [Programming and Software Practice](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/FND-PRG.md)
- Level: Level 100 · Explain
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: beginner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants build a working model of the machine and the cloud beneath data and AI code. They measure how processors, accelerators, memory and storage limit a workload, compare threads and processes, follow an API call from name lookup to response, and run a containerised batch job on a cloud virtual machine with object storage and least-privilege access. Every lab ends with a cost figure. Serving, orchestration and capacity planning follow in DEV-OPS-201, DEV-INF-201 and DEV-INF-302.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain the memory hierarchy and how accelerators differ from processors, and identify what limits a workload.
- Describe the steps between calling an API and receiving its response, from name lookup to status code.
- Measure a program's processor, memory and disk use, and compare threaded and multi-process versions.
- Use an HTTP API from code with authentication, timeouts and retries with back-off.
- Configure a virtual machine, object storage, a container image and a least-privilege role for a batch job.
- Plan, size and price a small batch inference job, run it, and explain the gap between estimate and actual.

## Prerequisites

- [FND-PRG-101 · Python Programming for Data and AI](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-PRG-101.md)
- [FND-PRG-102 · Command Line, Git and Reproducible Environments](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-PRG-102.md)

## Next courses

- [DEV-SWE-202 · Back-End Services and Interfaces for AI Applications](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-SWE-202.md)

## Topics

### Inside one machine

- Cores, threads and accelerators
- Memory hierarchy and bandwidth
- Storage throughput
- Model memory from parameter count and number format

### Operating system essentials

- Processes, threads and the global interpreter lock
- Asynchronous input and output

### Networks and APIs

- Addresses, ports and name lookup
- Transport encryption and certificates
- Methods, status codes and headers
- Timeouts, retries and rate limits

### Containers and cloud primitives

- Pushing an image to a registry and running it remotely
- Compute, object storage and managed services
- Identity, roles and least privilege
- Regions, residency and shared responsibility

### Cost basics

- Pricing units for compute, storage, transfer and tokens
- Idle resources, teardown and budgets
