# DEV-OPS-201 · Deploying AI Services: Containers, Serving and Monitoring

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Operations and Reliability](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-OPS.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants take a tabular classifier and a small open-weight language model from a notebook to a service that other people can call. They package each in a container image with pinned dependencies, serve it behind a typed HTTP API with validation and health checks, add structured logs, metrics and alerts, and release a new version through a staged rollout that they reverse when a health signal fails. Labs run on a laptop with 16 GB of memory, or on a provided lab virtual machine where a laptop cannot run containers.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish batch, online and streaming inference and the signals that matter for each.
- Package a model as a reproducible container image with pinned dependencies and no secrets inside.
- Implement a serving endpoint with input validation, timeouts, a concurrency limit and health checks.
- Configure structured logs, request metrics and two alerts with documented thresholds.
- Deliver a new version through a health-gated staged rollout and roll it back when a signal degrades.
- Prepare a runbook with versions, artefact hashes, owner, alerts and rollback steps.

## Prerequisites

- Writes and runs Python scripts from the command line
- Uses Git and a Python virtual environment, as taught in FND-PRG-102
- Has called an HTTP API and read a JSON response
- Loads a saved model in Python and calls it for predictions

## Next courses

- [DEV-AGT-402 · Agent Platforms: Sandboxes, Durable Execution and Identity](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-AGT-402.md)
- [DEV-OPS-301 · Machine Learning Operations: Pipelines, Registries and Delivery](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-OPS-301.md)
- [DEV-OPS-302 · Operating Language Model Applications: Tracing, Evaluation Gates and Safe Releases](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-OPS-302.md)
- [DEV-INF-301 · Container Orchestration for AI Workloads: Accelerators, Scheduling and Autoscaling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-INF-301.md)
- [DEV-INF-401 · Inference Performance and Cost Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-INF-401.md)

## Topics

### From notebook to service

- Batch, online and streaming inference
- Service contracts
- Latency, throughput and cost as requirements

### Packaging

- Images, layers and multi-stage builds
- Pinned dependencies
- Secrets out of images; image scanning

### Serving

- Typed APIs and input validation
- Timeouts, retries and concurrency limits
- A small language model behind a standard chat-completions interface
- Health, readiness and warm-up

### Observability basics

- Structured logs and correlation identifiers
- Latency, traffic, errors and saturation
- Tokens and time to first token
- Personal data kept out of logs

### Releasing

- Immutable, versioned artefacts
- Deployments, services and probes on a single-node cluster
- Rolling and blue-green updates
- Rollback drills and runbooks

# DEV-OPS-301 · Machine Learning Operations: Pipelines, Registries and Delivery

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Operations and Reliability](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-OPS.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 36 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants build the machinery that lets a model be retrained, checked and redeployed safely many times. On a synthetic customer dataset delivered in monthly batches with planted drift, they version data, code and models together, register models with lineage, write a training pipeline with validation and promotion gates, deliver it to staging and production, monitor drift and delayed-label performance, and wire retraining triggers that a person approves. Labs run on a laptop or a provided lab virtual machine with a single-node cluster. Feature stores are in DEV-MLE-203.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Implement versioning that ties each model to its data snapshot, code commit, configuration and environment.
- Build a training pipeline with data validation, evaluation against the production model and a promotion gate.
- Configure continuous integration and delivery that tests code, data contracts and model behaviour before deployment.
- Measure feature drift, prediction drift and delayed-label performance against a reference window.
- Design a retraining policy combining schedule, drift and performance triggers with human approval and a cost limit.
- Diagnose a training-serving skew incident from lineage and logs.

## Prerequisites

- [DEV-OPS-201 · Deploying AI Services: Containers, Serving and Monitoring](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-OPS-201.md)
- Trains and validates a supervised model in Python, as in DEV-MLE-201
- Writes unit tests and works in Git with merge requests

## Next courses

- [DEV-INF-403 · Designing an Internal AI Platform](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-INF-403.md)

## Topics

### Versioning and registries

- What changes behaviour: data, code, configuration, environment
- Experiment tracking and registry lineage
- The hand-off contract from data scientists

### Pipelines

- Parameterised and conditional steps
- Data validation and contracts
- Champion and challenger evaluation
- Failure recovery and reruns

### Delivery for models

- Tests for code, data and model behaviour
- Pipelines and environments as code
- Promotion gates and approvals
- Shadow, canary and rollback

### Monitoring and retraining

- Drift statistics and false alarms
- Delayed labels and proxy metrics
- Training-serving skew
- Retraining triggers and cost

### Governing the pipeline

- Maturity levels from manual to automated
- Subgroup metrics in every gate
- Audit logs, retention and decommissioning

# DEV-OPS-302 · Operating Language Model Applications: Tracing, Evaluation Gates and Safe Releases

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Operations and Reliability](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-OPS.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 36 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants run a grounded assistant, a synthetic public-services help desk with retrieval and two tools, as a production service. They version prompts, model identifiers, settings, retrieval index and tool schemas as one release unit, trace every request, put evaluation suites into a release gate, ship changes through shadow and canary stages with automatic rollback, configure guardrails, and sample live traffic for online evaluation and human review. Labs use a small open-weight model on a laptop or a free hosted tier. Evaluator design is in DEV-EVL-301 and organisation-wide release criteria in DEV-EVL-401; here participants operate evaluators.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Implement versioning of prompts, model identifiers, settings, index and tool schemas as one release unit.
- Instrument model, retrieval and tool calls with spans, token counts, time to first token and time per output token.
- Build a release gate that blocks a change when a critical failure rate rises beyond a stated margin.
- Deliver a change through shadow and canary stages with automatic rollback.
- Configure input and output guardrails and measure their false-block and miss rates.
- Design an online evaluation loop that samples traces, routes uncertain cases to people and feeds failures into the offline suite.

## Prerequisites

- [DEV-OPS-201 · Deploying AI Services: Containers, Serving and Monitoring](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-OPS-201.md)
- [DEV-LLM-201 · Building Applications on Language Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-LLM-201.md)
- Has written automated checks of model outputs; DEV-EVL-301 is recommended

## Next courses

- [DEV-OPS-303 · Operating AI Agents: Durable Execution, Sandboxing and Replay](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-OPS-303.md)
- [DEV-OPS-401 · Reliability Engineering for AI Services](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-OPS-401.md)

## Topics

### What changes behaviour

- The release unit
- Provider model updates and pinned identifiers
- Knowledge-base refresh as a release

### Tracing

- Spans for model, retrieval, tool and agent calls
- OpenTelemetry generative AI conventions, still in development
- Retention and redaction of traces

### Gates and releases

- Critical and tolerated failure modes
- Paired comparison under a call budget
- Shadow traffic, canaries and rollback triggers

### Guardrails and online evaluation

- Guardrails inline, evaluators after the fact
- Calibrated graders on live traces
- Review queues and new regression cases

---

# DEV-OPS-303 · Operating AI Agents: Durable Execution, Sandboxing and Replay

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Operations and Reliability](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-OPS.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Workshop: two days with labs and an operations shift
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants operate a small agent fleet on a provided cluster. They version each agent as one bundle, keep durable sessions alive through crashes and upgrades, test that tools are safe to retry, run sandboxes with quotas and egress policies, replay recorded traces to reproduce incidents, and throttle or stop agents at a gateway. Platform construction is in DEV-AGT-402.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Implement an agent bundle that pins model, prompts, tool schemas, skills and harness settings.
- Test tool idempotency by injecting crashes, timeouts and duplicate deliveries.
- Diagnose an agent failure by replaying its recorded trace against two versions.
- Decide whether to drain, pin or migrate in-flight sessions for an upgrade, then carry it out.
- Configure per-agent rate and spend limits, tool allowlists and a kill switch.

## Prerequisites

- [DEV-AGT-301 · Agentic Systems Engineering: Loops, Context and Harnesses](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-AGT-301.md)
- [DEV-OPS-302 · Operating Language Model Applications: Tracing, Evaluation Gates and Safe Releases](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-OPS-302.md)
- DEV-AGT-402, or has run agents on a durable workflow engine

## Topics

### Versioning agents

- Session, harness and sandbox split
- The agent bundle
- In-flight sessions during upgrades

### Durable execution

- Checkpoints and orphaned sessions
- Idempotency keys and duplicates
- Approval waits and timeouts
- Health signals: steps, tool errors, stuck sessions

### Sandboxes and controls

- Warm pools, quotas and egress policies
- Rate, spend and step budgets
- Kill switches and runbooks

### Replay

- Recorded tool responses
- Replay for reproduction and regression

# DEV-OPS-304 · AI Cost Engineering: Gateways, Routing, Caching and Unit Economics

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Operations and Reliability](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-OPS.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Workshop: two days with labs and a costed review
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants make the cost of AI applications measurable, attributable and smaller without losing quality. From a month of synthetic usage traces for three applications behind one gateway, they model cost per request, attribute spend, set budgets and alerts, tune routing in operation under a quality check, measure caches and report cost per successful outcome. Engine optimisation is in DEV-INF-401; model choice and prompt layout are in DEV-LLM-303.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compute request cost and cost per successful outcome from tokens, tool calls and retries.
- Configure gateway keys per team, environment tags and spend limits.
- Optimise a gateway routing policy so each request class meets its quality floor at lower cost.
- Evaluate exact, prefix and semantic caches for savings, staleness and cross-tenant leakage.
- Prepare a unit-economics report with trend, forecast, energy use and savings options.

## Prerequisites

- [DEV-LLM-201 · Building Applications on Language Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-LLM-201.md)
- Reads request traces with token counts; DEV-LLM-303 is recommended

## Topics

### The cost model

- Prefill, decode and cached tokens
- Retries, agent steps and long contexts
- Accelerator hours and utilisation

### Attribution and budgets

- Keys and tags per team
- Showback before chargeback
- Spend anomaly alerts
- Unsettled allocation for agents

### Routing and caching

- Request classes, cascades and fallbacks
- Measured cache hit rates
- Staleness and tenant isolation

### Reporting value

- Cost per successful outcome
- Forecasting spend
- Energy beside money

---

# DEV-OPS-401 · Reliability Engineering for AI Services

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Operations and Reliability](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-OPS.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 36 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants set and defend reliability standards for AI services that other teams build. They write service level objectives for availability, latency and answer quality, load-test a self-hosted language model to find the concurrency at which goodput meets the objective, design degradation and recovery paths, lead incident drills and blameless reviews, and admit models only after verifying signatures and bills of materials. Labs use small open-weight models on a provided GPU notebook and recorded traffic. Engine tuning is in DEV-INF-401; the full go-live review across disciplines is DEV-PRJ-401.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Design service level objectives for availability, latency and answer quality, with error budgets.
- Evaluate service capacity by load-testing to a goodput target and setting an admission limit.
- Design degradation for overload and dependency failure using load shedding and a smaller fallback model.
- Lead an incident drill from detection to recovery and write a blameless review.
- Build an admission check that verifies model signatures, an AI bill of materials and licences.
- Review another team's AI service for reliability readiness and set launch conditions.

## Prerequisites

- [DEV-OPS-302 · Operating Language Model Applications: Tracing, Evaluation Gates and Safe Releases](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-OPS-302.md)
- Has carried on-call or incident duties for a production service
- Reads latency percentiles and queueing behaviour; DEV-INF-401 and DEV-SEC-304 are recommended

## Topics

### Objectives for AI services

- Time to first token and time per output token
- Quality indicators from online evaluation
- Error budgets, burn-rate alerts and release policy
- Objectives for agents: completion and cost

### Capacity under load

- Queueing, batching and tail latency
- Goodput against an objective
- Trace-replay load and admission control

### Designing for failure

- Provider, retrieval and tool failures
- Fallback models and degraded modes
- Retry storms and chaos experiments
- Restoring indexes, session state and model artefacts

### Incidents

- Detecting silent quality regressions
- Roles and decision logs
- Incidents turned into regression tests

### Integrity and standards

- Signing a manifest of hashed model files
- AI bills of materials and admission policy
- Readiness reviews; provenance depth in DEV-SEC-304

---

# DEV-INF-201 · Machine Learning Systems on One Machine

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Infrastructure, Performance and Architecture](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-INF.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 36 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants follow one small model from data to a served endpoint on a single machine and account for its time and memory. They estimate a workload with simple performance models, profile training and inference, fit a run into a memory limit, compress and accelerate the model, benchmark it honestly and serve it under load. Labs use a laptop CPU, a free notebook GPU and public data.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compute a first-order time estimate with the roofline model and identify whether data, algorithm or machine binds the workload.
- Measure where time goes in a training step and explain the gap from the estimate.
- Compute a training memory budget and apply mixed precision and activation checkpointing to fit a memory limit.
- Apply quantisation, pruning and distillation and measure accuracy, size and latency for each variant.
- Prepare a fair benchmark with warm-up, repetitions, fixed inputs and latency percentiles.
- Deliver a served model that meets a stated requirement on two hardware targets and defend a ship, restrict or hold decision.

## Prerequisites

- [FND-PRG-101 · Python Programming for Data and AI](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-PRG-101.md)
- [FND-AIC-101 · How Machine Learning Works](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-AIC-101.md)
- Writes Python with array libraries from a terminal and a notebook
- Has trained a small neural network in a deep learning framework
- Explains processors, memory hierarchy and accelerators at the level of FND-PRG-105
- Linear algebra and probability at the level of FND-MTH-101 and FND-MTH-103

## Next courses

- [DEV-INF-302 · AI Infrastructure and Capacity Planning](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-INF-302.md)
- [DEV-INF-303 · Edge and On-Device AI: Small Models and Neural Processors](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-INF-303.md)
- [DEV-INF-304 · Embedded Machine Learning on Microcontrollers](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-INF-304.md)
- [DEV-INF-401 · Inference Performance and Cost Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-INF-401.md)
- [DEV-INF-402 · Scaling Machine Learning Systems: Distributed Training and Fleets](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-INF-402.md)

## Topics

### Workloads and estimates

- Deployment paradigms from data centre to microcontroller
- Roofline model and arithmetic intensity
- Finding the binding constraint first

### Frameworks and training

- Tensors, operators and automatic differentiation
- Eager execution, graph capture and compilation
- Training memory and mixed precision
- Input pipelines and data loading

### Compression and acceleration

- Numerical formats and post-training quantisation with calibration
- Pruning and distillation, with the accuracy cost measured
- Vectorisation, tiling and operator fusion

### Benchmarking and serving

- Benchmark hygiene and percentiles
- Latency budgets and queueing under load
- Dynamic batching and key-value caching
- Energy per inference; hand-off to DEV-OPS-201

---

# DEV-INF-301 · Container Orchestration for AI Workloads: Accelerators, Scheduling and Autoscaling

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Infrastructure, Performance and Architecture](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-INF.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 36 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants run AI workloads on a shared container cluster as a platform team must: accelerators allocated and shared safely, training jobs admitted fairly under quotas, distributed jobs placed all at once, and inference services scaled and routed on the metrics users feel. Labs use single-node clusters on provided virtual machines with simulated accelerators, small open-weight models and recorded traces, with the public Kubernetes AI conformance checklist as the rubric.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Configure accelerator allocation for whole, shared and partitioned devices and verify isolation between tenants.
- Configure queue-based admission with quotas, borrowing, priorities and preemption for a shared accelerator pool.
- Implement gang scheduling so that a multi-worker training job no longer holds accelerators idle.
- Design autoscaling for an inference service on queue or latency metrics, including scale to zero and a cold-start budget.
- Evaluate load-aware and prefix-cache-aware routing against round-robin.
- Audit a cluster against a public AI conformance checklist and deliver a ranked remediation plan.

## Prerequisites

- [DEV-OPS-201 · Deploying AI Services: Containers, Serving and Monitoring](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-OPS-201.md)
- Writes and applies declarative manifests on a container orchestrator
- Explains time to first token and throughput for a language model service

## Topics

### Accelerators as cluster resources

- Device plugins versus dynamic resource allocation
- Time-slicing, partitioning and virtualised devices
- Device health, taints and driver operators

### Admission and scheduling

- Queues, quotas, cohorts and borrowing
- Preemption with checkpoint and resume; dominant-resource fairness
- Gang and topology-aware placement

### Serving and autoscaling

- Serving operators and model weights as registry artefacts
- Cold start and scale to zero
- Scaling pods on service-objective metrics, nodes by accelerator type

### Inference-aware traffic

- Gateway inference extensions and endpoint picking
- Priority, fairness and load shedding
- Prefill and decode placement (depth in DEV-INF-401)

### Observability, isolation and conformance

- Per-accelerator metrics in a standard format
- Mediated device access and workload sandboxing
- Showback of accelerator-hours per tenant
- The checklist as an acceptance test

---

# DEV-INF-302 · AI Infrastructure and Capacity Planning

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Infrastructure, Performance and Architecture](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-INF.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Workshop: two days of analytical sizing labs and a defended case
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants size AI systems from first principles before purchase: they read accelerator datasheets, compute serving and training needs, turn benchmark curves into replica counts, check plans against rack power and cooling, and compare cloud, on-premises and sovereign-provider options in a cost model. Labs are analytical, checked against an open simulator.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compute the memory, bandwidth and compute needed to serve a language model at a given precision, context and concurrency.
- Analyse latency-throughput benchmark curves to choose an operating point and replica count for a service objective.
- Design a capacity plan in accelerators, racks, power and cooling for a growing demand forecast.
- Evaluate cloud, on-premises and sovereign options with a cost-of-ownership model including utilisation risk and placement limits.

## Prerequisites

- [DEV-INF-201 · Machine Learning Systems on One Machine](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-INF-201.md)
- Works with units and orders of magnitude in a spreadsheet or notebook

## Topics

### Accelerators and their limits

- Accelerator families and peak compute
- Memory capacity and bandwidth
- Scale-up versus scale-out interconnect

### Sizing workloads

- Serving: weights, key-value cache, concurrency
- Training compute from tokens and parameters
- Benchmark curves, goodput and vendor claims

### Facilities, cost and placement

- Rack power, liquid cooling and tokens per watt
- Energy, carbon and water by region
- Rented versus owned capacity; break-even utilisation
- Classification before placement (depth in DEV-INF-405)

# DEV-INF-303 · Edge and On-Device AI: Small Models and Neural Processors

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Infrastructure, Performance and Architecture](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-INF.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants move small language and vision models onto laptops, single-board computers, phones and the browser. They decide when on-device inference is worth it, quantise and convert models, run them on neural processing units and other on-device accelerators, measure speed, memory, energy and heat, and build a browser application with a server fallback. Labs use open-weight models, public data and provided boards.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Analyse whether on-device, browser, hybrid or server inference fits a case on privacy, latency, connectivity and cost.
- Prepare a small language model and a vision model for a device by quantising, converting and checking parity.
- Measure latency, peak memory, energy per inference and thermal throttling under sustained load.
- Optimise a model for a neural processing unit or GPU delegate by diagnosing unsupported operators.
- Build a browser application that runs a small model locally with a server fallback.
- Deliver an on-device application that meets a latency, memory and accuracy budget and defend its trade-offs.

## Prerequisites

- [DEV-INF-201 · Machine Learning Systems on One Machine](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-INF-201.md)
- Has trained and evaluated a small neural network with a deep learning framework
- Builds a simple web page with JavaScript, or completes the provided pre-work

## Topics

### When and why on device

- Privacy, residency and data minimisation
- Offline, latency and per-request cost
- Hybrid device and server patterns

### Small models and formats

- Small language models tested on own tasks
- Efficient vision backbones and detectors
- Weight-only and full-integer quantisation
- Quantised file formats and parity tests

### Runtimes and accelerators

- Mobile and embedded inference runtimes
- Neural processing unit delegates and fallbacks
- Browser inference on WebGPU and built-in model interfaces

### Measurement and operations

- On-device benchmark protocol
- Energy, battery and thermal limits
- Updating and protecting models on devices

# DEV-INF-304 · Embedded Machine Learning on Microcontrollers

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Infrastructure, Performance and Architecture](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-INF.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Workshop: two bench days with one board per pair and a live demonstration
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants build a sensing device that runs a neural network in a few hundred kilobytes of memory and a few milliwatts of power. On a low-cost board they record and label sensor data, train and quantise a tiny model, deploy it as firmware and measure latency, memory and energy per inference.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compute the flash, RAM and energy budget of a sensing application, including the tensor arena and duty cycle.
- Prepare a sensor dataset and feature pipeline with a documented collection protocol.
- Deploy a full-integer quantised model to a microcontroller and diagnose the memory, latency and accuracy problems that appear.
- Deliver a sensing device that meets a stated memory, latency and battery-life target under real conditions.

## Prerequisites

- [DEV-INF-201 · Machine Learning Systems on One Machine](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-INF-201.md)
- Reads and edits simple C or C++ code, or completes the provided two-hour firmware pre-work

## Topics

### Constraints of tiny devices

- Flash, SRAM, clock and power envelopes
- Always-on sensing and duty cycling
- Benchmarks for tiny inference

### From sensor to model

- Windowing, spectral and inertial features
- Small convolutional networks and autoencoders
- Quantisation-aware training and integer kernels

### Deployment and measurement

- Model as firmware: arena sizing and operators
- Energy per inference and battery life
- Desk accuracy versus field accuracy

# DEV-INF-401 · Inference Performance and Cost Engineering

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Infrastructure, Performance and Architecture](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-INF.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 40 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants take a language model deployment that is too slow and too costly and make it meet a service objective at the lowest cost they can defend. They build a first-principles cost model, measure goodput curves on replayed traffic, locate bottlenecks, and apply batching, caching, quantisation, speculative decoding, routing, disaggregated prefill and decode, and autoscaling, re-checking task quality after every change.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compute prefill cost, decode cost and key-value cache memory, and predict the binding resource.
- Benchmark a serving configuration as a goodput curve over concurrency against latency objectives.
- Diagnose why a deployment misses its service objective.
- Optimise batching, admission, prefix caching, cache precision and speculative decoding while holding task quality.
- Evaluate compressed variants against the base model and decide which to serve.
- Design a serving topology covering disaggregation, routing, replica count and scaling policy.

## Prerequisites

- [DEV-INF-201 · Machine Learning Systems on One Machine](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-INF-201.md)
- [DEV-OPS-201 · Deploying AI Services: Containers, Serving and Monitoring](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-OPS-201.md)
- Serves an open-weight model behind an HTTP endpoint and reads its metrics
- Explains latency percentiles and the difference between latency and throughput
- DEV-LLM-303 recommended

## Topics

### The cost model of inference

- Prefill and decode: compute-bound and memory-bound
- Key-value cache memory arithmetic
- Queueing and the latency-throughput trade-off

### Measuring serving performance

- Time to first token, time per output token, goodput
- Load patterns and trace replay
- Pareto curves and benchmark validity

### Scheduling and caching in the engine

- Continuous batching, chunked prefill, admission control
- Paged attention, cache precision and offload to host memory
- Prefix and semantic caching, and tenant isolation

### Cheaper models

- Quantisation formats per accelerator
- Speculative decoding and acceptance rates
- Distilled and multi-adapter serving (distillation itself: DEV-LLM-301)

### Serving across replicas

- Disaggregated prefill and decode; cache-aware routing
- Autoscaling on queue and service-objective metrics, scale to zero, cold starts
- Cost and energy per successful request

---

# DEV-INF-402 · Scaling Machine Learning Systems: Distributed Training and Fleets

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Infrastructure, Performance and Architecture](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-INF.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 36 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants time collective communication and fit a cost model to it, train a small transformer with replicated and then sharded state across worker processes, plan data, tensor and pipeline parallelism for a large model and check the plan in a simulator, set checkpoint intervals from failure rates, and diagnose low utilisation in recorded fleet telemetry. Labs run on CPU workers, a provided multi-accelerator node for one session, and an analytical simulator.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compute collective communication time with a latency-bandwidth model and calibrate it against measurements.
- Build a training run with replicated, then sharded, model and optimiser state and measure scaling efficiency.
- Design a parallelism plan that fits device memory and maximises throughput for a large model.
- Design a checkpoint and recovery policy from failure rates and checkpoint cost.
- Diagnose the causes of low accelerator utilisation in a fleet.
- Evaluate fleet serving options for several models across two sites.

## Prerequisites

- [DEV-INF-201 · Machine Learning Systems on One Machine](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-INF-201.md)
- [DEV-MLE-202 · Deep Learning Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-MLE-202.md)
- Debugs a training loop and reads its memory use
- Explains network bandwidth, latency and topology

## Topics

### The fleet and its limits

- Memory capacity and bandwidth
- Scale-up and scale-out interconnects
- Amdahl's law and the communication tax

### Collective communication

- All-reduce, all-gather, reduce-scatter, all-to-all
- Ring and tree algorithms
- Overlapping communication with computation

### Distributed training

- Data parallelism and sharded optimiser state
- Tensor, pipeline and expert parallelism
- Mixed precision and activation recomputation
- Planning with a simulator

### Fault tolerance

- Failure models and silent data corruption
- Checkpoint intervals and the Young-Daly rule
- Elastic restart and lost-work budgets

### Fleet efficiency and serving at scale

- Utilisation, stragglers and input stalls
- Job queues and gang scheduling (mechanics in DEV-INF-301)
- Placement across sites and failover
- Energy and carbon of training and serving

# DEV-INF-403 · Designing an Internal AI Platform

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Infrastructure, Performance and Architecture](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-INF.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Studio: six weeks part-time with weekly coaching, three design reviews and a final defence before a panel
- Total hours: 40 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants design the shared platform through which many teams reach models safely and at known cost. For a fictional organisation with twelve product teams and three data classification levels, each participant designs the model catalogue and admission rules, a gateway with quotas and fallback, tenant isolation, golden paths with evaluation and tracing built in, and showback, builds a thin working slice, and defends the design after three coached reviews.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Analyse platform demand into a matrix of workloads, tenants, classifications and service objectives.
- Design a model catalogue and gateway with admission criteria, routing, quotas, fallback and audit logging.
- Design tenant isolation, quotas and fair sharing of accelerators.
- Build golden-path templates with evaluation, tracing and governance gates on by default.
- Design cost attribution and showback with a tagging scheme and unit metrics.
- Defend the platform design, its build-or-buy decisions and a phased roadmap.

## Prerequisites

- [DEV-OPS-301 · Machine Learning Operations: Pipelines, Registries and Delivery](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-OPS-301.md)
- Has used or operated a shared machine learning platform in a team
- Reads container cluster manifests; has configured a model gateway and read a usage-based bill (DEV-OPS-304 covers both)

## Topics

### The platform as a product

- Tenants, users and the platform team
- Demand analysis and phasing
- Adoption, lead time and utilisation metrics

### Catalogue and gateway

- Admission: licence, evaluation evidence, permitted classification, cost tier
- Provider abstraction, credentials, quotas, fallback, protocol-server mediation
- Models as versioned, signed artefacts; deprecation and migration

### Tenancy and shared capacity

- Isolation of data, keys and compute
- Noisy neighbours and fair sharing
- Self-hosted open-weight capacity beside hosted APIs

### Golden paths

- Templates for retrieval, agent, batch and fine-tuning work
- Gates built into the default
- Paved roads against mandates

### Cost attribution

- Tags and one key per team and application
- Showback before chargeback
- Cost per successful outcome; agent workloads without an accepted method

---

# DEV-INF-404 · AI Solution Architecture and Decision Records

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Infrastructure, Performance and Architecture](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-INF.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 36 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants practise the architect's core loop on AI systems: requirements to quality-attribute scenarios, scenarios to options, options to recorded decisions, and decisions to designs others can review and reuse. On fictional public-sector and enterprise cases they write measurable scenarios, draw views as code, compare at least three options on three-year cost, risk and lock-in, keep a decision log, define a reference design with automated fitness checks, and review a peer's architecture alongside data architects.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare quality-attribute scenarios with measurable targets, including regulatory and classification constraints.
- Design an end-to-end architecture with context, container and data-flow views and a per-request latency and cost budget.
- Evaluate at least three solution options, including a non-generative baseline.
- Deliver a decision log whose records state context, options, decision, consequences and review trigger.
- Review a peer's architecture with a structured trade-off method and recommend approval or a recorded deviation.
- Design a reference architecture with fitness functions that check conformance automatically.

## Prerequisites

- [DEV-SWE-301 · System Design for AI Products](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-SWE-301.md)
- Has helped deliver an AI or data system to production
- Data architects may take DEV-DAT-401 in place of DEV-SWE-301

## Topics

### Requirements to scenarios

- Drivers, constraints and stakeholders
- AI quality attributes: accuracy, latency, cost, explainability, privacy, oversight
- Regulation as architecture constraints

### Views and patterns

- Views as code
- Retrieval, agentic, fine-tuned, classical, batch and event-driven patterns
- Evaluation, observability, fallback and trust boundaries as components
- Integration with enterprise systems and data platforms

### Options analysis

- Weighted criteria and their pitfalls
- Total cost of ownership and sensitivity
- Lock-in, portability, exit and procurement requirements

### Decision records

- Record structure and review triggers
- Decision logs as living documents
- Reconstructing decisions for legacy systems

### Reference designs and reviews

- Reference architectures and fitness functions
- Structured trade-off reviews and deviations
- Explaining trade-offs to sponsors

---

# DEV-INF-405 · Regulated and Sovereign Deployment Architecture

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Infrastructure, Performance and Architecture](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-INF.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Workshop: two days with four labs and a defended design
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants turn data rules into deployment architecture for a fictional health and government assistant. They classify data, prompts, embeddings, logs and model weights, trace every flow leaving the approved jurisdiction, place each component, and make the placement verifiable with customer-held keys, attestation, egress denial and signed model import.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Classify a system's data and AI artefacts and analyse every flow crossing a jurisdiction or trust boundary.
- Design a placement that puts each component in an allowed location.
- Design and test key custody, attestation, egress denial and signed model import.
- Defend a hybrid deployment design and its evidence pack.

## Prerequisites

- Has completed DEV-INF-404, DEV-SEC-401 or DEV-DAT-401, or designs deployment architectures at work
- Reads a data classification policy and a data-protection impact assessment

## Topics

### Rules to requirements

- Classification and impact assessment
- Transfer bases, safeguards and risk assessment
- Hosting rules that defer to data rules

### Placement options

- In-country regions, national providers, on premises, air gap
- Hosted model APIs: processing region, retention, sub-processors
- Local open-weight serving; hybrid splits and leakage

### Verifiable controls and evidence

- Customer-held keys, remote attestation and default-deny egress
- Signed models and bills of materials
- Evidence packs and approved exceptions

# DEV-DAT-201 · Modern Data Engineering

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Data Engineering and Architecture](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-DAT.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 36 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants build one batch pipeline end to end for a fictional trading company whose margin report nobody trusts. They query raw extracts with analytical SQL, load an API and a database change feed incrementally, and model a star schema with a slowly changing supplier dimension. Tested transformations and an agreed data contract run under an orchestrator, and the result lands in an open table format that a second engine reads. All data is synthetic and deterministic. Log-based capture and streaming continue in DEV-DAT-203; contract versioning and observability in DEV-DAT-204.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish transactional, warehouse, lake and lakehouse platforms and the workloads each serves.
- Analyse raw extracts with window functions, deduplication and incremental predicates in analytical SQL.
- Implement idempotent incremental loads from an API and a change feed, applying merges with type 2 history.
- Implement a dimensional model as version-controlled transformations with tests and documentation.
- Draft a data contract in an open standard and enforce it in the build.
- Build an orchestrated pipeline into an open table format that recovers from failure by re-running.

## Prerequisites

- [FND-DAT-101 · SQL and Relational Data](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-DAT-101.md)
- [FND-PRG-102 · Command Line, Git and Reproducible Environments](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-PRG-102.md)
- Writes Python scripts that read and write files

## Next courses

- [DEV-DAT-202 · Analytics Engineering and Semantic Layers](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-DAT-202.md)
- [DEV-DAT-203 · Streaming and Change Data Capture](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-DAT-203.md)
- [DEV-DAT-204 · Data Quality, Contracts and Observability](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-DAT-204.md)
- [DEV-DAT-301 · Data Modelling: Conceptual to Semantic](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-DAT-301.md)
- [DEV-DAT-302 · Data Infrastructure for AI](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-DAT-302.md)
- [DEV-DAT-303 · Data Platform Operations: Reliability, Security and Cost](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-DAT-303.md)
- [DEV-DAT-401 · Data Architecture](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-DAT-401.md)

## Topics

### Platform shapes and analytical SQL

- Transactional versus analytical systems; extract, load, transform (ELT)
- Layered raw, cleaned and served zones
- Window functions and incremental predicates
- Columnar files and partitioning

### Ingestion and change

- Schema drift and idempotent loads
- Change data capture (CDC), merge and slowly changing dimensions
- Single-node first, distributed when measured
- Classifying fields and dropping what is not needed

### Modelling, transformation and contracts

- Grain, facts and dimensions
- Tests, environments and state-aware builds
- Open contract standards
- Verifying agent-written transformations

### Orchestration and table formats

- Retries, backfills and data-aware scheduling
- Snapshots, schema evolution, time travel and compaction
- Catalogues and multi-engine reads

# DEV-DAT-202 · Analytics Engineering and Semantic Layers

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Data Engineering and Architecture](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-DAT.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants take over the analytics of a fictional online marketplace whose three dashboards report three different net-revenue figures. They define metrics once as tested code, build a semantic model of joins, dimensions and access rules over a dimensional layer, and rebuild two dashboards as version-controlled code. They then measure how often a language model answers 60 business questions correctly against the raw schema and through the semantic layer. Metric and dashboard design for analysts is SPC-ANL-203.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain how a semantic layer differs from a dimensional model and from a business intelligence (BI) tool's internal model.
- Implement metric definitions as code, including ratios, time grains and filters, with tests that reconcile them to source totals.
- Configure a semantic model with entities, joins, dimensions and row-level access rules.
- Prepare dashboards as code that read only from the semantic layer and ship through review.
- Measure the execution accuracy of natural-language querying with and without the semantic layer.
- Decide which questions may be routed to natural-language querying, and under which safeguards.

## Prerequisites

- [DEV-DAT-201 · Modern Data Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-DAT-201.md)
- Uses Git to branch, commit and open a review

## Topics

### Metrics as code

- Layered models reviewed through continuous integration
- Simple, ratio, cumulative and derived metrics
- Grain, time spines and fan-out traps
- Reconciliation tests, documentation and ownership

### Semantic models

- Entities, joins and dimensions
- Access rules and classification-aware fields
- Pre-aggregation, caching and query cost
- Open interchange specifications and portability

### Dashboards as code

- Version-controlled definitions
- Certified versus exploratory content

### Natural-language querying

- Text-to-SQL failure modes
- Context from semantic layer, glossary and examples
- Execution accuracy and safeguards

# DEV-DAT-203 · Streaming and Change Data Capture

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Data Engineering and Architecture](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-DAT.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants build the event backbone of a fictional delivery company. They publish order and courier events to a partitioned log, capture changes from the payments database without touching its code, and process both streams with event-time windows, watermarks and keyed state. They make the pipeline survive crashes and duplicate deliveries without double counting, write results into an open table format and serve a low-latency view in streaming SQL. Generators replay synthetic events, some late, out of order or duplicated.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish logs from queues and the three delivery guarantees, and state what each costs.
- Configure a partitioned log with keys, schemas and consumer groups that preserve per-entity ordering.
- Implement log-based change data capture, including deletes and schema changes.
- Implement event-time windows with watermarks and keyed state, and compare them with a batch recomputation.
- Build a stream into an open table format that loses and duplicates nothing after a crash.
- Decide between streaming, micro-batch and batch from latency, cost and correctness evidence.

## Prerequisites

- [DEV-DAT-201 · Modern Data Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-DAT-201.md)
- Runs multi-service applications with containers on a laptop
- A laptop with about 16 GB of memory for the container stack, or a provided remote workspace

## Topics

### Logs, queues and events

- Partitions, keys, offsets and retention
- Consumer groups and queue semantics
- Event schemas and compatibility rules

### Change data capture

- Log-based versus query-based capture
- Snapshots, deletes and schema changes
- The outbox pattern

### State and time

- Event time versus processing time
- Windows, watermarks and late data
- Keyed state and checkpoints
- Joining streams with tables

### Correctness under failure

- End-to-end delivery guarantees
- Idempotent sinks and transactional writes
- Consumer lag, back-pressure and dead-letter topics
- Replays and reprocessing

### Streams into tables and SQL

- Streaming into open table formats; compacting small files
- Incrementally maintained views
- Latency budgets and running cost

---

# DEV-DAT-204 · Data Quality, Contracts and Observability

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Data Engineering and Architecture](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-DAT.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 24 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants put quality controls into the synthetic claims platform of a fictional health insurer. They profile the sources, turn consumer requirements into executable rules, extend the contract basics of DEV-DAT-201 with versioning and service levels, and gate every build on them. Pipelines emit lineage and run events, which participants use to find the blast radius of a seeded incident, quarantine bad data, notify consumers and write a post-incident review. The quality programme and stewardship side is LDS-DMG-203.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Describe the data quality dimensions and match each to a check that runs inside a pipeline.
- Analyse tables with column, relationship and dependency profiling to propose rules.
- Implement rules with thresholds, severities and quarantine actions as pipeline gates.
- Implement contract versioning with breaking-change rules and service-level clauses for freshness and ownership, checked in continuous integration.
- Configure lineage and run events across the pipeline and use them to list affected downstream assets.
- Diagnose a data incident from alerts, lineage and logs, and lead it to closure.

## Prerequisites

- [DEV-DAT-201 · Modern Data Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-DAT-201.md)
- Runs and edits an orchestrated pipeline locally

## Topics

### Dimensions, profiling and rules

- Accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, validity, uniqueness
- Column, relationship and dependency profiling
- Critical data elements first
- Rules with scope, threshold, severity and owner
- Quality scores and trend reports

### Gates in pipelines

- Warn, block or quarantine
- Write, audit, publish
- Volume and distribution anomalies

### Data contracts

- Producer and consumer duties
- Service-level clauses: freshness, completeness, support
- Versioning and breaking-change rules in continuous integration

### Lineage and observability

- Lineage as events emitted by runs
- Freshness, volume and schema signals
- Alert routing and fatigue

### Incident handling

- Triage and consumer notice
- Root cause through lineage
- Backfills, corrections and blameless reviews

# DEV-DAT-301 · Data Modelling: Conceptual to Semantic

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Data Engineering and Architecture](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-DAT.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants model one domain of a fictional water utility, from interviews and undocumented source schemas to a semantic model. They derive conceptual and normalised logical models, then implement a dimensional mart, an auditable vault layer and a wide feature table, measuring each under its intended queries. They publish a semantic model over the mart and review language-model-generated schemas against modelling standards. Every choice is recorded and defended. Metrics as code and dashboards are DEV-DAT-202; ontologies and knowledge graphs continue in DEV-DAT-304.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compare normalised, dimensional, vault and wide-table models by the change, history and query patterns each serves.
- Prepare conceptual and normalised logical models from interviews and source-system analysis.
- Design a dimensional model with declared grain, conformed dimensions and chosen history types, and implement it.
- Design a vault layer and a wide feature table and optimise their physical layout.
- Implement a semantic model of entities, measures and dimensions carrying definitions and classification tags.
- Review a generated schema against modelling standards and defend the corrections.

## Prerequisites

- [FND-DAT-101 · SQL and Relational Data](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-DAT-101.md)
- [DEV-DAT-201 · Modern Data Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-DAT-201.md)
- Reads and writes table definitions with keys and constraints

## Next courses

- [DEV-DAT-401 · Data Architecture](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-DAT-401.md)

## Topics

### Conceptual and logical modelling

- Entities and business rules from interviews
- Normal forms and when to stop
- Natural, surrogate and composite keys
- Diagram-as-code notation

### Source analysis

- Schema inspection and reverse engineering
- Profiling for keys and dependencies
- Conflicting definitions across systems

### Dimensional design

- Grain, facts and conformed dimensions
- Slowly changing dimension types and bitemporal history
- Degenerate, role-playing and bridge structures

### Vault, wide tables and physical design

- Hubs, links and satellites
- Wide tables for lakehouse engines
- Partitioning, clustering and indexing
- Reference data and code sets

### Semantic models and review

- Measures and dimensions for reporting tools and agents
- Standards, naming and model repositories
- Schema evolution and backward-compatible change
- Reviewing generated schemas

# DEV-DAT-302 · Data Infrastructure for AI

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Data Engineering and Architecture](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-DAT.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 36 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants build the data layer that language model applications and agents read from, and run it as a pipeline rather than a one-off index. On a synthetic bilingual municipal corpus with a change feed, they embed incrementally, carry source permissions onto every chunk, propagate deletions, gate personal data, migrate embedding models and expose governed tables to an agent through a protocol server. Parser choice is DEV-LLM-204, search quality DEV-LLM-203, retrieval evaluation DEV-EVL-303 and graphs DEV-DAT-304.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Implement an incremental pipeline that parses, chunks and embeds documents and reprocesses only what changed.
- Configure a parsing stage that routes by document class, falls back to deterministic extraction and quarantines failures.
- Design an index whose chunks and vectors trace to source, version and permissions, and migrate it to a new embedding model.
- Build permission-aware indexing that copies source access rules onto chunks and filters before ranking.
- Measure personal-data detection before indexing and set a redaction rule per entity type.
- Build a protocol server that gives an agent read-only, scoped access to governed tables and metrics.

## Prerequisites

- [DEV-DAT-201 · Modern Data Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-DAT-201.md)
- Has called an embedding or language model API from Python

## Topics

### Unstructured data as a pipeline

- Change feeds and idempotent reprocessing
- Parsing routes and deterministic fallback
- Chunking as a versioned transform
- Quarantine and replay

### Embeddings and indexes as derived data

- Multilingual embedding choice
- Vectors in a relational database, table format, search service or object store
- Hybrid index refresh and dual-index migration

### Permissions, deletion and lineage

- Source access lists to chunk labels
- Filtering before ranking
- Erasure that reaches derived data

### Personal data and external services

- Detectors and what they miss
- Redaction and pseudonymisation at indexing
- Data sent to external model services
- Prompt and trace logs as governed data

### Governed agent access

- Protocol servers over a catalogue and semantic layer
- Read-only tools, scopes and audit logs
- When a plain API or command-line tool is enough

# DEV-DAT-303 · Data Platform Operations: Reliability, Security and Cost

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Data Engineering and Architecture](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-DAT.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants operate a running lakehouse for a synthetic utility company on a laptop container stack. They set service objectives for freshness, completeness and latency, promote changes through branch environments and continuous integration, enforce roles, masking, row filters and encryption at one policy point, attribute and cut spend, and block unsafe dependencies. The course ends with an on-call shift with injected faults and a restore drill. Quality rules and contracts are DEV-DAT-204; model and dataset provenance is DEV-SEC-304.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Configure service level objectives and error budgets for data product freshness, completeness and latency.
- Implement branch-based promotion with state-aware continuous integration, infrastructure as code and write-audit-publish gates.
- Design and test access controls combining roles, attributes, column masking, row filters and encryption at a single policy enforcement point.
- Optimise platform cost by attributing spend to workloads and changing engine placement, schedules and table maintenance.
- Prepare a software bill of materials for pipeline code, images and connectors and gate builds on it.
- Diagnose and resolve platform incidents from lineage, logs and metrics, and write a blameless review.

## Prerequisites

- [DEV-DAT-201 · Modern Data Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-DAT-201.md)
- Has run a pipeline under version control with automated tests
- Works with containers and a command-line shell
- Quality gates as in DEV-DAT-204 (recommended)

## Topics

### Reliability for data

- Freshness, completeness and latency indicators
- Error budgets and alerting on symptoms
- Compaction, snapshot expiry and restore drills

### DataOps

- Branches and zero-copy environments
- State-aware builds in continuous integration
- Promotion and rollback across environments
- Infrastructure as code; reviewing agent-written changes

### Access and security

- Role-based and attribute-based control
- Policy in the catalogue or query engine
- Masking, row filters and short-lived credentials
- Encryption at rest and in transit, key rotation
- Access reviews and lineage as audit evidence

### Cost

- Unit cost per query, pipeline and data product
- Showback before chargeback (FinOps Framework)

### Supply chain and incidents

- Pinned dependencies, bills of materials, signed images
- On-call, runbooks and blameless reviews

# DEV-DAT-304 · Knowledge Graphs and Ontology Engineering

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Data Engineering and Architecture](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-DAT.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Workshop: two days with labs and a short graded build
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants build a knowledge graph from two synthetic registries and a set of Arabic and English documents. They resolve duplicate entities, write an ontology from competency questions with public vocabularies, validate it with shape constraints, admit language-model-extracted facts only after validation and with provenance, and compare graph-grounded with text-only retrieval on multi-hop questions.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish Resource Description Framework (RDF) graphs, property graphs and relational models, and state when each fits.
- Apply entity resolution with blocking, scoring and clustering, and measure its precision and recall.
- Design an ontology and shape constraints that answer competency questions.
- Implement language-model extraction of facts into the graph with validation and source provenance.
- Evaluate graph-grounded against text-only retrieval and recommend one.

## Prerequisites

- Has designed a normalised relational schema (DEV-DAT-301 or equivalent)
- Has called a language model API from Python

## Topics

### Graph models

- Triples, identifiers and property graphs
- SPARQL, Cypher and ISO Graph Query Language
- When a relational model is enough

### Entity resolution

- Arabic transliteration and normalisation
- Blocking, scoring, clustering and human review

### Ontology engineering

- Competency questions
- Reusing SKOS, schema.org and PROV-O
- Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL) validation

### Using graphs

- Validated extraction with provenance
- Graph-grounded retrieval and paths as explanations
- Ontology versioning as sources change

# DEV-DAT-401 · Data Architecture

Participants act as data architect for a synthetic group of public service entities moving from a central warehouse and scattered lakes to a governed platform. - Contracts and interoperability

# DEV-SEC-201 · Secure Development of AI Applications

Participants make an insecure helpdesk assistant, with retrieval over synthetic policy documents and two tools, fit to ship. They map its weaknesses to public risk lists, treat model output as untrusted input, keep secrets server-side, scan dependencies and model files, carry each user's permissions into retrieval and log without personal data. - Apply document-level access control to retrieval.

- Why injection has no model-level fix

- Output as untrusted input
- Schema validation and context encoding
- Unbounded consumption and rate limits

### Secrets, permissions and dependencies

- Server-side keys and secret stores
- User permissions carried into retrieval
- Pinned dependencies and invented package names
- Unsafe model file formats

### Logging

- Security events worth logging
- Redacting personal data

# DEV-SEC-301 · Securing Language Model and Agent Applications

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Security and Privacy Engineering for AI](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-SEC.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 36 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants attack, then defend, a synthetic procurement agent that reads supplier email, searches documents, keeps memory and acts through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. They threat-model it, run injection and exfiltration attacks, then contain it with a sandbox and egress allowlist, scoped delegated tokens, hardened protocol servers, measured guardrails and well-placed approvals. Platform isolation and identity are DEV-AGT-402; red-team programmes are DEV-SEC-302.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare a threat model naming trust boundaries, private data, untrusted inputs and exit paths.
- Test the agent against injection and exfiltration through documents, images, links and tool arguments.
- Design containment that removes private data, untrusted content or the exit path from each high-risk flow.
- Build delegated authorisation with scoped, short-lived tokens exchanged at each hop.
- Measure guardrails on attack and benign sets and set thresholds.
- Evaluate the residual risk of a hardened agent and decide which actions still need approval.

## Prerequisites

- [DEV-SEC-201 · Secure Development of AI Applications](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-SEC-201.md)
- Has built an agent that calls tools in a loop (DEV-AGT-301 or equivalent)
- Runs containers locally

## Next courses

- [DEV-SEC-401 · Security Architecture for AI Platforms](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-SEC-401.md)

## Topics

### Threat modelling agents

- Trust boundaries, data flows and STRIDE applied to agents
- Private data, untrusted content and exit paths
- Risk lists and adversary technique mapping

### Injection and exfiltration

- Direct, indirect and cross-modal injection
- Exfiltration through permitted paths
- Memory and retrieval poisoning

### Containment and authorisation

- Sandboxes for generated code
- An egress allowlist is a capability grant
- Token exchange, audience, scope and lifetime
- Forbidden token passthrough and the confused deputy

### Protocol servers and tools

- Tool poisoning and changes after approval
- Hostile text in tool results
- Request forgery during metadata discovery
- Local, shadow and over-scoped servers

### Guardrails, approvals and audit

- Classifier error rates and false refusals
- Approval fatigue
- Action logs for investigation

# DEV-SEC-302 · AI Red Teaming and Adversarial Testing

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Security and Privacy Engineering for AI](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-SEC.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants plan and run a red-team exercise against two synthetic targets: a bilingual Arabic and English citizen-services assistant and a tool-using agent. They set scope and rules of engagement, pick objectives from a catalogue of adversary techniques, probe manually and with automated generators and scorers, measure attack success over repeated trials, rate findings and report them so a product owner can act. Every confirmed finding becomes a regression test. Building controls is DEV-SEC-301; governance-side testing is LDS-AIG-302.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish security, safety, privacy and misuse objectives and the harm each tests.
- Design an exercise plan with scope, rules of engagement, stop conditions and handling of harmful outputs.
- Apply manual techniques including multi-turn escalation, encoding, indirect injection and attacks in Arabic dialect and transliteration.
- Configure automated probing and compute attack success with intervals.
- Evaluate findings for severity, likelihood and reproducibility and prioritise fixes.
- Build regression tests from confirmed findings.

## Prerequisites

- [DEV-SEC-201 · Secure Development of AI Applications](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-SEC-201.md)
- Writes Python scripts that call an API
- Computes a proportion with a confidence interval

## Topics

### Planning

- Objectives tied to harms
- Scope, rules of engagement and stop conditions
- Handling harmful outputs and tester welfare

### Attack techniques

- Technique catalogues
- Jailbreak families and multi-turn escalation
- Indirect and cross-modal injection
- Hidden-context extraction and agent goal hijack
- Arabic, dialect, transliteration and code-switching

### Automated probing

- Generators, converters and scorers
- Attacker models and their limits
- Budgets and repeated trials

### Scoring and reporting

- Success rates with intervals
- Severity, likelihood and reproducibility
- Disclosure to suppliers

### From findings to regression

- Findings as test cases
- Suites that survive model updates
- Red-team suites in release gates

# DEV-SEC-303 · Privacy Engineering and Privacy-Enhancing Technologies

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Security and Privacy Engineering for AI](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-SEC.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants engineer privacy into a synthetic health-insurance claims pipeline that trains a model, answers questions over member documents and logs prompts. They minimise personal-data flows, pseudonymise identifiers with keyed tokens, re-identify a released table by linkage and repair it, publish differentially private statistics under a budget, generate synthetic data and measure its leakage, and build a detector for personal data in prompts, logs and retrieval chunks, including Arabic names. Legal procedure such as impact assessments is LDS-DMG-206; memorisation and deletion in trained models are LDS-AIG-306.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compare pseudonymisation, anonymisation, differential privacy, synthetic data and confidential computing by what each protects and costs.
- Prepare a personal-data flow inventory with a minimisation decision per field.
- Test a de-identified release for re-identification by linkage on quasi-identifiers.
- Compute differentially private statistics under a fixed budget.
- Evaluate a synthetic dataset for utility and membership-inference leakage and decide on release.
- Build a personal-data detector for prompts, logs and retrieval chunks.

## Prerequisites

- Cleans and joins tables with a DataFrame library in Python
- Computes a mean, a variance and a proportion

## Topics

### Privacy by design

- Purpose, minimisation and retention
- Personal data in training, retrieval, prompts and logs
- Linkage, inference and extraction threats

### Pseudonymisation and anonymisation

- Keyed hashing and tokenisation
- Quasi-identifiers and k-anonymity
- Generalisation, suppression and their limits

### Differential privacy

- Sensitivity, noise and budget
- Counts, histograms and means
- Training with differential privacy and its accuracy cost

### Synthetic data

- Tabular generators
- Utility and privacy metrics
- Membership inference

### Personal data in AI systems

- Detection in prompts, logs and corpora
- Arabic names and identifier formats
- Masking before external model calls
- Federated learning and secure computation in brief

# DEV-SEC-304 · AI Supply Chain Security: Signing, Bills of Materials and Provenance

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Security and Privacy Engineering for AI](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-SEC.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Workshop: one and a half days with labs and an adoption review
- Total hours: 12 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants secure the path by which models, datasets and dependencies reach production. On a pipeline pulling an open-weight model and a public dataset, they catch a tampered file and an unsafe format, sign and verify a manifest of hashed model files, generate a machine-learning bill of materials, store models as registry artefacts and fail builds on unacceptable licences. Supplier governance is LDS-AIG-203; release gating is DEV-OPS-401.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain where models, datasets, packages, prompts, tools and skills enter an AI system and the attack at each point.
- Test downloaded model files for unsafe serialisation and tampering before loading.
- Prepare a machine-learning bill of materials with model, dataset and licence provenance.
- Build a pipeline that signs model manifests and blocks unsigned, modified or badly licensed artefacts.
- Evaluate a third-party model's supply-chain evidence and decide whether to adopt it.

## Prerequisites

- Builds container images and edits a continuous integration pipeline
- Has loaded an open-weight model from a hub

## Topics

### Attack surface

- Entry points from weights to skills
- Poisoned and mislabelled artefacts
- Code execution on model load

### Provenance

- Model and dataset cards as evidence
- Bills of materials in open formats
- Build provenance attestations

### Signing and registries

- Signing a manifest of hashed files
- Models as registry artefacts
- Verification at admission

### Licences

- Licences and acceptable-use terms
- Licence policy as code
- Re-checking upstream changes
