# DEV-SEC-401 · Security Architecture for AI Platforms

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Security and Privacy Engineering for AI](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-SEC.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a design review day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 24 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants design and review the security architecture of a shared platform on which many teams run assistants and agents against an organisation's data. For a fictional ministry platform they set an identity for every agent and the person it acts for, least privilege across tools, stores and indexes derived from data classification, isolation tiers matched to code trust and sensitivity, action-level monitoring with kill switches, and the assurance evidence auditors ask for. They critique a rival design and defend a reference architecture before a panel. Building these parts is DEV-AGT-402; sovereign placement is DEV-INF-405.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Design an identity model that binds every agent action to an agent, a delegating person and a scoped grant.
- Design least-privilege access across tools, stores and indexes derived from data classification.
- Decide isolation tiers by code trust, tenant and data sensitivity.
- Design action monitoring that detects unsafe tool-call sequences.
- Prepare a control map to an AI controls framework and national controls.
- Review two competing platform security designs and recommend one.

## Prerequisites

- [DEV-SEC-301 · Securing Language Model and Agent Applications](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-SEC-301.md)
- Has designed or reviewed a production service used by several teams
- Reads OAuth flows and access-control policies

## Topics

### Threat model of a shared platform

- Cross-tenant leakage and confused deputies
- Shared prompt caches and indexes as tenant channels
- Cascading failures and rogue agents
- Insider and supplier threats

### Identity for agents

- Workload identity and attestation
- Token exchange at every hop
- Never deciding access from nested actor claims
- Consent, revocation and immature standards

### Least privilege across tools and data

- Classification-driven policy
- Permission-aware retrieval and index partitioning
- Toxic flows: private data, untrusted content, exits

### Isolation tiers

- Container, user-space kernel and micro virtual machine
- Confidential computing
- Egress architecture and credential proxies

### Monitoring and assurance

- Action-level audit trails
- Kill switches and blast radius
- Control frameworks and evidence packs
- Decision records

---

# DEV-PHY-201 · Sensors, Perception and Compute for Physical AI

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Physical AI and Robotics Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-PHY.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two lab days on a shared sensor kit and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

On a kit with a colour camera, a depth camera, an inertial measurement unit (IMU) and a single-board computer, participants measure sensor noise, calibrate the camera-IMU pair, record synchronised streams, fuse inertial data into an orientation estimate and run a quantised detector within a latency budget, ending with a node that reports object positions in 3D.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain how cameras, depth sensors and inertial units measure, and the main error sources of each.
- Calibrate camera intrinsics and the camera-IMU extrinsics and time offset.
- Implement synchronised recording and an inertial orientation filter with consistent frames.
- Measure the end-to-end latency of a quantised detector on embedded compute, stage by stage.
- Build a real-time node that reports 3D positions of one object class from colour and depth images.

## Prerequisites

- Writes Python with NumPy on Linux
- Uses rotation matrices and Gaussian noise (FND-MTH-101, FND-MTH-103)
- Has run a pretrained image model

## Next courses

- [DEV-PHY-301 · Simulation and Digital Twins for AI Systems](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-PHY-301.md)
- [DEV-PHY-302 · Robot Learning Systems: Data, Policies and Deployment](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-PHY-302.md)

## Topics

### Sensors and their errors

- Pinhole model, distortion and shutters
- Stereo, structured-light, time-of-flight and lidar depth
- IMU bias, noise and drift

### Calibration, time and frames

- Target-based calibration
- Camera-IMU extrinsics and time offset
- Timestamps, synchronisation and transforms

### Fusion

- Complementary and Kalman filters
- Back-projecting detections with depth
- Visual-inertial odometry and mapping in brief

### Real-time perception on embedded compute

- Latency budgets from motion to decision
- Quantised models in an interchange format
- Dropped frames and thermal throttling

---

# DEV-PHY-301 · Simulation and Digital Twins for AI Systems

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Physical AI and Robotics Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-PHY.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants use simulation to produce data and decisions they can trust. They build a simulated arm and conveyor cell, generate labelled synthetic images with domain randomisation, measure how a detector trained on them fares on real public images, fit simulator parameters to logged trajectories of a low-cost arm, and keep a digital twin synchronised with replayed telemetry. The capstone is a validated twin that answers one operational question and states where it must not be used.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Configure a physics simulation of an arm and conveyor cell, choosing time step, contact and solver settings.
- Generate a labelled synthetic image dataset with randomised lighting, texture, pose and camera placement.
- Evaluate the synthetic-to-real gap of a detector and decide the mix of synthetic and real training data.
- Apply system identification to fit the friction, damping and mass of a simulated arm to logged trajectories.
- Build a digital twin that ingests replayed telemetry, stays synchronised and flags divergence from the asset.
- Evaluate a twin against acceptance criteria for one stated use and decide the domain in which its answers hold.

## Prerequisites

- [DEV-PHY-201 · Sensors, Perception and Compute for Physical AI](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-PHY-201.md)
- Trains and evaluates a neural network, as taught in DEV-MLE-202
- Reads basic rigid-body mechanics: mass, friction, torque

## Topics

### Simulation foundations

- Rigid-body dynamics, contact and friction
- Simulated cameras, depth and inertial noise
- Determinism, seeds, speed and fidelity

### Synthetic data

- Procedural scenes and automatic labels
- Domain randomisation versus photorealism
- Label quality and coverage checks

### Closing the reality gap

- Measuring the gap on real data
- System identification
- Learned simulators and world models in brief

### Digital twins

- Models, shadows and twins
- Asset information models and telemetry synchronisation
- Co-simulation with Functional Mock-up Interface (FMI) units
- What-if analysis and virtual commissioning

### Validation and use

- Validity domains and acceptance criteria
- Comparing simulated and real runs statistically
- Drift between twin and asset

---

# DEV-PHY-302 · Robot Learning Systems: Data, Policies and Deployment

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Physical AI and Robotics Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-PHY.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day at robot stations, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 36 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

In teams of two or three at a station with a low-cost open arm and a leader arm for teleoperation, participants collect and audit demonstrations, train an imitation policy, fine-tune a small pretrained action model, evaluate both over many trials in simulation and on the arm, and deploy the better one with a timed control loop, limits and a stop. Methods research belongs to SPC-GEN-401 and safety cases to DEV-PHY-401; this course is about data, evaluation and deployment.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Collect teleoperated demonstrations and audit them for synchronisation, task success and coverage of starting conditions.
- Train an imitation policy and fine-tune a small pretrained action model on the same data at matched compute.
- Evaluate policies with randomised starting conditions and enough trials to separate them.
- Deploy a policy with a control loop that meets its rate, enforces joint, workspace and speed limits and stops on command.
- Diagnose the dominant failure of a deployed policy and decide what data to collect next.

## Prerequisites

- [DEV-PHY-201 · Sensors, Perception and Compute for Physical AI](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-PHY-201.md)
- Trains and debugs a neural network, as taught in DEV-MLE-202
- Has run a physics simulation; DEV-PHY-301 is recommended

## Topics

### Robot learning as a system

- Observation and action spaces, control rates and latency
- Where learned policies fail: contact, long horizons, novelty
- Control, imitation or reinforcement learning

### Demonstration data

- Teleoperation with leader arms, phones and headsets
- Episodes, synchronisation and dataset formats
- Quality audits, coverage and licences

### Policies

- Behaviour cloning and compounding error
- Action chunking and diffusion policies
- Fine-tuning pretrained vision-language-action models

### Evaluation

- Trial protocols, randomised starts and seeds
- Success rates with confidence intervals
- Simulation benchmarks versus real trials

### Deployment

- Inference latency and asynchronous action execution
- Limits, watchdogs and stops
- Logging for replay and collecting corrections

---

# DEV-PHY-401 · Safety Engineering for Autonomous Systems

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Physical AI and Robotics Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-PHY.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Workshop: two days of analysis and simulation labs, ending in a defended safety case
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

On a synthetic warehouse vehicle with learned perception, participants analyse hazards, specify the operational design domain, write a safety case linked to test evidence, fault-test a runtime monitor, measure human takeover in simulation and turn a public incident into new hazards and tests.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Apply system-theoretic hazard analysis to a system with learned perception and specify its operational design domain.
- Build a structured safety case linking claims to test evidence, with its defeaters.
- Design and fault-test a runtime monitor and fallback that keep the system in its safety envelope.
- Measure human takeover time and mode errors and derive interface requirements.
- Review a published incident and decide the changes to hazards, tests and the safety case.

## Prerequisites

- DEV-PHY-301, DEV-PHY-302, or work on a system that senses and acts
- Edits Python simulation scripts
- Has applied a risk assessment method (LDS-AIG-204)

## Topics

### Learned components and safety

- Functional safety and safety of the intended functionality
- Distribution shift and specification gaps
- IEC 61508, ISO 26262, ISO 21448, ISO/PAS 8800, UL 4600, ISO 3691-4

### Hazard analysis

- Fault trees and failure modes and effects
- System-Theoretic Process Analysis (STPA)
- Operational design domains and triggering conditions

### Safety cases and runtime assurance

- Goal Structuring Notation (GSN) and defeaters
- Scenario-based testing and domain coverage
- Simplex architectures and safety filters
- Out-of-distribution monitors

### Oversight and incidents

- Takeover time and mode confusion
- Automation bias and nominal oversight
- Just culture and incident feedback into tests

# DEV-PRJ-301 · AI Engineering Practicum

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Practicums](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-PRJ.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Practicum: about eight weeks part-time in teams of three to five for a sponsoring organisation, with weekly engineer reviews, two gates and a sponsor defence
- Total hours: 100 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Teams take one problem from a sponsoring government entity, company or non-profit to a shipped system in about eight weeks. They agree a specification and acceptance criteria with the sponsor, build in weekly iterations reviewed by experienced engineers, evaluate against the criteria, harden the system after another team attacks it, and hand it over with an operations plan. Sponsor data enters only as an anonymised extract or a synthetic replica of the sponsor's schema.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Draft a scoped specification with acceptance criteria, an initial evaluation set and an out-of-scope list.
- Prepare a data-handling plan that classifies the sponsor's data, replaces personal data and states what may reach which model.
- Build and ship a working AI system in weekly iterations with tests and human review of every merged change.
- Evaluate the system against the acceptance criteria with error analysis and a regression gate.
- Review the system's security with a threat model and another team's attack, and fix the highest risks.
- Deliver an operations plan and hand-over that the sponsor's team can run alone.

## Prerequisites

- DEV-LLM-201 and DEV-EVL-301, or has built and evaluated a language model application
- DEV-OPS-201, or has deployed a monitored container service
- DEV-SWE-201, or works in Git with coding agents, reviews and continuous integration

## Topics

### Engagement and scoping

- Sponsor agreements and intellectual property
- Discovery interviews and walk-throughs
- Acceptance criteria as the contract

### Team delivery

- Weekly iterations and demonstrations
- Coding agents with review proportionate to risk
- Tests, continuous integration and decision records

### Data and governance

- Classification and personal data
- Anonymised extracts and synthetic replicas
- Impact assessment and system card

### Quality and security

- Error analysis and regression gates
- Acceptance sessions with end users
- Threat modelling and a cross-team attack day

### Operations and hand-over

- Service objectives and monitoring
- Cost per successful task
- Runbooks, rollback and ownership

---

# DEV-PRJ-401 · AI Systems Capstone: Production Readiness Review

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [Practicums](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/DEV-PRJ.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Studio: about eight weeks part-time, an individual review of an existing AI system with four coached rounds and a panel defence
- Total hours: 60 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Each participant takes one existing AI system through a production readiness review and decides whether it may go live. The system is a sanitised copy from the participant's organisation, the DEV-PRJ-301 system, or an Academy reference system with seeded weaknesses, run in a sandbox. Participants reconstruct its architecture, load-test and fault-inject it against service objectives, cost it per successful outcome, threat-model and probe it, audit its governance evidence, and defend a go, conditional-go or no-go decision before a panel.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Evaluate the architecture against its requirements and reconstruct the key decisions and risks.
- Evaluate reliability against service objectives for latency and quality under load and injected faults.
- Audit cost per successful outcome and identify the largest cost levers.
- Audit security with a threat model and targeted tests of model, data, tool and supply-chain paths.
- Review governance evidence for classification, personal data, impact assessment, oversight, incidents and retirement.
- Decide go, conditional go or no-go and defend the decision and its conditions before a panel.

## Prerequisites

- DEV-PRJ-301, or has shipped and operated an AI system people depend on
- Two of DEV-OPS-401, DEV-SEC-301, DEV-EVL-401 and DEV-INF-404, or equivalent work
- Writes architecture decision records and reads latency percentiles

## Topics

### The readiness review

- Scope, independence and evidence standards
- Checklists versus judgement
- Findings with severity and owners

### Architecture and reliability

- Decision records
- Service objectives for latency and quality
- Auditing evaluation suites and release gates
- Load testing to a goodput target and fault injection

### Cost and security

- Token, compute and human review costs
- Threat models for model, data and agent paths
- Supply chain, signing and bills of materials

### Governance and operations

- Personal data flows and classification
- System cards and impact assessment
- Oversight, incident response and retirement

### The decision

- Go, conditional go and no-go
- Conditions with owners and dates
- Briefing decision makers

# AE-201 · Machine Learning Foundations and Model Evaluation

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Assistant level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-200.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-201/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-201/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-201/practice.html

## Description

Participants build and evaluate a tabular prediction model the way an engineer would ship it. On synthetic appointment data from a fictional clinic network they frame the prediction, prepare features inside a pipeline, set a baseline, move to regularised linear models and boosted trees, choose a validation scheme that matches time and patient grouping, find and remove planted leakage, pick metrics and a threshold from the cost of each error, analyse errors by slice, and compare two models with an interval rather than a single score. Every result is reproduced from a script with a fixed seed.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish random, grouped and time-ordered validation and state which one each described prediction task requires.
- Prepare a feature pipeline that imputes, encodes and scales inside cross-validation so that no statistic is computed on held-out rows.
- Implement a baseline, a regularised linear model and a gradient-boosted tree model and score each on the same validation splits.
- Analyse a dataset for target leakage and train-test contamination and remove each problem found.
- Compute ranking, threshold and calibration metrics and choose an operating threshold from a stated cost of each error type.
- Analyse errors by subgroup and slice to find where the model fails, then test one data or feature change aimed at the worst slice.
- Evaluate whether a challenger model beats the baseline using a paired comparison with a confidence interval and a stated minimum effect.

## Prerequisites

- [FN-101 · Python for Data and AI Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-101.md)
- [FN-103 · Mathematics for Machine Learning: Vectors, Gradients and Probability](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-103.md)
- [FN-104 · SQL and Data Wrangling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-104.md)
- [FN-105 · How Machine Learning and Language Models Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-105.md)
- Writes Python functions and uses dataframes to filter, join and group a table
- Computes a mean, a variance and a conditional probability by hand

## Next courses

- [AE-202 · Deep Learning and Generative AI Fundamentals](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-202.md)
- [AE-205 · Deploying AI Services: Containers, Serving and Monitoring](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-205.md)
- [AE-309 · Computer Vision Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-309.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Frame and prepare

- A prediction is a decision at a moment
- Baselines before models
- Features in a pipeline
- Time, lags and history

# AE-202 · Deep Learning and Generative AI Fundamentals

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Assistant level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-200.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-202/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-202/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-202/practice.html

## Description

Participants go from tensors to a working generative model and learn what each layer of the stack does. For a fictional crafts cooperative they write a training loop by hand, debug a network that will not learn, adapt a pretrained image model to synthetic textile images, implement attention for a toy sequence, build bilingual semantic search with sentence embeddings, and generate text with a small open-weight model while varying sampling settings. They finish by comparing model families on quality, size, latency, licence and cost for three of the cooperative's use cases.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain how a transformer turns input tokens into next-token probabilities, naming the role of embeddings, attention, the context window and sampling.
- Implement a training loop with a loss, an optimiser, mini-batches and validation checks, and use it to train a small network.
- Apply a debugging checklist to a network whose loss does not fall and correct each fault found.
- Use transfer learning to adapt a pretrained image model to a new label set with little data, and measure the improvement over training from scratch.
- Use sentence embeddings to build and test a bilingual semantic search over product descriptions.
- Measure how temperature, nucleus sampling and the instruction change the outputs of a small open-weight language model.
- Evaluate model families for three stated use cases on quality, size, latency, licence terms and cost, and recommend one per use case.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-201 · Machine Learning Foundations and Model Evaluation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-201.md)
- [FN-103 · Mathematics for Machine Learning: Vectors, Gradients and Probability](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-103.md)
- Multiplies matrices and computes a derivative with the chain rule
- Has trained and evaluated a model with a train, validation and test split

## Next courses

- [AE-309 · Computer Vision Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-309.md)
- [AE-310 · Model Adaptation: Fine-Tuning, Distillation and Small Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-310.md)

- Tensors, shapes and gradients
- Writing the training loop
- Learning rates, batches and regularisation
- When training goes wrong

### Day 2: Vision and transfer

- Convolutions and what they detect
- Pretrained backbones

- Evaluating a deep model

# AE-203 · Building Applications on Language Models

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Assistant level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-200.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-203/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-203/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-203/practice.html

## Description

Participants build a bilingual rider assistant for a fictional transit authority on top of any language model, hosted or open-weight. They call models through a provider-neutral interface, extract validated structured data from rider messages, add tool calls to a synthetic trip-status service, ground answers in a policy corpus with citations and abstention, write a small evaluation set and run the assistant against it, and add input and output checks for personal data and instruction-like text. The result is a small tested web service.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compare the main model API shapes and identify what changes in code when an application switches provider or moves to a local model.
- Implement structured extraction from free-text messages with schema validation, bounded retries and a fallback path.
- Implement tool calling for two services with typed arguments, argument validation and handling of tool errors.
- Implement a grounded answering step that retrieves policy passages, cites them and declines when the corpus holds no answer.
- Prepare a small evaluation set and measure the assistant with code-based checks and one model-graded check validated against labels.
- Configure input and output checks for personal data, off-topic requests and instruction-like text inside retrieved content.
- Build a bilingual assistant service that combines structured extraction, tool calls and grounded answers behind a tested API.

## Prerequisites

- [FN-101 · Python for Data and AI Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-101.md)
- [FN-102 · Command Line, Git and Reproducible Projects](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-102.md)
- [FN-105 · How Machine Learning and Language Models Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-105.md)
- Calls a web API from Python and handles JSON

- [AE-304 · Retrieval and Knowledge Engineering for Language Model Systems](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-304.md)
- [AE-305 · Operating Machine Learning and Language Model Systems](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-305.md)
- [AE-310 · Model Adaptation: Fine-Tuning, Distillation and Small Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-310.md)
- [AE-311 · Shaping the Build: Product Sense and Delivery Practice](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-311.md)
- [AE-312 · AI Cost Engineering and Model Routing](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-312.md)

## Format and days

- Tokens, context and cost
- Three API shapes, one interface

# AE-204 · Software Engineering with Coding Agents

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Assistant level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-200.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-204/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-204/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-204/practice.html

## Description

Participants build and change software by directing coding agents while staying accountable for every merged line. On the booking-service repository of a fictional government digital-services unit, they read and debug code by hand, write a specification and a plan before delegating, make the repository agent-ready with a short context file, a skill and test commands, run an agent with scoped permissions in an isolated worktree, review its changes by risk, add property-based and mutation tests, scan generated code and dependencies for vulnerabilities, and gate everything in continuous integration. One assessed checkpoint is done without AI.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Analyse an unfamiliar code base by hand to trace a request path and locate the cause of a failing test.
- Draft a specification with acceptance criteria and a plan of small, verifiable steps before delegating work to an agent.
- Configure a repository for agent work with a short context file, one reusable skill, scoped permissions and commands for tests and linting.
- Test agent-written code with unit, property-based and mutation tests and report what the original tests missed.
- Apply a risk-based review checklist to agent pull requests, including security scanning of the change and its dependencies.
- Configure continuous integration that runs tests, type checks, security scans and a dependency audit on every change.
- Deliver a feature through the specify, plan, execute and verify cycle with an agent and defend each design decision to a reviewer.

## Prerequisites

- [FN-101 · Python for Data and AI Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-101.md)
- [FN-102 · Command Line, Git and Reproducible Projects](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-102.md)
- Uses Git branches and pull requests
- Reads and writes Python tests

## Next courses

### Day 2: Make the repository agent-ready

- Context files that stay short
- Skills and hooks
- Permissions, sandboxes and secrets
- Executing in small steps

### Day 3: Verify and review

- Tests as the contract
- Property-based and mutation testing
- Reviewing by risk
- Security of generated code

### Day 4: Integrate and deliver

- Continuous integration as the gate
- Debugging a regression
- Explaining a change

- Searching code and managing context

- Failure modes: over-engineering, stopping short, destructive actions

### Reading code without help

- Debugging with tests and bisection

# AE-205 · Deploying AI Services: Containers, Serving and Monitoring

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Assistant level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-200.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-205/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-205/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-205/practice.html

## Description

Participants take two trained models from a notebook to a monitored service. For a fictional mutual insurer they package a claims-triage classifier and a similar-claims embedding model with pinned dependencies, register model versions, serve them behind a versioned API with input validation, build and scan a container image, run it on a single-node local cluster with health checks, add metrics, structured logs and traces, load-test and size the service, release a new version by canary and roll it back, and detect drift in a replayed stream of claims.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain the path from a trained model to a served prediction, naming the artefact, image, registry, runtime, endpoint and monitor at each step.
- Prepare a model artefact with pinned dependencies, a version, an input and output signature and a reproducible build.
- Implement a versioned prediction API with input validation, typed errors and separate health and readiness checks.
- Configure a container image for the service, scan it for vulnerabilities and run it with resource limits on a single-node cluster.
- Implement metrics, structured logs and traces for the service and a dashboard for latency percentiles, error rate and prediction distribution.
- Measure latency and throughput under load and size workers and replicas to meet a latency objective at the lowest cost.
- Deliver a new model version by canary release, decide on promotion or rollback from monitored metrics and detect drift in replayed traffic.

## Prerequisites

- [FN-102 · Command Line, Git and Reproducible Projects](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-102.md)

# AE-206 · Machine Learning Systems on One Machine

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Assistant level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-200.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-206/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-206/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-206/practice.html

## Description

Participants find out where time and memory go between raw data and a served prediction, and fix the largest cost first. For a fictional agritech company they profile a data pipeline and a training step, estimate memory from weights, activations, optimiser state and the key-value cache, apply mixed precision, batching, quantisation and pruning, export a model to a portable runtime, and benchmark latency, throughput and quality with repeated runs and intervals. Labs run on a laptop CPU, with an optional free notebook GPU, and every speed-up must be measured and checked for loss of quality.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain how compute, memory capacity and memory bandwidth limit training and inference, and identify which one binds for a described workload.
- Measure where time goes in a data pipeline and a training step with profilers and timers, and remove the largest bottleneck.
- Compute the memory needed for weights, activations, optimiser state and the key-value cache and check each estimate against measured peak memory.
- Apply mixed precision, batching and compilation and report their effect on speed, memory and accuracy.
- Apply post-training quantisation and pruning, export the model to a portable runtime and compare size, latency and quality with the original.
- Prepare a benchmark that controls warm-up, repetitions, batch size and input mix, and report percentiles with confidence intervals.
- Optimise a model and its serving path to meet a stated latency and memory budget on a target device while keeping quality within an agreed tolerance.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-202 · Deep Learning and Generative AI Fundamentals](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-202.md)
- Trains a small neural network with a hand-written training loop
- Reads a histogram and computes a percentile

## Next courses

- [AE-307 · Container Orchestration and Cloud Infrastructure for AI Workloads](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-307.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Measure first

- Compute, memory and bandwidth
- Timers, profilers and noise
- Profiling a training step
- Fixing an input-bound pipeline

### Day 2: Memory and training efficiency

- Where memory goes
- Mixed precision
- Accumulation and checkpointing
- Compilation and fusion

### Day 3: Inference and compression

- Latency, throughput and batching
- Language model inference on a laptop
- Quantisation
- Pruning or a smaller model

### Day 4: Export and benchmark

- Export to a portable runtime
- A benchmark you can trust
- Quality must survive
- Budgets and trade-offs

### Day 5: Capstone: an optimisation study and its defence


## Topics

### The physics of a machine

- Compute, memory capacity and bandwidth
- The roofline idea
- Caches and data movement
- CPUs, GPUs and neural accelerators

### Measuring first

- Timers and profilers
- Warm-up and variance
- Percentiles
- Flame graphs
- Memory profiling

### Data pipelines

- File formats and decoding
- Parallel loading and prefetching
- Caching preprocessed data
- Input-bound versus compute-bound

### Training efficiently

- Batch size and throughput
- Mixed precision
- Gradient accumulation
- Activation checkpointing
- Compilation and operator fusion

### Inference

- Latency versus throughput
- Batching
- Key-value cache for language models
- Prefill and decode
- Time to first token and tokens per second

### Compression

- Quantisation formats
- Post-training versus quantisation-aware training
- Pruning
- Distillation at concept level
- Re-evaluating quality after compression

### Portable runtimes and export

- Exchange formats
- Graph optimisation
- Runtimes for CPUs and edge devices
- Runtimes for small language models

### Benchmarking

- Benchmark design
- Repeated runs and intervals
- Goodput against a service objective
- Energy per prediction as an estimate

# AE-207 · Responsible and Secure AI Engineering Practice

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Assistant level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-200.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 21 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-207/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-207/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-207/practice.html

## Description

Participants turn data protection, security and responsible-AI duties into engineering work on one application. For a fictional housing support fund that uses a language model to summarise applicant documents and an eligibility screening model, they convert Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL) obligations into testable requirements, classify every data flow, add masking, pseudonymisation and retention controls, test the assistant against prepared injection and leakage attacks, add basic controls, check the screening model for subgroup errors, record risks in a register using the national framework, and write a system card and a plain-language statement of limits for case officers and applicants. Full attack and hardening work is left to AE-308.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain how PDPL principles, data classification levels and the AI Ethics Principles apply at each stage of a language model application.
- Classify the data flows of an AI application and implement the minimisation, masking and retention controls that follow from the classification.
- Test a language model application against prepared injection and data-leakage cases mapped to a standard risk list, and record which succeed.
- Implement basic controls: separation of untrusted content, output validation, least-privilege tool access and a human approval step for decisions about people.
- Analyse risks including subgroup errors of the screening model and third-party model terms, and record each in a risk register with likelihood, impact, treatment and owner.
- Defend the release conditions of an AI application to non-technical stakeholders using a system card, the risk register and a plain-language statement of limits.

## Prerequisites

- [FN-106 · Responsible Data and AI Practice in the Kingdom](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-106.md)
- [AE-203 · Building Applications on Language Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-203.md)
- Has built, or can read, a small language model application with retrieval
- Can name the four national data classification levels
- Computes error rates from a confusion matrix, as taught in FN-105 or AE-201

## Next courses

- [AE-308 · Securing Language Model and Agent Applications](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-308.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Data duties in a build

- From law to engineering requirements
- Classify before you build
- Minimise, mask and pseudonymise
- Records, retention and deletion

### Day 2: Risks of language model applications

- A risk list for language model applications
- Prompt injection and data leakage
- Basic controls
- Risk assessment with the national framework

### Day 3: Fairness, documentation and stakeholders

- Fairness checks on the screening model
- Third-party models and licences
- System cards
- Communicating limits to stakeholders

### Day 4: Capstone: the responsible-use and security pack


## Topics

### From law and policy to requirements

- Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL) principles for builders
- Lawful basis, purpose and minimisation
- Retention, deletion and data subject rights
- Transfers outside the Kingdom
- Records of processing
- Breach handling and notification duties

### Classification in a build

- The four national classification levels
- Classifying data flows
- What may reach a hosted model
- Masking and pseudonymisation

### Risks of language model applications

- The Open Worldwide Application Security Project (OWASP) Top 10 for LLM Applications
- Prompt injection and data leakage
- Excessive agency and insecure tool use
- Insecure output handling
- The OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications at concept level

### Basic controls

- Separating untrusted content
- Output validation
- Least-privilege tools
- Human approval for decisions about people
- Logging for audit without personal data

### Fairness and risk management

- Subgroup error rates
- Bias categories from the national bias guide
- Risk tiers in the AI Ethics Principles
- The four phases of the national AI risk framework
- Likelihood and impact scoring
- A risk register with owners

### Third-party models

- Licences and acceptable-use terms
- Data-processing terms
- Data residency
- Build or buy notes

### Documentation and communication

- System cards
- Statements of limits for users
- Briefing non-technical stakeholders
- Disclosure that users are talking to AI

# AE-301 · Applied Natural Language Processing Engineering

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-300.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 21 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-301/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-301/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-301/practice.html

## Description

Participants build the language layer of a customer-service system for a fictional regional water utility whose messages arrive in Modern Standard Arabic, Gulf dialect, Arabic written in Latin script and English. They trace text through tokenisers, embeddings and attention, build semantic search, route messages and extract account fields three ways (a classical baseline, a prompted generative model and a fine-tuned encoder), adapt a model with low-rank adapters in free notebook memory, and ship the chosen model as a small service with a model card. Every choice rests on scores by dialect, latency and cost.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain how tokenisation, embeddings and attention turn Arabic and English text into model inputs, and where script, diacritics and dialect break that pipeline.
- Implement semantic search over a bilingual message archive and measure it for each language variety.
- Implement schema-validated extraction of account numbers, districts and complaint types from free text, masking personal fields before text reaches a hosted model.
- Apply low-rank adapter fine-tuning to an encoder within a fixed memory budget and compare it with full fine-tuning.
- Decide among a classical baseline, a prompted generative model and a fine-tuned encoder for message routing.
- Deliver the chosen model as a tested service with a model card that states its limits by language variety.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-202 · Deep Learning and Generative AI Fundamentals](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-202.md)
- Trains a small neural network with a hand-written training loop
- Computes precision, recall and F1 from predictions
- Reads and writes UTF-8 Arabic text in Python

## Next courses

- [AE-408 · Multimodal and Speech Systems Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-408.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Represent

- Tokenisation
- Embeddings and semantic search
- Inside the transformer
- Decision models

### Day 2: Generate

- Generative language models
- Prompting and structured outputs
- Retrieval-augmented generation
- Model selection and evaluation

### Day 3: Adapt

- Fine-tuning data
- Fine-tuning an encoder
- Low-rank and quantised adapters
- Evaluate and deploy

### Day 4: Capstone: a routing and extraction service and its defence


## Topics

### Representing text

- Subword tokenisers and token cost per language
- Normalising alef, hamza, ta marbuta and diacritics
- Dialect and Arabic in Latin script
- Embeddings and vector indexes

### Models for decisions

- Attention, encoders and decoders
- Baselines first
- Classification and token-classification heads
- A prompted model as a zero-shot classifier

### Generation in applications

- Sampling and consistency
- Structured outputs with validation
- Grounding in a rule corpus (depth in AE-304)
- Choosing by quality, latency, cost and licence

### Adapting and shipping

- Splits without leakage
- Full fine-tuning against low-rank and quantised adapters
- CPU latency, a small API and a demo
- Model cards with subgroup results

# AE-302 · Agentic Systems Engineering: Loops, Context and Harnesses

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-300.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-302/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-302/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-302/practice.html

## Description

Participants build an agent as a model in a loop calling typed tools inside a sandbox, with most of the engineering in the harness. For a fictional ports authority they write the loop from scratch, budget the context, add a context file, a skill and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, compare an agent SDK with their own harness, gate bookings in a checkpointed state graph, and ship a traced, evaluated and contained agent behind an API.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Implement a tool-calling agent loop without a framework, with typed tool schemas, a step budget and explicit completion criteria.
- Apply compaction, offloading of tool results and staged loading of skills, and measure the effect on tokens and success.
- Implement a protocol server over a document store and connect the agent to it through capability discovery.
- Design a checkpointed state-graph agent with a human approval gate at a defined risk threshold.
- Evaluate the agent over repeated trials, including runs against a seeded prompt injection.
- Deliver the agent as a traced API service gated by a smoke evaluation in continuous integration.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-203 · Building Applications on Language Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-203.md)
- Writes typed Python and calls a web API that returns JSON
- Runs a container and reads its logs

## Next courses

- [AE-308 · Securing Language Model and Agent Applications](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-308.md)
- [AE-390 · AI Engineering Practicum](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-390.md)
- [AE-404 · Harness Engineering for Long-Running and Multi-Agent Systems](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-404.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: From Model to Agent

- Three API shapes
- Structured outputs
- Tools
- The agent loop from scratch

### Day 2: Context Engineering

- Context as a budget
- Retrieval for agents
- Memory, skills and context files
- Model Context Protocol

### Day 3: Harness and Loop

- Anatomy of a harness
- Agent SDKs and hosted agents
- Loop engineering
- Evaluating agents

### Day 4: Graph and Production

- State graphs with checkpoints
- Several agents and agent-to-agent delegation
- Securing agents
- Production

### Day 5: Capstone: a research agent and its defence


## Topics

### From model to agent

- Typed tool schemas and useful tool errors
- The loop written from scratch
- Completion criteria and step budgets

### Context and protocols

- Context as a budget
- Compaction, offloading and cache-aware layout
- Context files, skills and memory files
- Model Context Protocol, current revision; agent-to-agent delegation as a concept

### Harness and loop

- Tools, context, state and feedback as the harness
- Agent SDKs against an own loop
- Verification inside the loop

### Graphs and several agents

- Checkpoints and interrupts
- Approval at risk thresholds, and approval prompts nobody reads
- When several agents pay

### Securing and shipping

- The agentic risk list of the Open Worldwide Application Security Project (OWASP)

# AE-303 · Evaluation-Driven Development for Language Model Applications

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-300.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-303/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-303/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-303/practice.html

## Description

Participants treat evaluation as the specification of a language model application. Working on one synthetic case, a bilingual service assistant for a fictional licensing office, they read traces, name the failure modes, turn them into code-based checks and calibrated model-graded checks, evaluate an agent over repeated trials, compare two configurations with a sound statistical test, and wire the suite into a regression gate. Every number a participant reports comes from a run they executed.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish code-based checks, model-graded checks and human review, and state when each is the cheapest reliable instrument.
- Carry out open and axial coding of traces to produce a failure taxonomy with counts.
- Implement code-based evaluators for structure, grounding and policy rules.
- Calibrate a model-graded evaluator against human labels and report its agreement with an interval.
- Evaluate an agent on multi-step tasks for outcome and consistency over repeated trials.
- Decide between two configurations using a paired comparison with its uncertainty, cost and latency.
- Build a regression gate that blocks a change when a critical failure mode gets worse.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-203 · Building Applications on Language Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-203.md)
- Reads a confusion matrix and computes precision and recall
- Has run a test suite in continuous integration

## Next courses

- [AE-390 · AI Engineering Practicum](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-390.md)
- [AE-404 · Harness Engineering for Long-Running and Multi-Agent Systems](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-404.md)
- [AE-405 · Evaluation Programmes and Release Decisions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-405.md)
- [AE-406 · Post-Training Open Models on Domain Data](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-406.md)
- [AE-407 · AI Assurance, Red Teaming and Governance for Engineering Leads](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-407.md)
- [AE-408 · Multimodal and Speech Systems Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-408.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: See the failures

- Evaluation is the specification
- Traces are the raw material
- Open coding
- From codes to a failure taxonomy

### Day 2: Build the instruments

- Checks you can write in code
- Grounding and citation checks
- Model graders with binary criteria
- Calibrating a grader against people

### Day 3: Agents and comparisons

- Grading a transcript and an outcome
- Consistency over repeated trials
- Is B better than A
- Cost and latency belong in the decision

### Day 4: Gate the release

- Golden sets, versions and leakage
- A regression gate in continuous integration
- From offline suites to online monitoring
- Reporting results people can act on

### Day 5: Capstone: an evaluation suite and its release gate


## Topics

### Evaluation as specification

- Non-determinism and the gap between intent and behaviour
- Benchmarks versus application evaluations
- What a leaderboard does not tell you

### Error analysis

- Sampling traces
- Open and axial coding
- Failure taxonomies and saturation
- Prioritising by frequency and severity

### Evaluators

- Assertions and reference-based checks
- Binary criteria for model graders
- Calibration against human labels
- Correcting pass rates for grader error

### Agents and retrieval

- Grading transcript and outcome
- Consistency over repeated trials
- Groundedness and citation checks
- Arabic test sets

### Comparing and deciding

- Paired comparisons and bootstrap intervals
- Sample size and minimum effect
- Cost, latency and quality as one decision

### Evaluation in delivery

- Golden sets and leakage
- Regression gates
- Online monitoring and review queues
- Privacy of traces

# AE-304 · Retrieval and Knowledge Engineering for Language Model Systems

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-300.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-304/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-304/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-304/practice.html

## Description

Participants build and measure the retrieval layer of a language model system for a fictional university: bilingual regulations, study plans with tables, scanned Arabic circulars and an enrolment statistics warehouse. Starting from a graded test set, they build lexical, dense, hybrid and reranked search with Arabic normalisation, parse and chunk documents by structure, filter by date and role, give an agent search tools and a small knowledge graph, and answer statistical questions through a semantic layer instead of free text-to-SQL.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare a retrieval test set with graded relevance judgements and compute standard ranking metrics for each language.
- Implement lexical, dense, hybrid and reranked search with Arabic normalisation and compare them on quality and latency.
- Analyse parsing and chunking choices by scoring two parsers and two chunking schemes.
- Build retrieval that never returns a document the requester may not see or a superseded rule.
- Design an agentic search component that chooses among search tools and a small knowledge graph within a context budget.
- Evaluate free text-to-SQL against a semantic layer with validated SQL and decide which to ship.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-202 · Deep Learning and Generative AI Fundamentals](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-202.md)
- [AE-203 · Building Applications on Language Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-203.md)
- Writes SQL joins and aggregations
- Computes precision and recall
- Has built a small grounded application with citations

## Next courses

- [AE-390 · AI Engineering Practicum](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-390.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Measure and search

- Retrieval is measured on its own
- Lexical search and Arabic text
- Dense retrieval and embedding choice
- Hybrid search and reranking

### Day 2: Prepare the corpus

- Parsing is a separate problem
- Chunking by structure
- Dates, versions and duplicates
- Permissions in the index

### Day 3: Agentic search and knowledge

- Search as tools for an agent
- Multi-step questions
- Paging and offloading
- Knowledge graphs for linked facts

### Day 4: Structured data and diagnosis

- Questions over a warehouse
- Semantic layers and validated SQL
- Cost, latency and freshness
- Diagnosing failures by component

### Day 5: Capstone project presentations


## Topics

### Measuring retrieval

- Graded relevance and pooling
- Recall at k, reciprocal rank and discounted gain
- Slicing by language and query type

### Search methods

- Inverted indexes and BM25
- Arabic normalisation and light stemming
- Multilingual embeddings and approximate nearest-neighbour indexes
- Rank fusion and cross-encoder reranking

### Preparing a corpus

- Parsing right-to-left text and tables
- Small specialised parsing models against general vision models
- Chunking by structure
- Effective dates and deduplication

### Agentic search and knowledge

- The cheapest tool that works first
- Iterative search and query decomposition
- Paging and offloading large results
- Knowledge graphs for multi-hop questions

### Structured data, access and trust

- Schema grounding and semantic layers
- Validating generated SQL
- Permission filters before ranking
- Retrieved text as untrusted input

# AE-305 · Operating Machine Learning and Language Model Systems

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-300.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-305/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-305/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-305/practice.html

## Description

Participants run three systems of a fictional electricity distribution company in production: a fault-risk classifier retrained on monthly batches with planted drift, a field-crew assistant with retrieval and two tools, and an outage-ticket agent. They version everything that changes behaviour as one release unit, build pipelines with validation and promotion gates, release through canary stages with automatic rollback, trace requests, monitor drift and online quality, and keep the agent alive through crashes and runaway loops. Evaluators come ready-made from AE-303.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare a release manifest that versions data, code, configuration, model, prompt, retrieval index and tool schemas as one unit.
- Build a retraining pipeline, started by a drift or schedule trigger, with data validation and a promotion gate that compares challenger and champion overall and by region.
- Deliver language model changes through an evaluation gate and a canary stage with an automatic rollback trigger.
- Configure request tracing, drift monitors and online evaluation with a review queue, and tune alert thresholds.
- Diagnose an agent incident by replaying recorded traces and fix it with idempotent tools, durable state or a budget.
- Measure cost per successful outcome and resource use for each system and set budget alerts.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-205 · Deploying AI Services: Containers, Serving and Monitoring](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-205.md)
- [AE-203 · Building Applications on Language Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-203.md)
- Builds a container image and a continuous-integration workflow
- Reads an evaluation report with pass rates and intervals
- Has built a tool-calling agent, as in AE-302 or equivalent

## Next courses

- [AE-390 · AI Engineering Practicum](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-390.md)

- [AE-405 · Evaluation Programmes and Release Decisions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-405.md)

- What changes behaviour
- Registries and lineage
- Pipelines with validation
- Promotion gates

### Day 2: Deliver

- Continuous delivery for models
- Language model releases
- Shadow and canary on evidence
- Cost and capacity signals

- Tracing requests end to end
- Drift, skew and delayed labels
- Online evaluation and review queues

- Durable execution and safe retries

# AE-306 · Modern Data Engineering

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-300.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-306/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-306/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-306/practice.html

## Description

Participants build one batch pipeline end to end for Qafila, the fictional trading company of the Academy's data engineering course, whose margin report nobody trusts. They query raw extracts with analytical SQL, ingest an API and a database change feed incrementally, clean with dataframes, model a star schema with a slowly changing supplier dimension, write tested transformations and a data contract, orchestrate them, and land the result in an open table format that a second engine reads. Day four adds distributed processing, streaming and governance.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Analyse raw transactional extracts with analytical SQL, including window functions and incremental predicates.
- Implement incremental ingestion from an API and a change feed, keeping supplier history as a slowly changing dimension.
- Design a dimensional model at a stated grain and build it as tested, version-controlled transformations.
- Build an orchestrated pipeline with a data contract, quality gates, retries and backfills that fails safely when an upstream feed breaks.
- Configure an open table format with partitioning, schema evolution and time travel, and read it from a second engine.
- Classify every field under the national classification levels and apply minimisation, masking and access rules.

## Prerequisites

- [FN-102 · Command Line, Git and Reproducible Projects](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-102.md)
- [FN-104 · SQL and Data Wrangling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FN-104.md)
- Writes SQL joins, grouping and simple window functions
- Filters and joins tables with a Python dataframe library
- Commits with Git from a shell

## Format and days

### Day 1: Store and query

- Platform shapes
- Analytical SQL on a single node
- Window functions
- Columnar files and partitioning

### Day 2: Ingest and clean

- Ingesting from APIs
- Declarative ingestion pipelines
- Change data capture, merge and history
- Cleaning with dataframes

### Day 3: Model and test

- Dimensional modelling
- Transformations as code
- Data quality tests and contracts
- Orchestration

### Day 4: Scale and production

- Open table formats
- Distributed processing when measured
- Streaming fundamentals
- Governance with PDPL and NDMO

### Day 5: Capstone: the margin mart and its defence


## Topics

### Platform shapes and analytical SQL

- Transactional and analytical systems; extract, load, transform (ELT)
- Lakehouse, layered refinement and columnar files

### Ingestion and change

- Schema drift and idempotent loads
- Change data capture (CDC), merge and slowly changing dimensions
- Single node first, distributed when measured

### Modelling, transformation and contracts

- Grain, facts and dimensions
- Tests, environments and state-aware builds
- Data contracts in an open standard
- Verifying agent-written transformations

### Orchestration, scale and streaming

- Assets, retries and backfills
- Lineage as events
- Open table formats: snapshots, schema evolution, deletion vectors, compaction
- Logs and queues, delivery guarantees, watermarks

### Governance in the pipeline

- Classification levels; Restricted, which older texts call Confidential
- Minimisation and masking under the Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL)
- Erasure requests against history tables and snapshots
- National Data Management Office (NDMO) quality and architecture controls

# AE-307 · Container Orchestration and Cloud Infrastructure for AI Workloads

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-300.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-307/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-307/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-307/practice.html

## Description

Participants run the shared AI platform of a fictional regional health authority, where a training team, a bilingual patient-letter assistant and a nightly embedding job compete for scarce accelerators. On single-node clusters with simulated accelerators, small open-weight models and recorded traffic, they allocate and share devices, admit jobs fairly under quotas, place distributed jobs all at once, autoscale inference on the signals users feel, route requests through an inference-aware gateway, keep Restricted workloads on permitted nodes, and size capacity and cost for three hosting options. The requirements of the public Kubernetes AI conformance checklist that a simulated cluster can demonstrate serve as the acceptance rubric. Token-level cost and model routing are AE-312.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Configure accelerator allocation, sharing and health tainting for two tenants on a container cluster.
- Configure queues, quotas, borrowing and all-or-nothing admission for three teams.
- Optimise autoscaling of an inference service on a queue or service-objective metric, including scale to zero and cold start.
- Evaluate an inference-aware gateway against round-robin routing for goodput, latency and fairness between tenants.
- Compute memory, concurrency, replica count, power and monthly cost for a serving workload under cloud, on-premises and sovereign-provider options.
- Design a placement policy driven by data classification and audit the cluster against the conformance checklist.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-205 · Deploying AI Services: Containers, Serving and Monitoring](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-205.md)
- [AE-206 · Machine Learning Systems on One Machine](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-206.md)

## Next courses

- Accelerator metrics

### Day 2: Queues, quotas and placement

- Admission before scheduling
- Borrowing and preemption
- Gang and topology-aware placement
- Placement under data rules

- Why processor load is the wrong signal

- Inference-aware gateways
- Priority and load shedding
- Capacity from first principles
- Cloud, on-premises or sovereign

### Day 5: Capstone: a hardened cluster and its design review


## Topics

### Accelerators as cluster resources

- Device plugins versus dynamic resource allocation
- Time-slicing, partitioning and virtualised devices
- Device health, taints and per-accelerator metrics

- Preemption and fairness between teams

# AE-308 · Securing Language Model and Agent Applications

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-300.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-308/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-308/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-308/practice.html

## Description

Participants attack and then defend a working agent: a synthetic clearance assistant for a fictional port authority that reads importers' emails and invoices, searches a tariff knowledge base, remembers each importer, runs code to compute duties and acts through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. They threat-model it, run injection, exfiltration and poisoning attacks over repeated trials, then contain it with a sandbox and egress rules, scoped short-lived delegated tokens, separated privileged and quarantined model calls, measured guardrails and approvals placed where a person adds safety. Red-team programmes are AE-407.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare a threat model with data flows, trust boundaries and threats mapped to recognised risk lists and adversary-technique catalogues.
- Test the application with direct, indirect, memory and tool-poisoning attacks in Arabic and English over repeated trials.
- Design containment for generated code and outbound actions with a sandbox, an egress allowlist and recipient rules.
- Build delegated authorisation in which each tool call carries an exchanged token with one audience, a narrow scope and a short lifetime.
- Configure input guardrails and output validation and measure their false-positive and false-negative rates.
- Defend a residual-risk statement after another team attacks the hardened agent, with each confirmed finding turned into a regression test.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-207 · Responsible and Secure AI Engineering Practice](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-207.md)
- [AE-302 · Agentic Systems Engineering: Loops, Context and Harnesses](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-302.md)
- Has built a tool-calling agent and read its traces
- Runs containers locally and changes their network settings

## Next courses

- [AE-390 · AI Engineering Practicum](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-390.md)
- [AE-402 · AI Solution Architecture and Platform Design](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-402.md)
- [AE-407 · AI Assurance, Red Teaming and Governance for Engineering Leads](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-407.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Model the threats

- A fooled model must break nothing important
- Data flows and trust boundaries
- Risk lists and technique catalogues
- Scoring and choosing what to test

### Day 2: Attack

- Direct and indirect injection
- Exfiltration paths
- Memory and retrieval poisoning
- Hostile tools

### Day 3: Contain

- Sandboxes for generated code
- Egress rules as capability grants
- Delegated authorisation
- Privileged and quarantined calls

### Day 4: Guard, approve and verify

- Guardrails and their error rates
- Validating outputs and tool arguments
- Approvals that people can judge
- Audit logs and regression suites

### Day 5: Capstone: red-team day and live defence


## Topics

### Threat modelling agents

- Data-flow diagrams and trust boundaries
- Private data, untrusted content and exit paths
- Model as component versus model as actor
- Risk lists, technique catalogues and scoring

### Attacks

- Direct, indirect and cross-modal injection
- Exfiltration through links, tool arguments and permitted paths
- Memory, retrieval and tool poisoning
- Success rates over repeated trials

### Containment

- Sandboxes for generated code
- An egress allowlist is a capability grant
- Read-only mounts and resolving links before path checks
- Privileged and quarantined model calls

### Identity and authorisation

- OAuth-based delegation and token exchange
- Audience, scope and lifetime
- Token passthrough and the confused deputy
- Credentials kept outside the agent's reach

### Guardrails, approvals and audit

- Classifiers and their two error rates
- Schema and policy checks on tool arguments
- Approval fatigue and where a person adds safety
- Rate limits, spend caps and a kill switch
- Action logs and security regression suites

# AE-309 · Computer Vision Engineering

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-300.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-309/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-309/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-309/practice.html

## Description

Participants build vision systems for a fictional municipal roads and traffic department that must keep working in glare, dust, rain and at night. On public road-damage images and synthetic traffic-camera clips they audit and extend annotations, fine-tune convolutional and transformer backbones, train a pothole detector and a crack segmenter, track and count vehicles, and fit the chosen model to the latency and memory budget of a processor-only roadside unit. Each lab ends with a test under changed lighting, blur or camera position. Vision-language models and multimodal applications are AE-408.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare an image dataset with annotation guidelines, an agreement check, splits that keep each road segment in one split, and augmentations that preserve label meaning.
- Implement transfer learning with two pretrained backbones and compare them by condition slice with intervals.
- Build a detector and a segmenter and diagnose their errors by type to choose the next improvement.
- Measure tracking and counting accuracy for vehicles crossing a line in video.
- Optimise a model to a per-frame latency and memory budget on a processor through export, input resolution and quantisation, re-measuring accuracy at each step.
- Evaluate the model under corruption and camera shift and decide whether to release it.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-201 · Machine Learning Foundations and Model Evaluation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-201.md)
- [AE-202 · Deep Learning and Generative AI Fundamentals](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-202.md)
- Trains a neural network with a hand-written training loop
- Computes precision and recall from a confusion matrix

## Format and days

### Day 1: Visual data first

- How vision systems fail in the field
- Annotation guidelines and agreement
- Leakage by site and near-duplicates
- Augmentation and what it assumes

### Day 2: Backbones and transfer

- Convolutional networks and vision transformers
- How much to fine-tune
- Zero-shot baselines
- Licences of open-weight backbones

### Day 3: Detect, segment and track

- Detection and its metrics
- Detector error analysis
- Segmenting cracks
- Tracking and counting

### Day 4: Fit the budget and release

- Export to an interchange format
- Resolution and precision against latency
- Corruption and shift tests
- Privacy and monitoring in the field

### Day 5: Capstone: a service that meets its budget, defended on a failure


## Topics

### Visual data

- Boxes, masks and annotation formats
- Guidelines, agreement and label noise
- Near-duplicates and leakage by site
- Augmentation and what it assumes

### Backbones and transfer

- Convolutional networks and vision transformers
- Linear probe, partial and full fine-tuning
- Open-vocabulary models as zero-shot baselines
- Licences of open-weight backbones

### Detection, segmentation and video

- Non-maximum suppression and average precision
- Semantic and instance segmentation and overlap metrics
- Tracking by detection and identity switches
- Counting rules

### Deployment constraints

- Export to an interchange format
- Resolution, batch size and numeric precision
- Latency and memory on processors and accelerators

### Field reliability and privacy

- Corruption and camera-shift tests
- Monitoring camera drift
- Blurring faces and plates before storage
- Model cards for vision systems
