# AE-310 · Model Adaptation: Fine-Tuning, Distillation and Small Models

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-300.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-310/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-310/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-310/practice.html

## Description

Participants decide when adapting a model is worth it and then do it well. For a fictional chamber of commerce whose bilingual registration requests must stay on its own servers, a prompted small open-weight model fails at field extraction and tool calls. They sort the failures, set a stronger prompted baseline, build a tuning set from traces, staff corrections and filtered teacher outputs, train low-rank adapters, distil a larger model's tool-call behaviour, evaluate against the base and a larger prompted model, and serve the result quantised with several adapters. AE-301 introduces adapters on an encoder; post-training at scale is AE-406.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Analyse the failures of a prompted model and assign each failure class to prompting, retrieval, tuning or distillation.
- Prepare a tuning dataset from traces, corrections and teacher outputs, with template rendering, verifier filtering, deduplication, decontamination and personal-data removal.
- Configure and train low-rank adapters on a 16-bit and a 4-bit base model within the memory of one free-tier GPU.
- Evaluate the adapted model against the base and a larger prompted model with paired statistics, language slices, regression and safety checks.
- Deploy a quantised small model with several adapters and measure throughput, latency and cost per thousand requests.
- Decide whether to ship the adapted model, weighing quality, cost, licence terms and data placement.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-202 · Deep Learning and Generative AI Fundamentals](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-202.md)
- [AE-203 · Building Applications on Language Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-203.md)
- Fine-tunes a pretrained model with a training loop or a training library
- Compares two systems on an evaluation set with a paired test

## Next courses

- [AE-406 · Post-Training Open Models on Domain Data](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-406.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Decide whether to adapt

- Prompt, retrieve, tune or distil
- The baseline tuning must beat
- Licences and terms of open-weight models
- Cost and placement of the options

### Day 2: Data for tuning

- Tuning data from traces and corrections
- Teacher generation and verifier filtering
- Chat templates and tool-call formats
- Deduplication, decontamination and personal data

### Day 3: Train adapters and distil

- Low-rank adapters
- Quantised adapters and memory
- Settings that matter
- Distilling a behaviour

### Day 4: Evaluate and serve

- Paired evaluation against the base
- Regressions and safety after tuning
- One base, several adapters
- Cards and the decision memo

### Day 5: Capstone: an adapted small model and its defence


## Topics

### When to adapt

- Prompt, retrieve, tune or distil
- Tuning changes behaviour more than knowledge
- Narrow tasks small models suit and multi-step work they do not
- Licences and acceptable-use terms
- Cost and placement of each option

### Data for tuning

- Traces and staff corrections
- Teacher generation with verifier filtering
- Chat templates and tool-call formats
- Deduplication, decontamination and personal data

### Adapters and distillation

- Low-rank and quantised adapters
- Rank, learning rate and schedule
- Distilling a behaviour from a larger model

### Evaluating adapted models

- Paired comparison with the base and a larger model
- Arabic and English slices
- Forgetting and regressions
- Safety behaviour after tuning

### Serving small models

- Quantised weight formats
- Several adapters on one base model
- Throughput and cost per thousand requests

# AE-311 · Shaping the Build: Product Sense and Delivery Practice

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-300.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 21 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-311/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-311/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-311/practice.html

## Description

Participants practise the engineer's part in deciding what to build. In a role-played engagement with a fictional regional water utility that asks for an AI assistant for leak reports, they interview call-centre and field staff about what happened last week, map the workflow and its exceptions, choose and reject use cases, write the specification as the main deliverable with acceptance criteria as evaluation cases, test the riskiest assumption with a thin prototype built with a coding agent, cost the value case, brief the utility's leadership and hand over a system the utility's own team can run.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Analyse a requested AI use case through interviews about past behaviour and a workflow map, and restate the problem where the evidence differs from the request.
- Draft a specification with users, non-goals, constraints, data classification and acceptance criteria written as evaluation cases.
- Test the riskiest assumption with a thin prototype and role-played user sessions.
- Build a value case with cost per successful task, ranges for uncertain inputs and a break-even point, and decide whether to proceed.
- Deliver a recommendation and a hand-over package to non-technical leadership and the receiving team.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-203 · Building Applications on Language Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-203.md)
- [AE-204 · Software Engineering with Coding Agents](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-204.md)
- Has built and demonstrated a working language model application
- Writes a short technical document for a non-technical reader

## Next courses

- [AE-390 · AI Engineering Practicum](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-390.md)
- [AE-402 · AI Solution Architecture and Platform Design](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-402.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Discover

- The engineer's job before code
- Interviews about past behaviour
- Workflows and their exceptions
- Choosing the problem

### Day 2: Specify and test

- Specification as the deliverable
- Acceptance criteria as evaluation cases
- Data, permissions and classification
- Prototype the riskiest assumption

### Day 3: Decide, communicate and hand over

- Minimum viable decisions
- The value case
- Talking to leaders
- Hand-over

### Day 4: Capstone project presentations


## Topics

### Discovery

- Interviews about past behaviour
- Workflows and their exceptions
- Choosing and rejecting use cases

### Specification as the deliverable

- Problem, users and non-goals
- Acceptance criteria as evaluation cases
- Data, permissions and classification

### Minimum viable decisions

- Riskiest assumption first
- Reversible and irreversible choices
- Decision records

### Value and communication

- Cost per successful task and break-even
- Ranges instead of point estimates
- Updates for leaders
- Saying what the system cannot do

### Hand-over

- Runbooks and evaluation sets
- Ownership and exit criteria
- Training the receiving team

# AE-312 · AI Cost Engineering and Model Routing

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-300.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 21 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-312/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-312/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-312/practice.html

## Description

Participants make the cost of language model applications measurable, attributable and smaller without losing quality. For a fictional telecom operator running three applications behind one gateway, a bilingual care assistant, a call-summary job and a billing-dispute agent, they work from a month of synthetic usage traces: they model cost per request and session, attribute spend to teams, set budgets, evaluate model tiers and reasoning settings on their own tasks, route with fallbacks, measure prefix and semantic caches, compare hosted and self-hosted serving and report cost per successful outcome. Cluster capacity planning is AE-307; engine-level optimisation is AE-401.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compute cost per request and per session from prompt, output and cached tokens, retries, agent steps and accelerator-hours.
- Configure attribution, budgets and limits per team, application and environment on a model gateway.
- Evaluate model tiers, reasoning settings and a routing policy on the operator's own tasks, choosing by cost per successful outcome at a fixed quality floor.
- Measure how prefix and semantic caching change cost, latency and answer correctness, including isolation between customers.
- Decide between hosted APIs and a self-hosted open-weight model with a break-even analysis that includes utilisation and data-placement rules.
- Deliver a cost review with three measured savings options to engineering and finance stakeholders.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-203 · Building Applications on Language Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-203.md)
- [AE-205 · Deploying AI Services: Containers, Serving and Monitoring](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-205.md)
- Groups and joins usage logs with SQL or dataframes
- Has run an evaluation set against a language model application

## Format and days

### Day 1: Where the money goes

- The token cost model
- Agents, retries and long contexts
- Attribution and showback
- Budgets and limits

### Day 2: Route and cache

- Own tasks, several settings
- Routing and cascades
- Prompt layout for prefix caching
- Semantic caches and their risks

### Day 3: Host or buy, and report

- Self-hosting economics
- Batch versus interactive
- Cost per successful outcome
- The cost review

### Day 4: Capstone: the cost review, defended


## Topics

### The cost model

- Prefill, decode and cached tokens
- Retries, agent steps and context growth
- Accelerator-hours and utilisation

### Attribution and budgets

- Keys and tags per team and application
- Showback before chargeback
- No settled allocation method for multi-agent work

### Model choice and routing

- Own-task evaluation at several settings
- Cascades, tiers and fallbacks
- Cache cost of switching models

### Caching

- Prompt layout for prefix reuse
- Response and semantic caches
- Staleness and isolation between customers

### Hosting and reporting

- Self-hosting break-even
- Batch versus interactive tiers
- Cost per successful outcome
- Energy beside money

# AE-390 · AI Engineering Practicum

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Associate level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-300.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Practicum: about eight weeks part-time in teams of three to five for a sponsoring organisation, with weekly reviews by experienced engineers, two gate reviews and a defence before the sponsor
- Total hours: 100 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Teams of three to five take one problem from a sponsoring government entity or company from scoping to a shipped AI system in about eight weeks part-time. They agree a specification and acceptance criteria with the sponsor, build in weekly iterations reviewed by experienced engineers, evaluate against the criteria with a regression gate, harden the system after another team attacks it, deploy it with service objectives, monitoring and a rehearsed rollback, and hand it over with an evaluation report, a security note and an operations plan. Sponsor data enters only as an anonymised extract or a synthetic replica built to the sponsor's schema.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Analyse a sponsor's problem through discovery and translate it into a specification with acceptance criteria and a data-handling plan.
- Build, as a team, a working AI system that meets the agreed acceptance criteria, with coding-agent output reviewed in proportion to risk.
- Evaluate the system against the sponsor's criteria with error analysis and a regression gate.
- Harden the system after a cross-team attack and record the residual risks the sponsor must accept.
- Deploy the system with service objectives, capacity sizing, monitoring, cost per successful task and a rehearsed rollback.
- Defend the system, the team's design decisions and one's own contribution before the sponsor and experienced engineers.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-302 · Agentic Systems Engineering: Loops, Context and Harnesses](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-302.md)
- [AE-303 · Evaluation-Driven Development for Language Model Applications](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-303.md)
- [AE-304 · Retrieval and Knowledge Engineering for Language Model Systems](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-304.md)
- [AE-305 · Operating Machine Learning and Language Model Systems](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-305.md)
- [AE-308 · Securing Language Model and Agent Applications](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-308.md)
- [AE-311 · Shaping the Build: Product Sense and Delivery Practice](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-311.md)
- Works in a team through branches, pull requests and code review
- Can give about twelve hours a week for eight weeks

## Topics

### Engagement and scoping

- Sponsor roles, agreements and intellectual property
- Discovery and the problem brief
- Acceptance criteria as the contract
- Change control during delivery

### Team delivery

- Weekly iterations and demonstrations
- Coding agents with review by risk
- Tests, continuous integration and decision records

### Data and governance

- Classification of sponsor data
- Anonymised extracts and synthetic replicas
- Data sent to external models
- Impact assessment and system card

### Quality and security

- Owning the evaluation set
- Error analysis and regression gates
- Threat model and cross-team attack day

### Operations and hand-over

- Service objectives, capacity and monitoring
- Cost per successful task
- Runbooks, rollback drills and ownership after the practicum

# AE-401 · Inference Performance and Cost Engineering

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Expert level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-400.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-401/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-401/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-401/practice.html

## Description

Participants take the bilingual visitor assistant of a fictional national events authority, too slow at evening peaks and too costly, and make it meet its service objective at the lowest cost they can defend. They build a first-principles cost model, measure goodput curves on replayed traffic, diagnose seeded bottlenecks, then apply batching, caching, quantisation, speculative decoding, distillation, routing, disaggregated serving and autoscaling, re-running an Arabic and English task evaluation after every change.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compute prefill cost, decode cost and key-value cache memory, and predict the binding resource.
- Evaluate a serving configuration by measuring its goodput curve over concurrency against latency objectives.
- Diagnose why a deployment misses its service objective and confirm the fix.
- Optimise batching, admission, prefix caching and cache precision while holding task quality.
- Evaluate quantised, distilled and speculative-decoding variants against the base model and decide which to serve.
- Design and defend a serving topology covering disaggregation, routing, replica count and scaling policy.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-305 · Operating Machine Learning and Language Model Systems](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-305.md)
- [AE-307 · Container Orchestration and Cloud Infrastructure for AI Workloads](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-307.md)
- Has served an open-weight model behind an HTTP endpoint and load-tested it
- Computes percentiles and reads a latency histogram
- Estimates memory from parameter count and numeric precision

## Next courses

- [AE-490 · AI Systems Capstone: Production Readiness Review](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-490.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Model the cost first

- Prefill and decode are different problems
- Key-value cache arithmetic
- Goodput against an objective
- Curves, not single numbers

### Day 2: Scheduling and caching in the engine

- Continuous batching and admission
- Long prompts slow short ones
- Prefix caching starts with prompt layout
- Semantic caching and wrong answers

### Day 3: Cheaper tokens, same quality

- Quantising weights
- Cache precision buys concurrency
- Speculative decoding
- Distilled models and routing to them

### Day 4: Across replicas and over the day

- Disaggregated prefill and decode
- Routing across replicas
- Autoscaling and cold starts
- Cost per successful request

### Day 5: Capstone project presentations


## Topics

### The cost model of inference

- Prefill is compute-bound, decode is memory-bound
- Key-value cache arithmetic
- Roofline and queueing reasoning

### Measuring serving performance

- Time to first token, time per output token, goodput
- Profiling where a request's time goes
- Trace replay and load patterns
- Pareto curves and benchmark validity

### Inside the engine

- Continuous batching, chunked prefill, admission control
- Paged attention, cache precision and tiering
- Prefix and semantic caching; tenant isolation

### Cheaper models at the same quality

- Quantisation formats per accelerator
- Speculative decoding and acceptance rates
- Distillation and multi-adapter serving

### Across replicas and over the day

- Disaggregated prefill and decode
- Cache-aware routing
- Autoscaling, cold starts and scale to zero
- Cost per successful request and energy per token

# AE-402 · AI Solution Architecture and Platform Design

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Expert level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-400.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-402/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-402/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-402/practice.html

## Description

Participants practise the architect's loop on AI systems and apply it to the shared platform many teams build on. For a fictional ministry of municipal services with nine product teams and data at three classification levels, they turn requirements into measurable scenarios, draw views as code, cost three options including a non-generative one, keep a decision log, design a model catalogue, gateway, tenancy model, golden paths and showback, enforce a reference design with fitness checks, and review a peer's architecture. Serving optimisation and reliability engineering are left to AE-401 and AE-403.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare quality-attribute scenarios with measurable targets for answer quality, latency, cost, privacy and human oversight.
- Design an end-to-end architecture with context, container and data-flow views and a per-request latency and cost budget.
- Evaluate at least three solution options, including a non-generative baseline, and record the resulting decisions.
- Design a shared AI platform covering model admission, gateway, tenancy, golden paths and cost attribution.
- Design a reference architecture with fitness functions that check conformance automatically.
- Review a peer's architecture with a structured trade-off method and decide on a requested deviation.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-305 · Operating Machine Learning and Language Model Systems](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-305.md)
- [AE-308 · Securing Language Model and Agent Applications](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-308.md)
- [AE-311 · Shaping the Build: Product Sense and Delivery Practice](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-311.md)
- Has built and deployed at least one AI service that other people used
- Reads a cloud usage export or bill
- Can name the four national data classification levels

## Next courses

- [AE-490 · AI Systems Capstone: Production Readiness Review](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-490.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: From requirements to architecture

- The architect's loop for AI systems
- Quality attributes with numbers
- Regulation as a design constraint
- Views as code

### Day 2: Options and decisions

- Patterns and when each fits
- Total cost over three years
- Lock-in and exit
- Decision records

### Day 3: The shared platform

- The platform is a product
- Catalogue, admission and the gateway

# AE-403 · Reliability Engineering for AI Services

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Expert level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-400.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-403/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-403/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-403/practice.html

## Description

Participants set and defend reliability standards for AI services that other teams build. For a fictional postal and parcels operator running a bilingual tracking assistant on a self-hosted open-weight model with retrieval, they write service level objectives for availability, latency and answer quality, set admission limits with headroom from measured goodput, design and chaos-test degradation paths, lead incident drills and blameless reviews, release through canaries with automated rollback, and admit models only after verifying signatures and bills of materials.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Design service level objectives for availability, latency and answer quality, with error budgets and a release policy.
- Decide an admission limit and shedding priorities that keep headroom for the busiest hour.
- Design degradation for overload and dependency failure using load shedding, a smaller fallback model and a cached-answer mode.
- Lead an incident drill from detection to recovery and write a blameless review.
- Build a release gate that verifies model signatures, a bill of materials and licences before deployment.
- Review another team's AI service for production readiness and set launch conditions.

- [AE-307 · Container Orchestration and Cloud Infrastructure for AI Workloads](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-307.md)
- Has written alerting rules on service metrics
- Runs containers on a single-node cluster
- Has released a service through a canary or blue-green rollout
- Reads a goodput-versus-concurrency curve (the measurement method is taught in AE-401)

# AE-404 · Harness Engineering for Long-Running and Multi-Agent Systems

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Expert level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-400.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-404/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-404/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-404/practice.html

## Description

Participants design and measure harnesses for agents that run for an hour or more, hand work between roles and keep memory across sessions. For a fictional national library's digitisation unit, whose agents build small catalogue services from specifications checked by hidden acceptance tests, they separate planner, generator and evaluator roles, design memory that writes, consolidates, retrieves and forgets, steer asynchronous subagents, and make sessions survive crashes and approval pauses. On scaled-down tasks they hold the model fixed and remove harness components one at a time to find which still pay.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Implement planner, generator and evaluator roles that exchange work through files and stop on completion criteria agreed before work.
- Design a memory layer that writes, consolidates, retrieves and forgets, guarding against stale notes and concurrent overwrites.
- Build an orchestrator that steers asynchronous subagents and receives summaries rather than transcripts.
- Build durable sessions with an event log kept apart from the harness, idempotent tools and a human approval pause before irreversible actions.
- Evaluate harness components by ablation with the model held fixed, reporting success over repeated trials, cost and time per accepted task.
- Review a harness design and decide between a single agent with subagents and a multi-agent design on measured coordination cost.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-302 · Agentic Systems Engineering: Loops, Context and Harnesses](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-302.md)
- [AE-303 · Evaluation-Driven Development for Language Model Applications](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-303.md)
- Has written an agent loop with tool calling without a framework
- Computes a bootstrap confidence interval
- Reads and writes Python tests

## Next courses

- [AE-490 · AI Systems Capstone: Production Readiness Review](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-490.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Long runs and role separation

- Where long runs fail
- Planner, generator and evaluator
- Evaluators that hold the line
- What an accepted task costs

### Day 2: Context and memory across sessions

- Context as a budget
- Subagents for isolation
- Write, consolidate, retrieve, forget
- When memory goes wrong

### Day 3: Asynchronous, multi-agent and durable

- Steer, queue and notify
- Topologies and their costs
- Log, harness and sandbox apart
- Tools that are safe to retry

### Day 4: Measure the harness, then decide

- Ablation with the model held fixed
- Repeated trials and intervals
- Retesting after a model change
- Harness design review

### Day 5: Capstone project presentations


## Topics

### Long runs and role separation

- Premature wrap-up and self-praise
- Planner, generator and evaluator
- Completion criteria agreed before work
- When a separate evaluator pays

### Context and memory

- Compaction against reset with hand-off files
- Subagents return summaries, not transcripts
- Write, consolidate, retrieve, forget
- Stale notes and concurrent writers

### Asynchronous and multi-agent work

- Steer, queue and notify
- Orchestrator-worker, pipeline and peer topologies
- Cascading failures and coordination cost

### Durable sessions

- Session log, harness and sandbox as replaceable parts
- Resuming from the event log
- Pausing for human approval
- Idempotency keys and compensation

### Harness ablation

- Holding the model fixed
- Repeated trials and intervals
- Retesting after a model upgrade
- The harness as a versioned product

# AE-405 · Evaluation Programmes and Release Decisions

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Expert level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-400.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-405/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-405/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-405/practice.html

## Description

Participants design how an organisation decides that an AI system is good enough to release, and how it keeps knowing afterwards. For the fictional Wadi Noor Utilities (a bilingual customer assistant, a complaint-triage classifier, a meter-anomaly model and an internal coding agent) they tier systems by risk, report results with clustered, paired and grader-corrected uncertainty, audit a public benchmark before it informs a model choice, write and back-test release criteria, turn incidents into regression cases and brief a mock board. All logs, traces and incidents are synthetic. Single-system gates are AE-303; service objectives are AE-403.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compute clustered, paired and grader-corrected intervals for evaluation results and the number of items needed to detect a stated effect.
- Design a risk-tiered evaluation programme that states the evidence each tier needs before and after release.
- Audit a public benchmark for construct validity, label errors, contamination signals and sensitivity to harness and token budget.
- Specify blocking and advisory release criteria with non-inferiority margins and back-test them against history.
- Design post-release monitoring that grades sampled production traffic and turns incidents into regression cases.
- Defend a release recommendation with its uncertainty, residual risk and cost before a decision board.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-303 · Evaluation-Driven Development for Language Model Applications](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-303.md)
- [AE-305 · Operating Machine Learning and Language Model Systems](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-305.md)
- Computes a bootstrap interval and a paired difference in Python
- Has maintained an evaluation suite or release gate for a deployed system

## Next courses

- [AE-490 · AI Systems Capstone: Production Readiness Review](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-490.md)

## Format and days

### Day 1: Evaluation as a system

- An inventory comes before a suite
- Tiering by impact, autonomy and reach
- The evidence each tier needs
- A shared harness and dataset registry

### Day 2: Statistics of evaluations

- Items are a sample
- Repeated trials
- Paired comparisons and power
- Graders are instruments

### Day 3: Benchmarks and release criteria

- Auditing a public benchmark
- Harness and budget effects
- Writing release criteria
- Back-testing criteria

### Day 4: After release and to the board

- Change classes and exceptions
- Monitoring that feeds the suite
- Scorecards with uncertainty
- Briefing a release board

### Day 5: Capstone project presentations


## Topics

### Evaluation as an organisational system

- Inventory of systems and owners
- Tiering by impact, autonomy and reach
- Evidence per tier: capability, regression, adversarial, subgroup, human review
- Shared harness, dataset registry and grader records

### Statistics of evaluations

- Items as a sample and clustered standard errors
- Repeated trials and consistency
- Paired comparisons, power and minimum effect
- Correcting pass rates for grader error

### Auditing benchmarks and claims

- Construct validity and task ambiguity
- Contamination and models that recognise a test
- Harness, token budget and infrastructure effects on rankings

### Release criteria

- Blocking and advisory checks
- Non-inferiority margins and noise floors
- Change classes: prompt, model, retrieval, tool, provider
- Sign-off, exceptions and their expiry

### After release and reporting

- Sampled grading of production traffic
- Incidents turned into regression cases
- Scorecards with uncertainty, residual risk and cost
- Linking gates to the national risk framework

# AE-406 · Post-Training Open Models on Domain Data

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Expert level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-400.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-406/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-406/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-406/practice.html

## Description

Participants post-train open-weight models on domain data and prove the result is worth serving. For the fictional Eastern Coast Permits Authority they turn synthetic bilingual permit records, officer edits and agent traces into tuning mixtures, then run full and sharded supervised tuning, preference optimisation, a short reinforcement learning loop with verifiable rewards, distillation from a larger teacher and tuning on filtered agent traces. Each model is compared with its base and a prompting and retrieval baseline, for task gains and for regressions in general ability, safety and Arabic quality. AE-310 covers single-GPU adapters and serving; this course goes beyond them.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Decide whether post-training is justified over prompting and retrieval for a task, and which method fits it.
- Build a validated tuning mixture of domain records, teacher-generated examples and general data with licence, deduplication and leakage checks.
- Configure supervised tuning at scale, choosing full-parameter or adapter tuning and a sharding strategy that fit a stated accelerator memory budget.
- Train with preference data or verifiable rewards and diagnose reward hacking in the result.
- Produce a small model by distillation and by tuning on outcome-filtered agent traces that meets a latency and cost target.
- Evaluate an adapted model against its base for task improvement and for regressions in general ability, safety and Arabic dialect quality.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-310 · Model Adaptation: Fine-Tuning, Distillation and Small Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-310.md)
- [AE-303 · Evaluation-Driven Development for Language Model Applications](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-303.md)
- Writes and debugs a training loop in a deep-learning framework
- Has tuned a model with adapters and evaluated it against its base

## Format and days

### Day 1: Data decides the result

- When post-training beats prompting and retrieval
- Data mixtures against forgetting
- Synthetic data and its validation
- Memory and compute accounting

### Day 2: Supervised tuning

- Full tuning against adapters
- Hyperparameters that matter
- Forgetting and regressions
- Scaling out

### Day 3: Preferences and rewards

- Preference data from expert edits
- Direct preference optimisation
- Verifiable rewards
- Reward hacking

### Day 4: Distillation, traces and the decision

- Distilling a teacher
- Training on agent traces
- Merging task adapters
- Evaluating the adapted model

### Day 5: Capstone project presentations


## Topics

### Deciding to post-train

- Prompting, retrieval and tuning as alternatives
- Cost of training against cost of serving
- Open-weight licences and acceptable-use terms

### Data for post-training

- Curation, deduplication and mixing against forgetting
- Synthetic data from teachers and its validation
- Leakage against evaluation sets

### Supervised tuning at scale

- Full tuning, adapters and quantised adapters
- Memory accounting for weights, gradients and optimiser state
- Sharded multi-GPU training
- Forgetting and safety regressions

### Preferences and rewards

- Preference pairs and annotator agreement
- Direct preference optimisation and its variants
- Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards
- Reward hacking

### Distillation, traces and merging

- Distillation from a teacher
- Rejection sampling of agent traces
- Merging methods and interference between tasks

### Evaluating adapted models

- Task, general, safety and Arabic dialect slices
- Paired comparison with the base
- Model cards for adapted models

# AE-407 · AI Assurance, Red Teaming and Governance for Engineering Leads

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Expert level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-400.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-407/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-407/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-407/practice.html

## Description

Participants lead the assurance of AI systems that act on an organisation's data. For the fictional Northern Region Benefits Agency (a bilingual benefits assistant and a case-worker agent that reads case files and drafts letters) they plan and run a red-team exercise in Arabic and English, manually and with automated probes, assess the risks with the National AI Risk Management Framework, review the security architecture for agent identity, least privilege, isolation and egress, and assemble an assurance case that ends in a residual-risk briefing. Targets run in a sandbox on synthetic case data. Hardening a single application is AE-308.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Plan a red-team exercise with objectives tied to harms, scope, rules of engagement and stop conditions.
- Conduct manual and automated adversarial testing in Arabic and English and quantify attack success over repeated trials.
- Assess the risks of an agent with the national framework, from context to treatment and residual sign-off.
- Review a security architecture for agent identity, delegated authority, least privilege, isolation and egress control.
- Build an assurance case that links each claim to evidence and maps the evidence to a control framework.
- Present residual risk and a recommendation with conditions to an accountable executive.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-308 · Securing Language Model and Agent Applications](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-308.md)
- [AE-303 · Evaluation-Driven Development for Language Model Applications](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-303.md)
- Has written a threat model for a system they built
- Reads a risk register and a likelihood and impact matrix

## Next courses

## Format and days

- Objectives, scope and rules of engagement
- Choosing techniques from catalogues

- Findings people can act on

- Treatment and residual risk
- Supplier and model-change risk

### Day 4: Review and assemble the evidence

- Security architecture review
- Identity and delegated authority
- Assurance evidence packs
- Briefing the accountable executive

### Day 5: Capstone: an assurance pack and its defence


## Topics

### Assurance as argument

- Claims, arguments and evidence
- Independence of testers and reviewers
- Evidence that defeats a claim

### Red-team practice

- Objectives, rules of engagement and stop conditions
- Technique catalogues: OWASP lists and MITRE ATLAS
- Arabic, dialect and transliteration attacks
- Automated probing and success over trials
- Findings turned into regression tests

- Context and scope

- Likelihood and impact scoring and calibration
- Treatment and residual sign-off

# AE-408 · Multimodal and Speech Systems Engineering

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Expert level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-400.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 26 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: Available
- Open the course: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-408/
- The whole course in one file: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-408/llms-full.txt
- Practice questions: https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/ae-408/practice.html

## Description

Participants build and evaluate applications that see, listen and speak, with Arabic as the main case. For the fictional Heritage Trails Authority they extract grounded fields from visitor and ranger photos with vision-language models, benchmark open-weight speech recognisers on dialects and code-switched speech, test synthesised read-back, and assemble a bilingual voice booking line with turn-taking, interruption and tool calls within a latency budget. They test it with simulated callers and choose between open-weight and hosted, cascaded and speech-to-speech designs on measured quality, latency and cost. Photos are public-domain or synthetic; calls use synthetic voices and public speech corpora.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Implement image applications with vision-language models that return validated structured fields grounded in the image.
- Evaluate speech recognisers on Arabic dialects and code-switched speech with explicit normalisation rules.
- Build a bilingual voice agent that handles turn-taking, interruption and confirmed tool calls within a latency budget.
- Diagnose failure modes specific to image and audio inputs, including invented objects, text produced on silence and instructions hidden in images.
- Design a multimodal test set and an end-to-end evaluation with simulated callers.
- Decide between open-weight and hosted, cascaded and speech-to-speech designs on quality, latency and cost per call.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-301 · Applied Natural Language Processing Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-301.md)
- [AE-303 · Evaluation-Driven Development for Language Model Applications](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-303.md)
- Has built a language model application with structured outputs and tool calls
- Computes precision, recall and an error rate with an interval

## Format and days

### Day 1: Seeing

- How a vision-language model sees
- Structured extraction from photos
- Grounding answers in pixels
- Arabic text and hidden instructions

### Day 2: Listening

- From waveform to text
- Normalisation decides the error rate
- Dialects and code-switching
- Streaming and silence

### Day 3: Speaking

- Synthesis and read-back
- Cascaded versus speech-to-speech
- Turn-taking and interruption
- Tool calls during speech

### Day 4: Evaluating and choosing

- Multimodal test sets
- Simulated callers
- Choosing by quality, latency and cost
- Voice, faces and consent

### Day 5: Capstone project presentations


## Topics

### Vision-language models in applications

- Visual tokens, resolution and cost
- Structured extraction from photos
- Grounding with boxes and points
- Frames from video
- Instructions hidden in images

### Speech recognition

- Recogniser families and multilingual encoders
- Arabic normalisation of diacritics, letter variants and numerals
- Dialects, code-switching and telephone audio
- Streaming, voice activity detection, diarisation and text on silence

### Synthesis and voice agents

- Read-back of names, numbers and dates
- Cascaded, speech-to-speech and full-duplex designs
- End-of-turn detection and interruption
- Latency budgets and tool calls during speech

### Evaluation

- Multimodal test sets
- Error rates with intervals by slice
- Simulated callers
- Cost per call

### Responsible voice and image handling

- Voice and faces as personal data
- Consent, retention and minimisation
- Disclosure of synthetic voices

# AE-490 · AI Systems Capstone: Production Readiness Review

- Track: AI Engineering
- Path: [AI Engineering: courses that help prepare for the Expert level](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/AE-400.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Studio: about eight weeks part-time, an individual production readiness review with four coached review rounds and a panel defence
- Total hours: 60 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Each participant takes one existing AI system through a production readiness review and decides whether it may go live. The system is a sanitised copy from the participant's organisation, used with the owner's written approval, or the Academy reference system: the shipment-exceptions agent of the fictional Dune Line Freight company, with retrieval, tools and seeded weaknesses, run in a sandbox. Participants reconstruct the architecture, judge the model and retrieval choices, re-run its evaluations, load-test, fault-inject and cost it, threat-model and probe it, audit its governance evidence, and write a go, conditional-go or no-go recommendation defended before a panel.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Review the architecture of an existing AI system and the fitness of its model, retrieval and adaptation choices against its requirements.
- Audit the system's evaluation evidence and re-run its critical evaluations with stated uncertainty.
- Evaluate reliability, rollback readiness and cost against service objectives by load testing, fault injection and a rehearsed rollback.
- Assess security by threat modelling, sandboxed probing and checks of supply-chain evidence.
- Audit governance evidence for classification, personal data flows, risk assessment, human oversight, incidents and retirement.
- Decide and defend a go, conditional-go or no-go recommendation with conditions, owners and dates.

## Prerequisites

- [AE-401 · Inference Performance and Cost Engineering](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-401.md)
- [AE-402 · AI Solution Architecture and Platform Design](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-402.md)
- [AE-403 · Reliability Engineering for AI Services](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-403.md)
- [AE-404 · Harness Engineering for Long-Running and Multi-Agent Systems](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-404.md)
- [AE-405 · Evaluation Programmes and Release Decisions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-405.md)
- [AE-407 · AI Assurance, Red Teaming and Governance for Engineering Leads](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/AE-407.md)
- Has shipped or operated an AI system in production, or completed AE-390
- Can bring a sanitised copy of a system with its owner's written approval, or uses the Academy reference system

## Topics

### The readiness review as a practice

- Scope, independence and evidence standards
- Checklists versus judgement
- Findings with severity, owners and dates

### Architecture and model fitness

- Requirements and decision records
- Model, retrieval and adaptation choices
- Known model limits and fallbacks

### Evaluation, reliability and cost

- Audit and re-run of evaluation suites
- Service objectives for latency and quality
- Load testing to a goodput target and fault injection
- Cost per successful outcome and capacity assumptions

### Security and governance

- Threat models and sandboxed probes
- Bills of materials and signing
- Classification, personal data flows and transfers
- Risk assessment, cards, oversight, incidents and retirement

### The decision

- Go, conditional go and no-go
- Conditions with owners and dates
- Briefing decision makers

# SPC-ANL-201 · Exploratory Analysis and Visualisation

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Analysis and Business Intelligence](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-ANL.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants start every analysis from written questions, then use summaries and charts to examine distributions, relationships and change over time in public and synthetic datasets. They build charts with a grammar-of-graphics library, choose encodings and scales that do not mislead, and test by resampling whether an apparent pattern could be chance. Every step lives in a notebook that reruns from raw data. The capstone is an exploratory report on an unseen dataset, defended live.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish exploratory from confirmatory analysis and explain why an exploratory pattern needs a fresh test.
- Prepare an analysis plan listing questions, units of observation, variables and the comparison that answers each question.
- Analyse distributions and pairwise relationships with summaries and charts suited to each variable type.
- Use a grammar of graphics to map variables to position, colour and facets, with honest scales and baselines.
- Test whether an apparent difference or correlation could arise by chance, using permutation or bootstrap resampling.
- Build a reproducible exploratory report stating findings, open questions and limits.

## Prerequisites

- [FND-DAT-102 · Data Wrangling with DataFrames](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-DAT-102.md)
- Computes and reads means, medians, quantiles and standard deviations
- Has run a permutation test or bootstrap interval (FND-MTH-104 or the pre-work notebook)

## Next courses

- [SPC-ANL-202 · Analysis with AI Assistants: Delegate, Verify, Reproduce](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-ANL-202.md)
- [SPC-ANL-203 · Metrics, Semantic Models and Dashboards](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-ANL-203.md)
- [SPC-ANL-301 · Data Storytelling and Decision Briefings](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-ANL-301.md)
- [SPC-ANL-302 · Geospatial Analytics](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-ANL-302.md)
- [SPC-MOD-307 · Problem Framing, Product Sense and Analytical Review](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-MOD-307.md)

## Topics

### Questions before charts

- Analysis questions and units of observation
- Provenance and data dictionaries
- Exploratory versus confirmatory work

### Distributions and relationships

- Shape, skew, outliers and missing values
- Scatter plots, overplotting and binning
- Confounding and Simpson's paradox
- Trend, seasonality and breaks

### Grammar of graphics and perception

- Aesthetics, geometries, scales and facets
- Accuracy of visual encodings
- Colour, including colour-vision deficiency
- Baselines, dual axes and truncated scales
- Showing uncertainty with intervals and bands
- Bilingual and right-to-left chart labels

### Checking patterns and notebooks

- Permutation tests and bootstrap intervals
- Forking paths and recording dead ends
- Notebooks that rerun from raw data

# SPC-ANL-202 · Analysis with AI Assistants: Delegate, Verify, Reproduce

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Analysis and Business Intelligence](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-ANL.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days with labs, guided pre-work and a peer-rerun project
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants analyse data with a coding agent in a notebook. They decide which steps to delegate, brief the agent with acceptance checks, and confirm results by recomputing key numbers another way. Each lab ends with a verification note: what the agent produced, how it was checked, what was wrong. They measure run-to-run variability and package an analysis that a peer reruns from logged prompts, code and data.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare a delegation plan marking which steps stay with the analyst, and a brief stating question, data, constraints and acceptance checks.
- Test assisted analyses by recomputing headline numbers and checking joins, filters and denominators.
- Measure run-to-run variability by repeating one request and comparing code, numbers and conclusions.
- Deliver an assisted analysis package that another analyst can rerun and audit.

## Prerequisites

- [SPC-ANL-201 · Exploratory Analysis and Visualisation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-ANL-201.md)
- Writes and debugs short dataframe or SQL analyses without assistance

## Topics

### Delegation and briefing

- Where agents fail on data work
- What stays with the analyst: framing, causal claims, sign-off
- Checks written before the run

### Verification

- Second-route recomputation
- Row counts, cardinality and denominators
- Agents that try many analyses and report one
- Narrative checked against numbers

### Reproducibility

- Asking the same question several times
- Logging prompts, model and transcripts
- Pinned data versions and environments

---

# SPC-ANL-203 · Metrics, Semantic Models and Dashboards

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Analysis and Business Intelligence](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-ANL.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants turn business questions from a synthetic service organisation into governed metrics, each with a definition, formula, grain, filters, owner and tests. They build a star-schema semantic model over a small warehouse, define metrics once in an open specification, and design a dashboard that answers the questions with few charts and loads within a time budget. They then acceptance-test a conversational analytics agent on certified questions and report where it returns wrong but plausible numbers. Metrics as tested pipeline code are DEV-DAT-202; deep platform tuning is SPC-ANL-303.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain where inconsistent numbers arise between metric definitions, semantic models and dashboards.
- Draft metric definitions with formula, grain, filters, time logic, owner and known limits.
- Implement a dimensional semantic model with conformed dimensions and metrics defined once.
- Design a dashboard for a named audience and decision, choosing layout, comparisons and drill paths.
- Measure dashboard load time and reduce it through aggregation, filters or model changes.
- Evaluate a conversational analytics agent against governed metrics and decide whether it is fit for a stated use.

## Prerequisites

- [FND-DAT-101 · SQL and Relational Data](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-DAT-101.md)
- [SPC-ANL-201 · Exploratory Analysis and Visualisation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-ANL-201.md)
- Writes SQL with joins, grouping and window functions

## Next courses

- [SPC-ANL-303 · Business Intelligence Platform Practice: Governance, Performance and Enablement](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-ANL-303.md)

## Topics

### Metrics

- Ratios, rates, distinct counts and snapshots
- Grain, time windows and calendars
- Metric trees from goal to driver
- Owners, certification and change control

### Semantic models

- Star schemas and slowly changing dimensions
- Join paths and fan-out errors
- Metrics in an open interchange specification
- Synonyms and descriptions as context for AI

### Dashboard design and performance

- Audience, decision and update cycle
- Comparisons with targets, prior periods and peers
- Freshness, as-of dates and data-quality flags
- Accessibility and right-to-left layouts
- Task-based testing with intended users
- Pre-aggregation and load-time budgets

### Conversational analytics

- From question to query
- Certified question sets
- Wrong grain, wrong filter, invented metric
- Human review before use

# SPC-ANL-204 · Data Acquisition, Preparation and Quality for Analysis

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Analysis and Business Intelligence](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-ANL.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants assemble an analysis dataset from an API, open-data files and an internal extract. They record provenance and licences, link records across sources with and without shared keys, and clean the result with validation rules that rerun on every build. They show how missing data and measurement error move a headline estimate. They label a free-text column with a language model, measure agreement with a human-coded sample and stability across reruns, and use that sample to correct the estimate the labels feed. Pipeline gates and data contracts are DEV-DAT-204; text modelling in depth is SPC-MOD-303.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Describe missing-data mechanisms and types of measurement error, and the bias each can introduce.
- Prepare a provenance record for each source with origin, coverage, licence, refresh date and limits.
- Implement record linkage across sources, with cardinality tests, reconciliation counts and a clerical review of uncertain matches.
- Configure validation rules for types, ranges, uniqueness, completeness and cross-field consistency.
- Analyse how complete-case analysis, imputation and a sensitivity range change a headline estimate.
- Evaluate language-model labels of free text as a measurement instrument and decide whether they are fit for the analysis.

## Prerequisites

- [FND-DAT-101 · SQL and Relational Data](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-DAT-101.md)
- [FND-DAT-102 · Data Wrangling with DataFrames](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-DAT-102.md)
- Has fitted a simple linear regression and read its coefficients
- Calls a paginated API from Python (FND-DAT-103 or equivalent)

## Topics

### Sourcing

- Data requirements from the question
- Found data versus designed data
- Licences, coverage and selection bias

### Linking and cleaning

- Keys, grain and join cardinality
- Linkage without shared keys: blocking, similarity, clerical review
- Arabic name variants and transliteration
- Linkage error and its effect on counts
- Rules as code and change logs

### Missing data and measurement error

- Missing completely at random, at random, not at random
- Single and multiple imputation
- Proxies and misclassification
- Sensitivity ranges

### Labelling with language models

- Labels as measurement
- Codebooks and human-coded samples
- Chance-corrected agreement
- Correcting estimates for label error
- Drift after model or prompt changes

# SPC-ANL-301 · Data Storytelling and Decision Briefings

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Analysis and Business Intelligence](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-ANL.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 24 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants turn a completed analysis into a recommendation a decision maker can act on. They identify the decision and audience, structure a briefing that gives the answer first, redesign charts to explain rather than explore, and state uncertainty, assumptions and risks in plain words with ranges and natural frequencies. They write a two-page decision memo and rehearse against hard questions. The course ends with a live briefing to a panel playing decision makers. Framing the question before analysis is SPC-MOD-307; general technical writing is FND-AIC-106.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Analyse a decision context to identify the decision maker, options, criteria and the evidence that would change the choice.
- Draft a storyline that puts the answer first and supports it with grouped, ordered reasons.
- Prepare explanatory charts whose titles state the finding, with annotation matched to the message.
- Draft statements of uncertainty, assumptions and risks in plain words using ranges, natural frequencies and scenarios.
- Deliver a decision memo stating recommendation, evidence, uncertainty, alternatives considered and what to monitor after the decision.
- Defend a recommendation in a live briefing under questioning, stating what is not known.

## Prerequisites

- [SPC-ANL-201 · Exploratory Analysis and Visualisation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-ANL-201.md)
- Reads a confidence interval and states what it does and does not mean
- Brings a completed analysis of public or synthetic data, or uses one provided

## Topics

### From analysis to recommendation

- Decision, options and criteria
- What the audience knows, needs and worries about
- From finding to claim to recommendation
- Counter-evidence and selective emphasis

### Structure and charts

- Answer first, then reasons
- Situation, complication, question, answer
- Titles that state the finding
- Annotation, emphasis and bilingual layouts

### Uncertainty in plain words

- Ranges and natural frequencies
- How readers misread verbal probability terms
- What would change the conclusion

### Delivery

- Spoken structure and timing
- Handling challenge and saying what is not known
- Checking every number in AI-drafted material

# SPC-ANL-302 · Geospatial Analytics

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Analysis and Business Intelligence](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-ANL.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Workshop: two days with labs, guided pre-work and a short defended project
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants answer location questions with open vector data on a laptop. They correct coordinate reference systems, geocode addresses, use spatial joins and network distance to measure access to services, map rates rather than counts, and test whether a cluster is stronger than chance. The workshop ends with a service-access analysis on open geodata, defended live. Imagery and learned models are DEV-MLE-305.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain how projections and the modifiable areal unit problem can change a spatial result.
- Apply spatial joins, buffers and distance measures to compute access to services.
- Prepare maps with normalised measures, suitable class breaks and colour schemes.
- Diagnose spatial clustering with global and local autocorrelation and judge whether a hot spot is meaningful.
- Deliver a service-access analysis with stated assumptions and limits.

## Prerequisites

### Spatial data

- Reference systems and projections
- GeoJSON, GeoPackage and GeoParquet
- Geocoding addresses and match errors
- Open geodata and licences

### Spatial operations

- Joins, overlays and buffers
- Network distance and travel-time areas
- Hexagonal and square grids

### Map design

- Rates by population or area
- Unstable rates in small areas
- Class breaks, colour and Arabic labels

### Spatial statistics and privacy

- Global and local autocorrelation
- Modifiable areal unit and edge effects
- Re-identification and minimum-count aggregation

# SPC-STA-201 · Statistical Inference by Simulation

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Statistics and Inference](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-STA.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 36 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Building on the single-sample bootstrap and permutation tests of FND-MTH-104, participants turn a question into an estimand, estimate it with an interval, test it, and check by simulation that their method does what it claims. They handle paired and clustered observations, skewed outcomes and ratios, compute power by simulating the planned analysis, control error rates across a planned family of claims and test equivalence when the claim is that nothing changed. The capstone is an inference report on public data, defended live.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare an analysis plan stating estimand, unit of analysis, method and error rates before seeing the data.
- Compute bootstrap and large-sample intervals for ratios and differences in dependent data, resampling the correct unit.
- Implement a simulation that measures the coverage and Type I error of a method when its assumptions fail.
- Compute power and sample size by simulating the planned analysis, including clustering and attrition.
- Apply family-wise, false discovery rate and gatekeeping control to a planned family of claims, and test equivalence where the claim is no meaningful difference.
- Deliver an inference report that states estimates, intervals, effect sizes and limits in plain words.

## Prerequisites

- [FND-MTH-104 · Statistics by Simulation: Variation, Estimation and Testing](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-MTH-104.md)
- Writes short analysis scripts in Python or R with a dataframe library
- A pass in the placement test is accepted in place of FND-MTH-104

## Next courses

- [SPC-STA-301 · Regression and Generalised Linear Modelling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-STA-301.md)
- [SPC-STA-302 · Survey, Sampling and Measurement Design](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-STA-302.md)
- [SPC-EXP-402 · Statistical Evaluation of AI Systems](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-EXP-402.md)
- [SPC-MOD-402 · Simulation and Agent-Based Modelling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-MOD-402.md)
- [SPC-RSP-302 · Data Science Practicum](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-RSP-302.md)

## Topics

### From question to estimand

- Population, unit of analysis and estimand
- Scope of inference
- Pre-specified analyses and forking paths

### Intervals that respect the data

- Studentised and bias-corrected bootstrap
- Paired, clustered and blocked resampling
- Where large-sample formulas fail
- Confidence versus prediction intervals

### Tests and their error rates

- Restricted permutations for paired and clustered data
- Equivalence and non-inferiority margins
- Simulation studies to check a method

### Power by simulation

- Minimum effect of interest
- Clustering, unequal allocation and attrition
- Why post-hoc power is not evidence

### Many comparisons and reporting

- Choosing an error rate for a family of claims
- Gatekeeping for primary and secondary claims
- Effect sizes with intervals
- Verification notes for assistant-written code

# SPC-STA-301 · Regression and Generalised Linear Modelling

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Statistics and Inference](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-STA.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 36 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants build regression models that answer stated questions and defend what the coefficients mean. They fit linear, logistic and count models with interactions and spline terms, diagnose misfit with residuals and fake-data simulation, compare cluster-adjusted errors with a first mixed-effects model for grouped data, and apply penalised regression when predictors are many. Results are reported as predicted quantities and marginal effects with intervals. The capstone is a modelling report on public data, defended live.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish descriptive, predictive and causal uses of a regression and the assumption each requires.
- Implement linear, logistic and count models with interactions and splines, interpreted as predicted values and average marginal effects.
- Diagnose misfit with residuals, influence measures and fake-data simulation, and correct the model.
- Analyse grouped data with cluster-adjusted standard errors and a random-intercept model, compared with a naive fit.
- Apply ridge and lasso penalties with cross-validated tuning and measure the stability of the selected predictors.
- Build and defend a regression model that answers a stated question, justifying terms, family and uncertainty.

## Prerequisites

- [SPC-STA-201 · Statistical Inference by Simulation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-STA-201.md)
- Reads matrix notation for a linear model
- Writes analysis notebooks in Python or R

## Next courses

- [SPC-STA-401 · Bayesian Modelling and Decisions under Uncertainty](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-STA-401.md)
- [SPC-EXP-302 · Causal Inference from Observational Data](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-EXP-302.md)
- [SPC-EXP-402 · Statistical Evaluation of AI Systems](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-EXP-402.md)

## Topics

### Linear models as answers

- Description, prediction and causal claims
- Adjustment sets and the Table 2 fallacy (identification in SPC-EXP-302)
- Contrasts, interactions and transformed outcomes
- Splines for non-linear relationships

### Generalised linear models

- Links and outcome families
- Logistic regression and separation
- Poisson, negative binomial and offsets
- Average marginal effects

### Diagnostics

- Residuals, hat values and influence
- Overdispersion and calibration
- Recovering known parameters from fake data

### Grouped data

- Heteroskedasticity-consistent and cluster-adjusted standard errors
- Random intercepts and slopes
- No, complete and partial pooling

### Regularisation and reporting

- Ridge, lasso and elastic net
- Why intervals after selection mislead
- Effect plots on the outcome scale

---

# SPC-STA-302 · Survey, Sampling and Measurement Design

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Statistics and Inference](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-STA.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Workshop: two days with labs, guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants design a survey that can answer its question and analyse one honestly. They choose a stratified or cluster design from a frame, compute design effects and design-based standard errors, weight for non-response and to population margins, and critique, pretest and check the reliability of questionnaire items. The workshop ends with a defended sampling and measurement plan.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compute design weights, design effects and design-based standard errors for a stratified cluster sample.
- Apply non-response adjustment and raking to population margins and measure the effect on estimates.
- Analyse questionnaire items for wording faults, scale reliability and evidence of validity.
- Review two disagreeing survey results and trace the gap to frame, non-response, wording or denominator.
- Design a sampling and measurement plan with frame, design, sample size, weighting and pretest.

## Prerequisites

- [SPC-STA-201 · Statistical Inference by Simulation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-STA-201.md)
- Fits and reads a logistic regression

## Topics

### Frames and designs

- Total survey error and coverage
- Stratified, cluster and multi-stage designs
- Design effect and sample size
- Linearisation and replicate-weight variance

### Weighting

- Response propensity adjustment
- Raking and calibration
- Opt-in panels and limits of adjustment

### Measurement

- Wording, order and response scales
- Cognitive pretesting and mode effects
- Reliability and validity

### Language models in survey work

- Model coding of open answers as measurement (see SPC-ANL-204)
- Why simulated respondents are not a sample
