# SPC-STA-401 · Bayesian Modelling and Decisions under Uncertainty

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Statistics and Inference](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-STA.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Extended: 10 weeks part-time, with weekly labs, graded assignments and a defended capstone
- Total hours: 60 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants build Bayesian models for real decisions and judge models built by others. They set priors and check them by prior predictive simulation, fit models with Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, diagnose the computation, and test fit with posterior predictive checks and cross-validation. They build hierarchical models for many small groups and verify their code by simulation-based calibration. The final weeks turn posteriors into decisions through expected utility and the value of further data.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Implement a Bayesian workflow from prior predictive simulation through fitting to sampler diagnosis.
- Design a hierarchical model for many small groups and defend the pooling it implies.
- Evaluate competing models with posterior predictive checks and approximate leave-one-out cross-validation.
- Validate a model implementation by parameter recovery and simulation-based calibration.
- Decide between actions by expected utility under the posterior, including the value of collecting more data.
- Review another analyst's Bayesian analysis for priors, computation, checking and reporting.

## Prerequisites

- [SPC-STA-301 · Regression and Generalised Linear Modelling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-STA-301.md)
- Works with conditional probability and likelihoods at the depth of FND-MTH-103
- Writes simulation code in Python or R

## Topics

### Priors and posteriors

- The model as a data-generating story
- Eliciting priors from domain experts
- Prior predictive simulation
- Bayesian and frequentist answers compared

### Computation

- Grid approximation for intuition
- Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
- Convergence, effective sample size and divergences
- Reparameterisation; limits of variational approximation

### Hierarchical models

- Partial pooling and shrinkage
- Varying intercepts and slopes
- Measurement error and missing data

### Checking models

- Posterior predictive checks
- Approximate leave-one-out cross-validation and stacking
- Simulation-based calibration
- Prior sensitivity
- Reporting a Bayesian analysis

### Decisions

- Utility and loss
- Expected value of information
- Small experiments and benchmarks
- Bandits and Thompson sampling

---

# SPC-EXP-201 · Designing and Reading Experiments

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Experimentation and Causal Inference](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-EXP.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Workshop: two days with labs, short guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants design a randomised experiment from a decision question and read its results without fooling themselves. They write a pre-registration with a hypothesis, primary and guardrail metrics, a unit of randomisation and a sample size computed by formula and checked by simulation. They analyse a synthetic experiment log, test whether the randomisation worked, and measure by simulation how peeking, many metrics and a mismatched unit of analysis inflate false wins. The workshop ends with a written critique of a flawed result and a design pack for one experiment.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish a randomised experiment, a quasi-experiment and an observational comparison, and explain what causal claim each can support.
- Draft a pre-registration that states the decision, hypothesis, unit of randomisation, primary and guardrail metrics and the analysis plan.
- Compute the sample size and run time needed to detect a minimum effect of interest, and check the answer by simulation.
- Analyse a completed two-arm experiment with a difference in means, a confidence interval and a sample ratio mismatch test.
- Measure the false-positive rate caused by repeated peeking and by testing many metrics in the same experiment.
- Review a reported experiment result and decide whether it supports the decision it claims to support.

## Prerequisites

- [FND-MTH-104 · Statistics by Simulation: Variation, Estimation and Testing](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-MTH-104.md)
- Writes short analysis scripts in Python or R with a dataframe library
- Equivalent knowledge of sampling variation and bootstrap intervals, shown in the placement test, is accepted in place of FND-MTH-104

## Next courses

- [SPC-EXP-301 · Online Experiments at Scale](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-EXP-301.md)
- [SPC-EXP-303 · Measuring the Impact of AI Deployments](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-EXP-303.md)

## Topics

### From decision to hypothesis

- The decision and what result would change it
- Estimands: whose outcome, compared with what
- Primary, secondary and guardrail metrics
- Pre-registration and analysis plans

### Randomisation and control

- Units of randomisation: person, session, cluster
- Simple, stratified and blocked assignment
- Control groups and A/A tests
- Factorial designs and interactions in brief
- Consent and review for experiments on people

### Sample size and power

- Minimum effect of interest
- Variance, baseline rates and traffic
- Formula versus simulation
- Run time and weekly cycles

### Analysis

- Difference in means and proportions
- Confidence intervals and p-values read correctly
- Sample ratio mismatch
- Unit of analysis versus unit of randomisation
- Non-compliance and intention-to-treat analysis

### Reading a result without fooling yourself

- Peeking and optional stopping
- Many metrics and post-hoc subgroups
- Novelty effects, dropout and survivorship
- Practical versus statistical significance

### Reporting

- Results table and decision
- Uncertainty in plain words
- What the experiment does not show

---

# SPC-EXP-301 · Online Experiments at Scale

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Experimentation and Causal Inference](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-EXP.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants run the statistics behind an experimentation programme that launches many tests a year, including tests of AI features. On a synthetic event stream from an online service they apply regression adjustment with pre-experiment data, compute intervals for ratio metrics, design sequential tests that allow continuous monitoring, and define guardrail metrics for latency, errors, cost and harm. They detect interference in marketplaces and networks and design cluster and switchback alternatives. They build a trustworthiness check pack and sit on a mock review board that decides whether experiments launch, iterate or stop.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Apply regression adjustment with pre-experiment covariates (CUPED, controlled-experiment using pre-experiment data) and report the variance reduction and the saving in sample size.
- Compute standard errors for ratio and per-session metrics with the delta method and with a bootstrap over the randomisation unit.
- Implement a group sequential design and an always-valid confidence sequence, and test their error rates under daily monitoring.
- Design a metric set and decision rule for a launch: a primary metric, guardrails for latency, errors, cost and harm, and how they combine.
- Diagnose interference in a two-sided marketplace experiment and design a cluster-randomised or switchback alternative with its power.
- Review experiment write-ups as a member of a review board and decide launch, iterate or stop for each.

## Prerequisites

- [SPC-EXP-201 · Designing and Reading Experiments](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-EXP-201.md)
- Fits and reads a linear regression with covariates
- Queries event-level data with SQL, including grouping and joins

## Topics

### Experimentation as a programme

- Experiment lifecycle and platform components
- Overall evaluation criterion and metric taxonomy
- Guardrail and quality metrics
- Testing AI features: model, prompt and ranking changes

### Trustworthiness checks

- A/A tests and sample ratio mismatch
- Logging, triggering and exposure
- Novelty, primacy and carry-over
- Bots, outliers and capped metrics

### Variance and metrics

- Delta method for ratio metrics
- Bootstrap at the randomisation unit
- Regression adjustment with pre-experiment data
- Power calculations that include variance reduction

### Sequential testing

- Why continuous monitoring inflates error
- Group sequential boundaries and alpha spending
- Always-valid inference and confidence sequences
- Stopping for harm on guardrails

### Interference and complex designs

- Network and marketplace interference
- Cluster randomisation
- Switchback and time-split designs
- Holdouts and long-term effects
- Surrogate metrics for long-term outcomes and their validation

### Many experiments at once

- False discovery rate across a programme
- Pre-planned segments versus fishing
- Winner's curse and shrinkage of reported effects
- Bandits versus fixed-allocation tests for inference

### Review and decisions

- Review board practice
- Launch criteria and decision records
- Archiving results and learning across experiments
- Consent and notice for experiments at scale

---

# SPC-EXP-302 · Causal Inference from Observational Data

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Experimentation and Causal Inference](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-EXP.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 36 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants answer causal questions where no experiment was run. They write each question as an estimand, draw a causal graph and derive what must be adjusted for, then estimate effects with matching and weighting, difference-in-differences with staggered adoption, synthetic control, regression discontinuity and instrumental variables. Each method is practised on a public or synthetic dataset where the answer is known or has been debated in the literature. Every analysis ends with a sensitivity analysis and a plain statement of the assumptions a reader must accept. The capstone is a full observational analysis defended before a panel.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Draft a causal graph (directed acyclic graph, DAG) for a stated question and derive a valid adjustment set, identifying colliders and bad controls.
- Apply propensity-score matching and inverse probability weighting to estimate an average treatment effect, checking overlap and covariate balance.
- Apply difference-in-differences to estimate a programme effect, including an event-study plot and an estimator suited to staggered adoption.
- Implement synthetic control, regression discontinuity and instrumental-variable estimates, each with its standard diagnostic.
- Defend the choice of an identification strategy for a new causal question against at least two alternatives.
- Evaluate how sensitive an estimate is to unmeasured confounding and state how strong a confounder would have to be to change the conclusion.
- Deliver an end-to-end observational analysis from question to defended conclusion.

## Prerequisites

- [SPC-STA-301 · Regression and Generalised Linear Modelling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-STA-301.md)
- Designs and reads a randomised experiment at the depth of SPC-EXP-201
- Writes analysis notebooks in Python or R

## Next courses

- [SPC-EXP-401 · Causal Machine Learning and Policy Evaluation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-EXP-401.md)

## Topics

### Questions, estimands and potential outcomes

- Average, on-the-treated and local effects
- Target populations
- Why prediction is not causation
- Pre-analysis plans for observational work

### Causal graphs and identification

- Directed acyclic graphs and the back-door criterion
- Colliders, mediators and bad controls
- The front-door idea
- What a graph cannot tell you

### Matching and weighting

- Propensity scores
- Matching and inverse probability weighting
- Estimators that combine outcome and propensity models
- Overlap, trimming and balance diagnostics

### Panel designs

- Difference-in-differences and parallel trends
- Event studies
- Staggered adoption and effects that change over time
- Interrupted time series and its limits
- Synthetic control and placebo tests

### Discontinuities and instruments

- Sharp and fuzzy regression discontinuity
- Bandwidth choice and manipulation tests
- Instrument relevance and exclusion
- Weak instruments and the local average treatment effect

### Sensitivity and partial identification

- Sensitivity to unmeasured confounding
- Bounds and partial identification
- Falsification and placebo outcomes

### Reporting causal claims

- Assumptions in plain words
- Checking assistant-written analysis code
- Limitations sections that a decision maker can use

---

# SPC-EXP-303 · Measuring the Impact of AI Deployments

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Experimentation and Causal Inference](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-EXP.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Workshop: two days with labs, guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants design and analyse the measurement of an AI deployment such as a coding assistant for developers, a drafting assistant for case workers or an agent in a service centre. They choose between randomised, stepped-wedge and encouragement designs, measure outcomes that matter (quality, completed work, rework, time to resolution) instead of throughput or self-report, and correct for selection in who adopts first. On synthetic data modelled on published trials they compare perceived and measured gains, then turn an estimate and its uncertainty into a return case with costs. The product is a measurement plan an organisation can run.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain why self-reported speed-ups, usage counts and output throughput mislead as measures of AI impact.
- Prepare an outcome set for an AI deployment that separates speed, quality and value, including rework and the cost of errors.
- Analyse a staggered rollout of an AI assistant across teams, correcting for selection into early adoption.
- Design a trial for an AI deployment, choosing among randomised, stepped-wedge and encouragement designs and setting unit, duration, power and contamination controls.
- Build a return case from an impact estimate that carries its uncertainty through costs, benefits and the break-even point.
- Evaluate an impact report from a vendor or internal team and decide whether it supports scaling.

## Prerequisites

- [SPC-EXP-201 · Designing and Reading Experiments](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-EXP-201.md)
- Fits a linear regression with group fixed effects
- Reads a difference-in-differences estimate and its parallel-trends check, from SPC-EXP-302 or from the tracked pre-work on staggered rollouts
- Can describe one AI assistant or agent workflow from a work setting, including what it produces and who checks it

## Topics

### Why AI impact is hard to measure

- Perceived versus measured productivity
- Throughput, activity and self-report as proxies
- Uneven effects across tasks and people
- Novelty and observation effects in short pilots
- Learning curves and skill loss over time

### Outcomes that matter

- Speed, quality, rework and error cost
- Blind expert review of sampled work outputs
- Cost per completed task
- Effects on staff and on service users

### Trial designs for rollouts

- Individual and cluster randomisation
- Stepped-wedge and phased rollouts
- Encouragement designs when use cannot be forced
- Contamination and spillover between teams

### When the rollout already happened

- Selection into adoption
- Staggered difference-in-differences
- Matched comparison teams
- Rollout order or licence allocation as an instrument

### From estimate to return case

- Costs of usage, licences, review and change
- Distributions instead of point estimates
- Value versus speed
- Stop, continue or scale

### Reporting and governance

- Measurement plans as a gate before scaling
- Communicating uncertainty to sponsors
- Ethics of measuring workers

---

# SPC-EXP-401 · Causal Machine Learning and Policy Evaluation

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Experimentation and Causal Inference](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-EXP.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 36 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants use machine learning to estimate who benefits from a treatment and to choose and evaluate targeting policies. They estimate average effects with double machine learning and cross-fitting, estimate conditional average treatment effects with meta-learners and causal forests, and validate them on held-out randomised data. They build uplift models for targeting, evaluate new decision policies offline from logged data, and learn a policy under budget and fairness constraints. Each policy ends with the confirmatory experiment that would test it. The capstone is a policy evaluation defended before a panel.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Implement double machine learning with cross-fitting for an average effect with many confounders, and compare it with plain regression adjustment.
- Build conditional average treatment effect (CATE) estimators with at least three methods and validate them on held-out randomised data.
- Evaluate a proposed targeting policy offline from logged decisions with inverse propensity and model-assisted estimators, and diagnose when the estimate cannot be trusted.
- Design a treatment-assignment policy under a budget and a fairness constraint, and compare it with treat-all and risk-based targeting.
- Diagnose a heterogeneous-effect claim that rests on overfitting, unstable subgroups or reuse of the same data for estimation and evaluation.
- Design a confirmatory experiment for a learned policy, with power for the comparison against the current policy.

## Prerequisites

- [SPC-EXP-302 · Causal Inference from Observational Data](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-EXP-302.md)
- [SPC-MOD-201 · Machine Learning for Tabular Data: Baselines and Validation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-MOD-201.md)
- Fits, tunes and cross-validates gradient-boosted tree models
- Derives an adjustment set from a causal graph

## Topics

### From average to heterogeneous effects

- Conditional and individual effects
- Why risk models are not benefit models
- Identification under randomisation and under unconfoundedness

### Double machine learning

- Orthogonal scores and cross-fitting
- Choosing and tuning nuisance models
- Inference for average and partial effects
- Partially linear and interactive models

### Heterogeneous-effect estimators

- S-, T- and X-learners
- R-learner and DR-learner
- Causal forests and honest splitting
- Bayesian tree ensembles

### Validating effect estimates

- No ground truth for individual effects
- Calibration by predicted-effect group
- Uplift and Qini curves
- Rank-weighted average treatment effect

### Uplift modelling for targeting

- Response versus uplift
- Persuadable, sure-thing, lost-cause and do-not-disturb segments
- Cost-aware targeting thresholds

### Off-policy evaluation

- Logged bandit feedback and propensities
- Inverse propensity scoring and self-normalised estimators
- Direct and combined estimators
- Overlap, effective sample size and variance
- Logging propensities so future policies can be evaluated

### Policy learning and hand-over

- Policy trees and welfare maximisation
- Budget and fairness constraints
- Confirmatory experiments and monitoring
- Hand-over of the assignment rule to engineering

---

# SPC-EXP-402 · Statistical Evaluation of AI Systems

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Experimentation and Causal Inference](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-EXP.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants treat every model evaluation as an experiment with a sampling design. Using item-level results they generate from small open-weight models on public benchmarks and a synthetic in-house task set, or from provided item-level logs, they compute standard errors that respect clustered items and repeated samples, compare models with paired designs, size an evaluation for a minimum effect of interest, use exact and Bayesian intervals when items are few, and correct pass rates for the measured error of a model grader. They audit published comparisons and write a statistical reporting standard for evaluation claims. Benchmark design, contamination and grader validation are taught in SPC-TRU-301 and DEV-EVL-301.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compute standard errors for an evaluation score that account for clustered items, repeated sampling and several runs per item.
- Decide whether the difference between two models on a shared item set is real and large enough to matter, using a paired analysis.
- Design the size of an evaluation in items, samples per item and grader calls to detect a stated difference within a budget.
- Decide which interval method to use for small evaluations, showing by simulation where the large-sample interval fails.
- Evaluate how model-grader error biases an observed pass rate and correct it using measured sensitivity and specificity, carrying the calibration uncertainty into the final interval.
- Audit a published or internal evaluation claim for statistical validity and write a reporting standard for future claims.

## Prerequisites

- [SPC-STA-201 · Statistical Inference by Simulation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-STA-201.md)
- [SPC-STA-301 · Regression and Generalised Linear Modelling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-STA-301.md)
- Runs a language model evaluation with a harness and exports item-level scores, at the depth of DEV-EVL-301
- Writes simulation code in Python or R

## Topics

### Evaluations as experiments

- Items as a sample from a population of tasks
- Sources of variance: items, sampling, graders, harness
- Published recommendations for reporting evaluation uncertainty

### Standard errors and clustering

- Large-sample intervals and their assumptions
- Clustered items and design effects
- Repeated samples per item and variance decomposition
- Estimators of success at k attempts and their variance

### Paired designs and comparisons

- Paired differences and correlated item results
- Comparing many models and multiple comparisons
- Leaderboard ranks with uncertainty

### Power and sizing

- Minimum effect of interest
- Power for paired and clustered designs
- Trading items against samples per item and grader calls

### Small samples and extreme rates

- Wilson, exact and Bayesian intervals
- Beta-binomial models for item difficulty
- Item response models and reduced item sets
- Coverage checks by simulation

### Grader error

- Graders as noisy measurement
- Correction with sensitivity and specificity
- Propagating calibration uncertainty
- Combining a small human-labelled set with many model-graded items (prediction-powered inference)

### Reporting and standards

- Evaluation reports with uncertainty
- Slices by language and subgroup, including Arabic and English
- An organisational standard for evaluation claims

---

# SPC-MOD-201 · Machine Learning for Tabular Data: Baselines and Validation

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Machine Learning and Modelling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-MOD.md)
- Level: Level 200 · Apply
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 36 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants answer a prediction question on tabular data the way an independent reviewer will check it. They climb a baseline ladder, tune gradient-boosted trees under a fixed budget, test an automated or pretrained challenger on the same folds, choose validation that mirrors use, audit for leakage, break errors down by subgroup and write a model card. Data are public or synthetic, with repeated entities and dates that defeat naive splits. Production pipelines are DEV-MLE-201.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Identify the leakage type and the fitting validation scheme in short modelling cases.
- Apply a baseline ladder from a constant predictor to tuned gradient-boosted trees, logging every run.
- Implement validation that matches the data structure and measure how far a random split overstates performance.
- Test an automated or pretrained challenger against the tuned champion under identical folds and budget.
- Analyse held-out errors by subgroup with intervals that reflect slice size.
- Audit another analyst's modelling notebook and decide whether its reported score can be trusted.

## Prerequisites

- [FND-AIC-101 · How Machine Learning Works](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-AIC-101.md)
- [FND-DAT-102 · Data Wrangling with DataFrames](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-DAT-102.md)
- Computes and reads a bootstrap interval

## Next courses

- [SPC-EXP-401 · Causal Machine Learning and Policy Evaluation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-EXP-401.md)
- [SPC-MOD-301 · Uncertainty, Interpretability and Model Validation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-MOD-301.md)
- [SPC-MOD-302 · Forecasting and Time Series](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-MOD-302.md)
- [SPC-MOD-303 · Text and Unstructured Data for Data Science](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-MOD-303.md)
- [SPC-MOD-304 · Optimisation and Operations Research for Decisions](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-MOD-304.md)
- [SPC-MOD-305 · Clustering, Anomaly Detection and Dimensionality Reduction](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-MOD-305.md)
- [SPC-MOD-306 · Responsible Data Science: Privacy, Fairness and Documentation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-MOD-306.md)
- [SPC-MOD-308 · Graph, Network and Relational Data Analysis](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-MOD-308.md)
- [SPC-MOD-401 · Foundation Models for Structured Data](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-MOD-401.md)
- [SPC-RSP-302 · Data Science Practicum](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-RSP-302.md)

## Topics

### Framing and baselines

- Target, unit and moment of prediction
- Metrics tied to the cost of errors
- Class imbalance and decision thresholds
- Constant, rule and regularised linear baselines

### Boosted trees and challengers

- Key settings, early stopping and tuning budgets
- Automated search and post-hoc ensembling
- Pretrained tabular models: row limits and licences

### Validation and leakage

- Stratified, grouped and time-ordered splits
- Nested tuning and an untouched test set
- Imputation, scaling and target encoding fitted inside folds
- Leakage types and feature availability at prediction time

### Error analysis and documentation

- Slicing by subgroup and operating condition
- Small slices and honest intervals
- Model cards and verification notes for AI-assisted code

# SPC-MOD-301 · Uncertainty, Interpretability and Model Validation

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Machine Learning and Modelling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-MOD.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants produce the evidence an independent validator needs about a trained model: whether its probabilities can be trusted, how wide its errors are, what drives its predictions and where it stops working. They measure and repair calibration, wrap models in conformal intervals and prediction sets, test coverage by subgroup and under shift, apply explanation methods and show where they mislead, and write a validation report against a published checklist. Labs use synthetic readmission and credit data.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Explain what calibration, conformal coverage and feature attribution each guarantee, and their assumptions.
- Measure calibration with proper scores and reliability diagrams, then recalibrate and report the effect by subgroup.
- Implement conformal intervals and prediction sets and test coverage overall, by group and under simulated shift.
- Compute permutation, accumulated-local-effect and Shapley-value explanations and test their stability across refits.
- Diagnose why a model degrades on a later batch from slice metrics, coverage loss and explanation changes.
- Audit a model package against a reporting checklist and deliver a fit-for-use decision.

## Prerequisites

- [SPC-MOD-201 · Machine Learning for Tabular Data: Baselines and Validation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-MOD-201.md)
- Reads hypothesis tests and bootstrap intervals at the depth of SPC-STA-201

## Topics

### Probabilities you can act on

- Proper scoring rules
- Reliability diagrams and binned calibration error
- Platt, isotonic and temperature scaling

### Conformal prediction

- Exchangeability and what coverage means
- Split, cross and quantile-based methods
- Group-conditional coverage and shift
- Abstention and referral to a person when sets are large

### Explanation and its limits

- Interpretable models as the first option
- Importance, effect plots, Shapley values and counterfactuals
- Correlated features and unstable attributions
- Explaining the model, not the world

### Validation practice

- Independent challenge
- Leakage and reproducibility checklists
- Stress and shift testing
- Validation report structure

---

# SPC-MOD-302 · Forecasting and Time Series

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Machine Learning and Modelling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-MOD.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 36 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants forecast with the discipline of a backtest. On public energy, retail and tourism series they decompose series, set a benchmark floor with naive and seasonal-naive methods, fit exponential smoothing and ARIMA-family models with calendar effects, including holidays that move against the Gregorian year, train global boosted forecasters and run pretrained zero-shot forecasters as baselines. Forecasts are scored by rolling-origin cross-validation with point and probabilistic measures and reconciled across hierarchies. The production system is DEV-MLE-306.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish forecasting settings by horizon, number of series, information available and demand pattern.
- Compute seasonal-trend decompositions and a benchmark floor scored by rolling-origin cross-validation.
- Apply exponential smoothing, ARIMA-family and dynamic regression models with moving-holiday features and check residuals.
- Test global boosted and pretrained zero-shot forecasters against statistical models on point and quantile accuracy.
- Review a forecast evaluation for leakage across time and for model selection on the test window.
- Build a forecasting analysis for new series and defend the method, horizon and uncertainty to a planner.

## Prerequisites

- [SPC-MOD-201 · Machine Learning for Tabular Data: Baselines and Validation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-MOD-201.md)
- Fits and reads a linear regression
- Handles dates and resampling in a dataframe library

## Next courses

- [DEV-MLE-306 · Forecasting Systems in Production](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/DEV-MLE-306.md)
- [SPC-MOD-401 · Foundation Models for Structured Data](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-MOD-401.md)

## Topics

### Framing and exploring series

- Forecast unit, horizon and information set
- Seasonal-trend decomposition
- Outliers, structural breaks and missing periods
- Lunar and solar calendars and moving holidays

### Benchmarks and evaluation

- Naive, seasonal-naive and drift forecasts
- Rolling-origin cross-validation
- Scaled errors, pinball loss and coverage

### Statistical forecasters

- Exponential smoothing
- ARIMA and seasonal ARIMA
- Dynamic regression and intermittent demand

### Learned and pretrained forecasters

- Lag features with boosted trees
- Global models across many series
- Zero-shot baselines, licences and pretraining overlap

### Hierarchies and uncertainty

- Bottom-up and optimal reconciliation
- Quantile forecasts and fan charts for planners

---

# SPC-MOD-303 · Text and Unstructured Data for Data Science

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Machine Learning and Modelling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-MOD.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 30 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants turn text into measurements they can defend. On public Arabic and English consultation responses, reviews and tender notices they build sparse-feature baselines, use embeddings as features, classify and extract fields with prompted language models, and find topic structure by clustering embeddings. Every model output is treated as a measurement, with agreement against a human gold set, stability across runs and prompts, dialect gaps and versions reported. Retrieval systems are DEV-LLM-203; production document extraction is DEV-LLM-204.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compare sparse features, embeddings and prompted language models on data needs, cost, transparency and failures.
- Prepare a codebook and gold set and measure agreement between annotators with chance-corrected statistics.
- Measure sparse, embedding-based and prompted classifiers against the same held-out gold set.
- Implement schema-constrained field extraction and measure field-level precision and recall.
- Evaluate a language model as an annotator and decide whether its labels can feed a downstream analysis.
- Design a text-measurement project that answers a stakeholder question and defend each measurement choice.

## Prerequisites

- [SPC-MOD-201 · Machine Learning for Tabular Data: Baselines and Validation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-MOD-201.md)
- [FND-AIC-102 · How Language Models Work](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-AIC-102.md)
- Calls a language model from Python and parses structured output

## Topics

### Text as data

- Units of analysis and sampling
- Arabic normalisation, dialects and code-switching
- Personal data in free text

### Representations

- Sparse term weighting
- Multilingual sentence embeddings
- Embeddings as tabular features

### Language models as instruments

- Zero-shot and few-shot classification
- Extraction schemas and structured output
- Local open-weight versus hosted models

### Measurement reliability

- Cohen's kappa and Krippendorff's alpha
- Model labels against people
- Correcting estimates for label error with a gold subsample
- Drift after model or prompt changes

### Structure discovery

- Clustering embeddings into topics
- Human validation of topic labels

# SPC-MOD-304 · Optimisation and Operations Research for Decisions

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Machine Learning and Modelling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-MOD.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 36 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants turn decisions about resources, schedules and routes into mathematical models, solve them with open solvers and check that answers make operational sense. They formulate linear and mixed-integer programmes for allocation and staffing, solve rostering and vehicle routing with constraint programming, test plans under uncertain demand by Monte Carlo simulation, and judge forecasts by the decision cost they cause. Cases use synthetic demand on open map data. Discrete-event simulation is SPC-MOD-402.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish linear, integer, constraint and scenario-based formulations and identify which a problem needs.
- Implement a linear programme for allocation and interpret shadow prices for a manager.
- Implement a staff roster with hard and soft rules and measure solve time and optimality gap as it grows.
- Analyse a plan under uncertain demand by Monte Carlo simulation against a scenario-based alternative.
- Build a predict-then-optimise pipeline and evaluate forecasts by the decision regret they cause.
- Design a decision model from a stakeholder brief, verify it against the owner's rules and defend its trade-offs.

## Prerequisites

- [FND-MTH-101 · Linear Algebra for Machine Learning](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/FND-MTH-101.md)
- [SPC-MOD-201 · Machine Learning for Tabular Data: Baselines and Validation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-MOD-201.md)
- Simulates random variables in Python

## Topics

### Formulation

- Variables, objectives and constraints
- Linear programming, duality and sensitivity
- Multiple objectives and trade-off curves
- Algebraic modelling languages

### Integer and combinatorial models

- Binary variables and logical constraints
- Assignment and location structures
- Branch and bound and optimality gaps
- Diagnosing infeasible and unbounded models

### Scheduling and routing

- Rostering with constraint programming
- Vehicle routing with time windows
- Local search when exact methods stall

### Uncertainty and prediction

- Monte Carlo evaluation of plans
- Two-stage and scenario formulations
- Decision regret versus forecast error
- Language models drafting formulations, verified by tests

---

# SPC-MOD-305 · Clustering, Anomaly Detection and Dimensionality Reduction

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Machine Learning and Modelling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-MOD.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Workshop: two days with labs, guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants find structure in unlabelled data and show whether it is real. They reduce dimensions with principal components and nonlinear embeddings and see how projections mislead, segment with several clustering families, and validate clusters by internal indices, resampling stability and review with domain owners. They detect anomalies in synthetic transaction and sensor data and set alert thresholds against an investigation budget. Production drift monitoring is DEV-OPS-301.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Apply principal components and a nonlinear embedding and test which structures survive changes of settings and seeds.
- Apply centroid, mixture and density-based clustering under different scaling choices and measure internal indices and bootstrap stability.
- Measure the precision of anomaly detectors at a fixed investigation budget.
- Evaluate a segmentation delivered by another team and decide whether it is stable and useful enough to act on.
- Design an anomaly-monitoring rule for a data feed with thresholds, alert budget and a review step.

## Prerequisites

- [SPC-MOD-201 · Machine Learning for Tabular Data: Baselines and Validation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-MOD-201.md)
- Uses vectors, distances and matrix notation

## Topics

### Reducing dimensions

- Principal components and loadings
- Nonlinear embeddings and their distortions

### Clustering

- Distance and scaling choices, including mixed data types
- Centroid, mixture and density-based methods

### Validation without labels

- Internal indices
- Stability under resampling
- Usefulness checks with domain owners

### Anomalies and monitoring

- Median-based and seasonal baselines
- Isolation forests and local outlier factors
- Alert budgets and precision at k

# SPC-MOD-306 · Responsible Data Science: Privacy, Fairness and Documentation

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Machine Learning and Modelling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-MOD.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 3 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 24 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants take one synthetic public-service dataset with personal attributes through the checks a responsible analysis needs before release. They measure re-identification risk and de-identify the data, answer aggregate queries under a differential privacy budget, audit a classifier's errors across subgroups, and write the datasheet, model card and reproducibility record that let a reviewer rerun and challenge the work. The method is general; national data protection rules are the worked reference. It extends the first model card of SPC-MOD-201; privacy attacks on trained models are SPC-TRU-304 and compliance casework is LDS-DMG-206.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Distinguish pseudonymisation, de-identification, aggregation and differential privacy by the guarantee each gives.
- Measure re-identification risk from quasi-identifiers and reduce it while tracking analytic utility.
- Compute differentially private counts and means and state the accuracy cost of a privacy budget.
- Audit a classifier for subgroup disparities, choose fairness criteria that fit the decision and evaluate mitigations.
- Build the documentation set that lets an independent reviewer rerun an analysis and judge its limits.

## Prerequisites

- [SPC-MOD-201 · Machine Learning for Tabular Data: Baselines and Validation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-MOD-201.md)
- Computes classification metrics and group-wise aggregates in Python or R

## Topics

### Personal data in analysis

- Identifiers, quasi-identifiers and sensitive attributes
- Minimisation, purpose limitation and classification
- Linkage and re-identification attacks

### De-identification and its limits

- k-anonymity and its successors
- Generalisation, suppression and aggregation
- Synthetic data with utility and disclosure checks
- When de-identified data are still personal data

### Differential privacy basics

- Privacy budget and composition
- Mechanisms for counts and means
- Evaluating a differential privacy claim against a published hazards list, such as the US National Institute of Standards and Technology guidelines (SP 800-226)

### Subgroup fairness audit

- Group metrics and why they conflict
- Intersectional slices and small-group uncertainty
- Auditing when protected attributes are missing or restricted
- Mitigation before, during and after training

### Documentation and reproducibility

- Datasheets and model cards
- Reproducibility checklists such as REFORMS
- Pinned environments and versioned data

---

# SPC-MOD-307 · Problem Framing, Product Sense and Analytical Review

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Machine Learning and Modelling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-MOD.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Workshop: two days with labs, guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants practise the work before and after an analysis. They turn vague requests into decision questions with an estimand, a metric and a decision rule, map who decides and who is affected, and test whether data and deadline make the question answerable. Then they review others' analyses, including assistant-generated ones, and write notes a colleague can act on. Delegating analysis to assistants is SPC-ANL-202; briefing decision makers is SPC-ANL-301.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare a decision question with estimand, population, metric and decision rule from a request.
- Analyse a metric set for proxy failure and gaming, and propose guardrail metrics.
- Design an analysis plan stating data, method, threats to validity and the result that would change the decision.
- Review an analysis for errors in question fit, data handling, method, inference and communication.
- Decide whether a request needs description, an experiment, a causal study, a model or no analysis.

## Prerequisites

- [SPC-ANL-201 · Exploratory Analysis and Visualisation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-ANL-201.md)
- Has completed an analysis that a colleague or client used
- Tells a randomised comparison from an observational one, as in SPC-EXP-201

## Topics

### From request to question

- Decision, estimand and population
- Descriptive, predictive and causal questions
- CRISP-DM and its limits

### Stakeholders and product sense

- Decision makers, users and affected groups
- The evidence each will accept
- Value, cost of delay and reversibility

### Metrics

- Metric trees and proxies
- Goodhart's law and guardrails
- Definitions others can recompute

### Planning and review

- Feasibility and scoping to a deadline
- A review checklist from question to conclusion
- Spot-checking assistant-generated analyses

# SPC-MOD-308 · Graph, Network and Relational Data Analysis

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Machine Learning and Modelling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-MOD.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Workshop: two days with labs, guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: practitioner
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants build networks from event data and analyse them with methods whose assumptions they can state. They choose nodes, edges, weights and time windows, compare centrality and clustering with null models, test whether detected communities are real, and predict links with a time-respecting split, ending with a small graph neural network set against simple heuristics. Data are public research networks and a synthetic supplier and payment ledger.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Construct a network from transaction records, justifying node, edge, weight and window choices.
- Compute centrality, clustering and assortativity against a degree-preserving null model.
- Evaluate community structure across two methods, under resampling and against external attributes.
- Build and compare heuristic, embedding and graph neural network link predictors.
- Explain how message passing generalises neighbourhood features and when engineered features suffice.

## Prerequisites

- [SPC-MOD-201 · Machine Learning for Tabular Data: Baselines and Validation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-MOD-201.md)
- Reads a matrix as an adjacency or similarity table
- Has trained a small neural network, or completes the pre-work notebook

## Topics

### From records to networks

- Nodes, edges, weights and direction
- Bipartite projections and their distortions
- Temporal networks and missing edges

### Measures and null models

- Centrality and what each measure assumes about flow
- Clustering and assortativity
- The configuration model

### Community structure

- Modularity and its resolution limit
- Leiden and stochastic block models
- Validation without ground truth

### Link prediction and relational learning

- Heuristics and node embeddings
- Temporal splits and leakage
- Message passing; knowledge graphs are in DEV-DAT-304

---

# SPC-MOD-401 · Foundation Models for Structured Data

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Machine Learning and Modelling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-MOD.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Workshop: two days with labs, guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants decide whether a pretrained model for tables, time series or relational data should replace or join a tuned baseline. They test tabular in-context learners against tuned boosted trees across sample sizes and zero-shot forecasters against statistical benchmarks, survey relational and graph pretraining, audit leaderboard claims and weigh licences, cost and data residency. Labs run on a free notebook GPU or a provided accelerator.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Evaluate a tabular foundation model against a tuned, ensembled boosted-tree baseline across training-set sizes.
- Evaluate zero-shot and fine-tuned forecasters against seasonal naive, exponential smoothing and a tuned global boosted-tree model.
- Audit a published claim for pretraining overlap, unequal tuning budgets and leaderboard overfitting.
- Design a reusable evaluation protocol and decide on adoption for one structured-data task, including licence, hosting and data-flow conditions.

## Prerequisites

- [SPC-MOD-201 · Machine Learning for Tabular Data: Baselines and Validation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-MOD-201.md)
- [SPC-MOD-302 · Forecasting and Time Series](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-MOD-302.md)
- Tunes boosted trees under a fixed budget and runs rolling-origin backtests

## Topics

### How the models work

- In-context learning on tables
- Pretrained forecasters and covariates
- Relational deep learning and graph foundation models

### When they win

- Small-data and many-series regimes
- Tuned, ensembled baselines
- Cost and latency per prediction

### Evaluation caveats

- Pretraining and test overlap
- Leaderboard overfitting
- Uncertainty in rankings

### Adoption conditions

- Non-commercial and research-only weights
- Hosted against local inference
- Version pinning and hand-over

# SPC-MOD-402 · Simulation and Agent-Based Modelling

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Machine Learning and Modelling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-MOD.md)
- Level: Level 400 · Evaluate
- Format: Workshop: two days with labs, guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 16 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants build a discrete-event model of a service centre and an agent-based model of how people adopt a new public service, validate both, calibrate unknown parameters against observed patterns, and compare policies through scenario experiments with replications and sensitivity analysis. Starter models are provided, so lab time goes to experiments and validation.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Build a discrete-event model of a queueing service and compare staffing policies with replications and common random numbers.
- Build an agent-based model of adoption and document it with a standard protocol.
- Calibrate model parameters against observed aggregate patterns and report their uncertainty.
- Analyse which inputs drive outputs with designed experiments and global sensitivity analysis.
- Evaluate scenarios for a policy decision and defend what the model can and cannot support.

## Prerequisites

- [SPC-STA-201 · Statistical Inference by Simulation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-STA-201.md)
- Writes Python classes and fits probability distributions to data

## Topics

### Choosing an approach

- Discrete-event, agent-based and system dynamics models
- When plain Monte Carlo is enough
- Optimisation is in SPC-MOD-304; physical twins in DEV-PHY-301

### Building the models

- Entities, resources, queues and input modelling
- Warm-up, run length and replications
- Agents, rules, networks and emergence
- Language-model agents as simulated people and their limits

### Calibration and validation

- Verification against analytic cases
- Pattern-oriented and predictive validation
- Approximate Bayesian computation and history matching

### Scenario analysis

- Experimental designs over parameters
- Global sensitivity analysis

# SPC-DLR-301 · Mathematics for Model Builders

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Deep Learning and Model Development](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-DLR.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Extended: 9 weeks part-time, one lecture and one lab a week, weekly problem sets, two supervised tests and a capstone notebook
- Total hours: 45 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants rebuild the mathematics of deep learning, deriving each idea on paper and checking it in code. They compress trained weight matrices with the singular value decomposition, derive and verify gradients of softmax, normalisation and attention, write a small scalar reverse-mode automatic differentiation engine (extended to tensors in SPC-DLR-302), predict from curvature when gradient descent diverges, and measure language-model losses in bits. A placement test routes each participant to bridging units for the gaps it finds, so the cohort starts level.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Apply eigen and singular value decompositions to explain and compress the weight matrices of a trained network.
- Compute gradients and Jacobians of vector and matrix expressions in matrix notation.
- Build a scalar reverse-mode automatic differentiation engine and use it to train a two-layer network.
- Analyse how step size, momentum and adaptive scaling interact with curvature and conditioning.
- Compute entropy, cross-entropy, divergence and bits per byte, and derive training losses from maximum likelihood.
- Diagnose and fix numerical failures such as overflow, cancellation and precision loss in low-precision formats.

## Prerequisites

- Writes Python functions and NumPy array code, at the depth of FND-PRG-101
- First-year university calculus, linear algebra and probability (FND-MTH-101 to FND-MTH-103 or equivalent); a placement test routes each gap to a bridging unit

## Next courses

- [SPC-DLR-302 · Deep Learning from First Principles](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-DLR-302.md)

## Topics

### Linear algebra for networks

- Linear maps, norms and tensor shapes
- Eigen and singular value decompositions
- Low rank and conditioning

### Calculus and automatic differentiation

- Jacobians and vector-Jacobian products
- Forward and reverse mode
- Gradient checking

### Probability and estimation

- Expectation and estimator variance
- Maximum likelihood and the losses it produces
- Monte Carlo estimates

### Optimisation

- Convexity, curvature and the Hessian
- Momentum and adaptive methods
- Stochastic gradient noise

### Information theory

- Entropy, cross-entropy and divergence
- Perplexity and bits per byte
- Prediction as compression

### Numerics

- Floating-point formats and rounding
- Stable softmax and log-sum-exp
- Variance propagation and initialisation

---

# SPC-DLR-302 · Deep Learning from First Principles

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Deep Learning and Model Development](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-DLR.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Extended: 12 weeks part-time, two sessions a week (concepts, then a supervised lab), weekly build modules, two supervised tests and a reproduction capstone
- Total hours: 80 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants build deep learning from the bottom up, then test what they believe about it. They extend their scalar engine from SPC-DLR-301 into a small NumPy tensor library with broadcasting, layers and optimisers, and train a convolutional network with it. They then use a standard framework to train convolutional, recurrent and transformer models on public data, transfer hyperparameters across widths, probe a self-supervised encoder and run controlled ablations over several seeds. Production training pipelines are DEV-MLE-202.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Build a tensor library with automatic differentiation, layers, losses and optimisers on the SPC-DLR-301 engine.
- Implement and train multilayer, convolutional, recurrent and transformer models in a standard framework.
- Apply schedules, normalisation, initialisation and width-aware hyperparameter transfer when tuning a model.
- Diagnose why a training run fails or underperforms and fix the cause.
- Measure the quality of learned representations with linear probes and nearest-neighbour retrieval.
- Design and run a controlled ablation that tests a claim about architecture, optimisation or generalisation.

## Prerequisites

- [SPC-DLR-301 · Mathematics for Model Builders](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-DLR-301.md)
- Writes object-oriented Python and NumPy code
- Has trained a classical model and reported held-out metrics, at the depth of FND-AIC-101

## Next courses

- [SPC-DLR-303 · Building a Language Model from Scratch](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-DLR-303.md)
- [SPC-DLR-402 · Efficient Deep Learning: Compression, Quantisation and Long Context](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-DLR-402.md)
- [SPC-GEN-301 · Diffusion and Flow Matching from Scratch](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-GEN-301.md)
- [SPC-GEN-302 · Vision and Multimodal Foundation Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-GEN-302.md)
- [SPC-GEN-303 · Speech and Arabic Language Modelling](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-GEN-303.md)
- [SPC-GEN-304 · Reinforcement Learning and Decision Making](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-GEN-304.md)
- [SPC-TRU-302 · Interpretability of Neural Networks](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-TRU-302.md)
- [SPC-TRU-304 · Trustworthy Machine Learning: Robustness, Privacy and Fairness](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-TRU-304.md)

## Topics

### Automatic differentiation and frameworks

- Reverse mode on tensors
- Broadcasting and its gradients
- Saved activations and memory

### Optimisation and scaling rules

- Momentum, AdamW, warm-up and decay
- Initialisation and normalisation
- Hyperparameter transfer across width
- Newer optimisers as claims to test

### Architectures and inductive bias

- Residual and convolutional networks
- Recurrent and state-space models in one session
- Attention and the transformer block

### Generalisation

- Regularisation and augmentation
- Overparameterisation and double descent
- Distribution shift and calibration

### Representation learning

- Contrastive and masked self-supervision
- Linear probes and embedding geometry
- Transfer to new tasks

### Experimental practice

- Debugging on a CPU before spending accelerator hours
- Seeds, variance and intervals
- Experiment tracking

# SPC-DLR-303 · Building a Language Model from Scratch

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Deep Learning and Model Development](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-DLR.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Extended: 12 weeks part-time, one lecture and one long lab a week, five graded assignments, a supervised test and an end-to-end training capstone
- Total hours: 80 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants write every part of a small decoder-only language model themselves, without model libraries: a byte-level byte-pair encoding (BPE) tokeniser trained on Arabic and English text, the transformer, the optimiser and training loop, and decoding with a key-value (KV) cache. After debugging on a CPU they train a model end to end on public text within a fixed accelerator budget, evaluate it and publish it with a model card. Training systems are SPC-DLR-304, data pipelines SPC-DLR-305 and post-training SPC-DLR-306.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Build a byte-level BPE tokeniser and compare its compression across languages.
- Build a decoder-only transformer and its training loop from tensor operations.
- Compute parameters, operations and memory for a configuration, and choose a model size and token count within budget.
- Implement sampling strategies and a KV cache for generation.
- Diagnose instability in language model training from logged loss, gradient norms and activation statistics.
- Evaluate a trained small language model on held-out loss, benchmarks and samples, and document its limits.

## Prerequisites

- [SPC-DLR-302 · Deep Learning from First Principles](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-DLR-302.md)
- Writes and debugs PyTorch or JAX training code
- Uses the command line, version control and a remote machine, at the depth of FND-PRG-102

## Next courses

- [SPC-DLR-304 · Training Systems for Large Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-DLR-304.md)
- [SPC-DLR-305 · Data and Scaling for Foundation Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-DLR-305.md)
- [SPC-DLR-306 · Post-Training I: Fine-Tuning, Preference Optimisation and Distillation](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-DLR-306.md)
- [SPC-DLR-402 · Efficient Deep Learning: Compression, Quantisation and Long Context](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-DLR-402.md)

## Topics

### Tokenisation

- Unicode and Arabic script normalisation
- Training and applying BPE
- Vocabulary size and unequal token costs across languages

### The transformer

- Causal multi-head and grouped-query attention
- Rotary positions
- Pre-normalisation and gated feed-forward layers

### Training

- Next-token cross-entropy
- AdamW, warm-up and cosine schedules
- Clipping, accumulation, mixed precision and checkpoints
- Resource accounting before a run

### Decoding

- Temperature, top-k and nucleus sampling
- The KV cache
- Batched generation

### Evaluation

- Perplexity and bits per byte
- Benchmarks scored by likelihood
- Contamination checks
- Reading samples critically

---

# SPC-DLR-304 · Training Systems for Large Models

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Deep Learning and Model Development](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-DLR.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Extended: 10 weeks part-time, one lecture and one long lab a week on a provided multi-GPU node, four graded assignments, a supervised test and a performance capstone
- Total hours: 60 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants make a language model train faster and larger on the hardware they have. They account for floating-point operations (FLOPs), memory and communication before running anything, profile a training step, write a fused attention kernel and test it against a reference, fit a larger model into memory with mixed precision and activation checkpointing, and build sharded data parallelism from collective primitives, tracking model FLOPs utilisation (MFU) throughout. Labs debug on CPU processes, then run on a provided multi-GPU node. Fleet operation at scale is DEV-INF-402.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Compute the arithmetic, memory and communication cost of a training configuration and predict its step time with a roofline model.
- Analyse a profiler trace of a training step, attributing time to kernels, transfers, data loading and communication.
- Build a fused attention kernel with tiling and an online softmax.
- Build data-parallel training with sharded optimiser state from collective communication primitives.
- Optimise end-to-end training throughput under a fixed memory limit without changing results beyond a stated tolerance.
- Analyse tensor, pipeline, sequence and expert parallelism plans for a model too large for one node.

## Prerequisites

- [SPC-DLR-303 · Building a Language Model from Scratch](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-DLR-303.md)
- Explains processes, memory hierarchy and caches, at the depth of FND-PRG-105
- Reads simple C or array-kernel code

## Topics

### Resource accounting

- FLOPs and memory per training step
- Arithmetic intensity and the roofline model
- Model FLOPs utilisation

### Profiling and benchmarking

- Timers, synchronisation and warm-up
- Profiler traces
- Variance and honest benchmarks

### Kernels

- GPU execution model and memory hierarchy
- Tiling and fusion
- Compilers against hand-written kernels

### Precision and memory

- Low-precision formats including 8-bit floating point
- Loss scaling
- Activation checkpointing, accumulation and offloading

### Distributed training

- Collective operations and their cost
- Data parallelism and sharded state
- Tensor, pipeline, sequence and expert parallelism
- Checkpointing and restart

---

# SPC-DLR-305 · Data and Scaling for Foundation Models

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Deep Learning and Model Development](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-DLR.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task
- Total hours: 40 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants turn raw web crawl archives into pretraining data and decide how to spend a compute budget on it. They extract text, identify languages including Arabic varieties, filter for quality, remove personal data and near-duplicates, record licences and provenance, and set a mixture that may include filtered synthetic data. Each filtering decision is tested by training small models on the data it produces. Finally they fit scaling laws from small runs to choose a model size and token count for a stated budget.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare a text pipeline from raw web archives covering extraction, language identification, quality filters and personal-data removal.
- Implement near-duplicate detection with MinHash and decontaminate the corpus against evaluation sets.
- Evaluate a filter, synthetic dataset or mixture by training small models on its output at equal compute.
- Build a scaling-law fit from small runs and use it to decide model size and token count for a budget.
- Draft a data card recording sources, licences, opt-out handling, filters and known gaps.

## Prerequisites

- [SPC-DLR-303 · Building a Language Model from Scratch](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-DLR-303.md)
- Processes multi-gigabyte files with a dataframe or SQL engine
- Fits and reads a regression on log-log axes

## Topics

### Sources and rights

- Web crawls, books, code and open government data
- Licences and opt-out signals
- Personal data in web text

### Cleaning and filtering

- Text extraction and language identification for Arabic varieties
- Rule-based and classifier quality filters
- What filters remove from dialect and minority text

### Deduplication and decontamination

- Exact and near-duplicate detection
- MinHash and locality-sensitive hashing
- Removing benchmark overlap

### Mixtures and synthetic data

- Domain weights and multilingual balance
- Generating and filtering synthetic data
- Degradation from training on model output

### Scaling laws and budgets

- Compute-optimal allocation
- Checking extrapolation
- Data-constrained regimes and repetition

---

# SPC-DLR-306 · Post-Training I: Fine-Tuning, Preference Optimisation and Distillation

- Track: Data Science
- Path: [Deep Learning and Model Development](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/paths/SPC-DLR.md)
- Level: Level 300 · Develop
- Format: Extended: 10 weeks part-time, one lecture and one long lab a week, four graded assignments, a supervised test and a post-training capstone
- Total hours: 60 h
- Audience: specialist
- Status: In development

## Description

Participants take a small open-weight base model through instruction tuning, preference optimisation and distillation, writing each loss themselves before using a library. They build datasets with correct chat templates and loss masks, compare full fine-tuning with low-rank adapters (LoRA), train a reward model and a direct preference optimisation (DPO) run, distil a larger open model into a smaller one, merge checkpoints, and measure what each step adds and costs, including forgetting and safety regressions. Reinforcement learning is SPC-DLR-401; application-level adaptation is DEV-LLM-301.

## Learning outcomes

By the end, the participant can:

- Prepare instruction and preference datasets with chat templates, loss masking, decontamination and licence checks.
- Build supervised fine-tuning runs with full-parameter and low-rank adapter variants and decide between them.
- Build a reward model and a DPO run from their loss functions.
- Apply sequence-level and logit-level distillation from a larger teacher to a smaller student.
- Apply weight-merging methods to combine checkpoints tuned for different skills.
- Evaluate an adapted model for improvements, forgetting, instruction following and safety regressions.

## Prerequisites

- [SPC-DLR-303 · Building a Language Model from Scratch](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-DLR-303.md)
- Has fine-tuned a pretrained network and read its loss curves
- Runs a model evaluation with a harness; DEV-EVL-301 or SPC-TRU-301 is recommended

## Next courses

- [SPC-DLR-401 · Post-Training II: Reinforcement Learning for Language Models](https://sdaiaacademy.github.io/en/courses/SPC-DLR-401.md)

## Topics

### Supervised fine-tuning

- Base and instruction models; chat templates
- Loss masking and sequence packing
- Full fine-tuning, LoRA and quantised adapters
- Catastrophic forgetting

### Preference optimisation

- Pairwise reward models
- Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) in outline
- Direct preference methods and variants
- Over-optimisation against a reward

### Distillation

- Logit, sequence-level and on-policy distillation
- Distilling reasoning traces
- Licence terms on teacher outputs

### Merging

- Linear and spherical interpolation
- Task arithmetic, TIES and DARE
- When merging helps

### Evaluating adapted models

- Held-out capability suites
- Validated model graders
- Refusal and safety regressions
- Contamination and language slices
